speaker: Jacob
en: Well, Charlie, I suppose the Ghost Club holds some new horror for me today?

speaker: Evie
en: How nice to see you again, Mister Dickens. Is it time for another of the Ghost Club's stories?

speaker: Dickens
en: As a matter of fact, yes! Follow me! Number fifty Berkeley Square: four storeys high, and branded: "BEWARE ALL THOSE WHO ENTER". There have been many strange tales of this dreadful domicile. The earliest report of a haunting was said to be the specter of a small girl who was murdered by a servant. She could be seen at the attic windows, weeping and wringing her little hands in an agony of despair. Come along! The house awaits! You're not afraid are you?

speaker: Dickens
en: Another legend claims the attic is haunted by the spirit of a young woman, who purportedly threw herself from the top floor windows to escape her abusive uncle. Her screaming ghost has reportedly been sighted hanging from the window ledge. This residence was briefly owned by a Mr. James Jasper. A choirmaster and an opium addict. His nephew, Edward, was betrothed to one of Mr. Jasper's pupils, the fair and delicate Rose. However, Edward disappeared under mysterious circumstances, followed by Jasper himself. Perhaps grief sent him back to the soothing arms of his narcotic mistress.

speaker: Dickens
en: Shall we? Though this house is vacant, some say it comes alive at night with screams of terror, ringing bells, and slamming shutters.

speaker: Dickens
en: Although eerie, this phenomenon is easily produced by pneumatic tubes and valves! There are claims that a young man was caged in the attic, his only connection to the rest of the world a tiny hole in the door - a young man who was reduced to madness by this extreme isolation. The legends all seem to focus on one room in particular.

speaker: Dickens
en: A sudden draft, nothing more!

speaker: Dickens
en: My word. Perhaps... perhaps I shall wait while you investigate the source of that laughter, which is not at all unsettling!

speaker: Child
en: Let me go, you moke!

speaker: Jacob
en: Why were you hanging around that house?

en: Charming. Now tell me, why were you at that house?

speaker: Evie
en: Out with it!

en: Secret passage?

en: What secret passage?

en: I've found a lock but I haven't located the key.

en: It's here.

en: Ah! So this is how it works!

en: Impressive.

en: Good lord!

speaker: Dickens
en: Alas, the myth has been discredited. There was no ghost in Berkeley Square. Just a wretched soul, driven to murder and madness by guilt and intoxication. I think this has the making of a rather fine novel. I wonder if I have one left in me...

en: I don't see Mister Abberline.

en: What

en: I was expecting you to be a policeman.

en: I was expecting you to be discreet.

en: Henry Green said that you could help us go unnoticed.

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, we'll be as quiet as an old lady. A very hairy, strange old lady, that looks like a policeman.

speaker: Abberline
en: Now whatever you do, try to remain within the bounds of the law. For my sake. I don't need any corpses at the station... Approach the target from behind and attempt to make them talk. Then bring them to my carriage, carefully.

en: Get off me! Piss off! Oi!

en: Shut your gob. Meet my blade.

en: Get off me! Piss off! Oi!

speaker: Darwin
en: Ah, my young friend! How good it is to see you! Fortunate, really... It would appear a highly toxic plant, which has the extraordinary effect of making people quite delirious, has been found in this very park. Yet as far as modern science is aware, no such plant exists. I fear the good people of London might be in danger. Will you investigate?

speaker: Evie
en: Mmm... Not your average flower... Mr. Darwin was right about these plants... Oh... I don't feel well...

speaker: Jacob
en: There you go.

speaker: Evie
en: That's one less to worry about.

speaker: Jacob
en: Hello, footprints! Might lead me to the culprit!

speaker: Evie
en: These footprints must belong to a rogue gardener.

speaker: Driver
en: I didn't do nothin'! What do you want with me? Leave me alone!

speaker: Jacob
en: Mr. Darwin will know what to do with this.

speaker: Evie
en: Dr. Darwin will want to inspect these flowers...

speaker: Darwin
en: Well done! But you... You don't seem quite like yourself, if I may say so. Mmm... it's just as I suspected! Those noxious fumes are not being released from the flowers, but from the pots! There must be something in there... A hallucinogenic concoction of some kind, not unlike the Soothing Syrup, I should think. We must dispose of it. And quickly! I believe, my young friend, that I might know just the place. Who would want to poison the population of London? Who could devise such a nefarious plan? Obviously, it can't be Dr. Elliotson... So who CAN it be?

speaker: Jacob
en: The same people I've been fighting since I arrived in London. The same group Elliotson worked for.

speaker: Evie
en: An organization my brother and I have been fighting all our lives. Dr. Elliotson was one of them.

speaker: Darwin
en: I don't need to know more if you do not care to tell me. However, may I be so bold as to suggest you continue to fight them?

speaker: Jacob
en: That's exactly what I aim to do, Mr. Darwin.

speaker: Evie
en: Of course, Mr. Darwin. You can count on us.

speaker: Darwin
en: I'm afraid, my young friend, that some of your enemies want their toxin returned to them. Might I suggest you position our carriage directly in front of theirs? I believe the fumes will impair their ability to drive.

speaker: Darwin
en: Well done! Well done indeed! Now we must hurry and destroy our cargo... We're almost there!

speaker: Darwin
en: What an escapade! That's pepped me up to no end! The people of London are fortunate to have you by their side, my young friend. Very fortunate indeed! Well, I better run now. You will take good care of yourself, won't you?

Frank is consumed by grief - he blames the government for refusing to protect the rights of the worker. I can't blame him for his rage, but I fear his actions have gone too far. He plans to steal a shipment of and use it to attack the Houses of Parliament. Killing people and destroying property solves nothing. Democracy is the only road to socialism. Please, stop him before he gets himself or anyone else killed. I expect he's on his way into the City of London now.

speaker: Bella

speaker: Bella

en: I should return to Charlie and Charlie to tell them the happy news.

en: And so all's well that ends well! Our young lovers are united at last and will soon marry.

speaker: Jacob

speaker: Abberline
en: The bank is designed to protect England's gold reserves—a fortress guarded under lock and key. There is the bank manager, Mr. Osborne. Only he is allowed free access to the vault. You can spot him near the entrance. And, oh yes, one man keeps a close watch on the vault door, he watches it like a hawk. If he sees you, he's sure to seal it. The guard captain, Gus Howard, knows Twopenny well. He is in on this, I'm certain. Mr. Frye, please, use discretion. The only way to implicate Twopenny is to catch him in the act. Do not jeopardize him, no big displays. This is the Bank of England. If you encounter any trouble, I'll be in the atrium—in disguise.

speaker: Jacob
en: Twopenny won't be leaving that vault.

speaker: Abberline
en: Mr. Howard has worked as Mr. Twopenny's guard captain for years. He can tell you where to find him. The only one who can command the guards in front of the door, is the bank manager. I should warn you, a man watches over the vault and will close it at the first sign of trouble.

speaker: Jacob
en: Understood. Got it. Thank you.

speaker: Jacob
en: Ooh, fancy. Fitting for Twopenny's tomb.

speaker: Employee
en: Last chance for the tour! See the inner workings of this thrilling marvel of commerce! The official bank tour is leaving soon! Last chance to join our group and learn of the great wonders of the banking world!

speaker: Employee
en: Has everyone assembled? Yes? Yes. Excellent. I shall begin the tour. We start in the pay hall, the bank's center of activity. This way please! The Bank of England was founded in 1694 and has been situated in Threadneedle Street since 1734. We are approaching the celebrated rotunda. Originally built in 1765, it was secured against fire and from collapse by Sir in 1794.

speaker: Visitor
en: Marvelous.

speaker: Osborne
en: I'll be with you shortly, sir. Ah, so good to see you again, sir. My apologies for keeping you waiting.

speaker: Customer
en: Thank goodness you're here. My bank's Irish interests are being damaged by those damned s!

speaker: Osborne
en: Now, now, I'll take you in and you'll see everything is perfectly secure.

en: The accounting appears impeccable, my dear sir. I shall update our ledgers accordingly. Do you require assistance in any other matter?

speaker: Customer
en: No thank you.

speaker: Osborne

en: For the path of the dead.

speaker: Starrick
en: No more dallying. The halls of Parliament must be free to govern, again! Understood? You may see yourself out.

en: Better suited than I? Pff. Who's better suited than Miss Beatrice Gribble? Who? I've good blood in my veins, royal ancestry in Spain and no one bats an eyelash. en: I'll ensure Dr. Schwartz's safety and makes sure you get that fossil.

speaker: Darwin
en: Splendid! But please do be careful... Do hurry to Charing Cross, please. Please hurry. I fear Dr. Schwartz might be in danger. You'll find Dr. Schwartz at Charing Cross Station.

speaker: Schwartz
en: What is the meaning of this?

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm collecting you and your precious cargo for our friend, Mr. Darwin. Just act naturally.

speaker: Evie
en: Mr. Darwin has sent me to ensure you reach him safely, with your cargo intact. Just act naturally.

speaker: Schwartz
en: Right... So how is your father? By which I mean my dear brother Franck, with whom I grew up, of course. Oh, splendid! Wonderful to hear. I'll do my best not to call attention to how remiss he was in forgetting to warn me about the delicate situation which brings me here today.

speaker: Blighter 1
en: Wouldn't hurt to know what the bugger looks like.

speaker: Blighter 2
en: How am I going to find him among all these people?

speaker: Blighter 3
en: Like finding a needle in a haystack, this is.

speaker: Blighter 4
en: What's a German doctor supposed to look like anyway?

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: Doctor Schwartz?

speaker: Schwartz
en: ... never got on the train. Darwin's fate is sealed! Goodbye, Assassin. I did so enjoy meeting you.

speaker: Imposter
en: Darwin must be silenced! will destroy the very fabric of our society! Do you not see how dangerous Darwin's theories are?! We cannot allow Darwin to destroy what we have built!

speaker: Jacob
en: Where do you think you're going?! Stop, and I might let you live. I'll run you off the road! Your choice, imposter: we do this the hard way, or we do it the very hard way!

speaker: Evie
en: Stop and hand over the specimen. Now! Don't force me to kill you! Don't make me do anything you'll regret! You can't escape! You must realize that!

speaker: Jacob
en: Now to take this fossil to Darwin.

speaker: Evie
en: I should deliver this to Mr. Darwin.

speaker: Darwin
en: At last! My heart hasn't stopped pounding. You have it? Wonderful? But... where is Dr. Schwartz?

speaker: Jacob
en: Most likely dead, I'm afraid. He never left Germany. At least I managed to get the fossil back.

speaker: Evie
en: I'm afraid he was intercepted, sir, in Germany. However, I have recovered the fossil.

speaker: Darwin
en: Dear Lord... I should tell you I was recently approached by men who sought to purchase all my research, on the condition I work only for them. Obviously, I refused. Scientific knowledge cannot be bought, it belongs to everyone. Let these villains do their worst!

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Bloody Nora asked us to keep a close eye on activity here in the City of London. Says there's a rebel group rising up in Whitechapel.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: The Blighters are more than just a bunch of rebels. We are a well-thought through organization, a family. These Rooks will never understand that concept.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: We need to show the other boroughs what it means to be a true Blighter. We must take out those Rooks and make them sorry they ever crossed us.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: We bow our heads for our fallen brothers and sisters but this fight is far from over, we will crush those Rooks under our feet and march our way back to city wide domination.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Miss Graves will show them the meaning of brutality. This borough belongs to us. To the Blighters!

speaker: Jacob
en: So much for the house call. I'll have to find a way into that carriage.

speaker: Benjamin
en: What's the meaning of this? Who the devil are you?

speaker: Jacob
en: Prime Minister, I'm your new bodyguard. Jacob Frye

speaker: Benjamin
en: I wasn't informed of any new bodyguard. Who is your commanding officer?

speaker: Mary Anne
en: Let the boy speak, Dizzy.

speaker: Jacob
en: Madam. Apologies, but we've learned of a threat on your life, and the Met thought it best to move quickly.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Threat? What sort of threat?

speaker: Jacob
en: That sort. And if you'll excuse me a moment.

speaker: Benjamin
en: See here, what's all this

speaker: Thug
en: Not so fast, Your Excellency.

speaker: Jacob
en: Oi! Get back here with that... Prime Minister!

speaker: Jacob
en: Everyone all right?

speaker: Mary Anne
en: We seem to have come through unscathed. You have our thanks, Mr. Frye.thumb|250px|right|Disraeli rages

speaker: Benjamin
en: It was Gladstone, I bet my life on it. This is perfectly in keeping with his lack of character. Show yourself, Gladstone! Show yourself, you feckless muck-snipe!

speaker: Mary Anne
en: Well, he's hardly going to be in the van with a cudgel, Dizzy.

speaker: Disraeli
en: Damn Gladstone! That bloody man! He will pay for this!

speaker: Mary Anne
en: Thank you. What do you intend to do about Gladstone, young man?thumb|250px|right|Jacob helping Mrs. Disraeli out of the carriage

speaker: Jacob
en: I assure you, madam, Gladstone is innocent in this.

speaker: Mary Anne
en: But he tried to kill my husband.

speaker: Jacob
en: Well, we'll look into Gladstone. Perhaps you can help me in another inquiry, madam. A gentleman with ties to parliament. Older, wears cavalry uniforms and has a large moustache?

speaker: Mary Anne
en: You seem like a rough and ready sort of fellow, Mr. Frye.

speaker: Jacob
en: Well... yes, I am, actually.

speaker: Mary Anne
en: And are you familiar with the poorer districts of our city?

speaker: Jacob
en: Roughly.

speaker: Mary Anne
en: Wonderful! As it happens, I've been eager to tour the Devil's Acre. If you were to escort me, I'd be happy to assist you in your inquiry.

speaker: Jacob
en: That strikes me as a dangerous idea.

speaker: Mary Anne
en: Then it's settled. Come back here to Downing Street tomorrow night, eight o'clock sharp. Good day, Mr. Frye.

speaker: Jacob
en: But, I

speaker: Mary Anne
en: Good day, Mr. Frye.

speaker: Bell
en: Argh! Oh, Jacob, Evie, it's you. Thank goodness.

speaker: Evie
en: Experimenting, are we, Aleck?

speaker: Bell
en: Correct.

speaker: Jacob
en: And looking a bit frazzled.

speaker: Bell
en: Nerves. It's those great oafs Starrick keeps sending 'round to coax me. He is offering a ridiculous amount of money.

speaker: Jacob
en: Aleck, you're not thinking of jumping ship, are you?

speaker: Bell
en: Never! I've been working on something in case they get too insistent. It's meant to stun an assailant, should the need arise.

speaker: Evie
en: Are you certain that it works?

speaker: Bell
en: Not as such. I've made three of them with varying degrees of acidity and whatnot. One must be the right formula.

speaker: Jacob
en: Let's find some Starrick lackeys to target then, shall we?

speaker: Bell
en: Speaking of Starrick, he is still transmitting false information.

speaker: Evie
en: We could simply destroy his transmitters...

speaker: Bell
en: His company's too well guarded. The bombs will help, but it would be awkward to produce bombs that potentially do not stun...

speaker: Bell
en: Oh- Wait a minute, looks like opportunity has come knocking. Oh, dear. They never looked so angry before.

speaker: Jacob
en: Stand clear, Aleck.

speaker: Bell
en: Let us instead play a little linguistic game with them. Um, take the bombs and climb onto the roof. When I say the name of a-a fruit, toss one near the thugs.

speaker: Evie
en: Right, then.

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, uh, wait! Uh, I nearly forgot...

speaker: Bell
en: Slip these into your boots and you will henceforth be immune to all voltaic discharge! I think.

speaker: Bell
en: Good day, gentlemen. Uh, I would ask you in for tea, but I'm afraid I'm running rather late...

speaker: Bill
en: Enough of the niceties. We've come to smash your place up, in't we, Baz?

speaker: Baz
en: You've got one of them tele-whatsit in there, ain't ya? And you've been reading messages from the Starrick Company?

speaker: Bell
en: That is as untrue as the notion that the Starrick Telegraph Company is emitting impartial information, sir.

speaker: Baz
en: Come again?

speaker: Bell
en: Your employer's promises are nothing but hot air. And his operations are about to turn... Pear-shaped!

speaker: Bill
en: Whatcha going on about air and pears for?

speaker: Baz
en: Aw, I don't alf feel rough...

speaker: Bill
en: That's disgusting... Uh!

speaker: Bill
en: Gawd blimey...

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, kids, eh! Those playful young scamps get everywhere...

speaker: Bill
en: Listen up, Bell, or I'll thump you till your ears are ringing.

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, a pun. Your wordplay delights me! And to think I worried you had the mental capacity of a dollop of donkey's apples.

speaker: Baz
en: Apples?

speaker: Bill
en: I think he's trying to be funny.

speaker: Baz
en: Pwah! You dropped another one, Bill, you little sod...

speaker: Bill
en: Ain't me, Baz. Gor blimey, it's got me froat...

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, those rascals throwing stink bombs again. It happens all the time around here.

speaker: Baz
en: Right, tell us where you keep that tele-whatsit. I'll count to three.

speaker: Bell
en: Three? Well, well, let's see how far you get!

speaker: Baz
en: One...

speaker: Bell
en: Do you really think I would keep it here? Do you see a cable? A telegraph without a cable is about as useful as a bell without a clapper.

speaker: Baz
en: I'll give you a bleedin' clapper!

speaker: Bell
en: Well, bless my boots, you're as purple as... a plum!

speaker: Baz
en: A plum?

speaker: Jacob
en: Bravo, Aleck!

speaker: Bell
en: Thanks to you, Jacob. Your mere presence gave me courage and resolve I never knew I had. I found myself rather witty, too.

speaker: Jacob
en: Well... make some more bombs and let's sort out Starrick's propaganda machine, shall we?

speaker: Evie
en: Good show, Aleck!

speaker: Bell
en: Thanks to you, Evie. Your mere presence gave me courage and resolve I never knew I had.

speaker: Evie
en: I'm glad I could help. Now it's time to shut down Starrick's Empire of Propaganda.

speaker: Bell
en: Come on, we haven't got all day!

speaker: Bell
en: The longer we can keep Starrick from spewing out false information, the more we can awaken the people with the truth about his operations.

speaker: Jacob
en: Let's get to it, then.

speaker: Bell
en: Would you believe, my mother says there are still some wives in her street that swear by that Soothing Syrup. So I took it upon myself to tell her neighbors the truth about the obnoxious draught.

speaker: Jacob
en: Good on you, Aleck, but you can't go knocking on everyone's door.

speaker: Bell
en: No... I wasn't always welcome... which shows how false information can be as difficult to stamp out as fishwives' profanities at .

speaker: Jacob
en: Or rats in the sewers.

speaker: Bell
en: But if we can eradicate the source that continually feeds such detrimental trash, then little by little, the truth will take the upper hand and the sham will be flushed out.

speaker: Jacob
en: Let's crack on, then. Here we are!

speaker: Bell
en: We will have to get in without being detected, mind.

speaker: Jacob
en: While I stun them, you sneak inside.

speaker: Bell
en: I shall destroy not one, but three parts of the transmitter. He'll be as good as dancing before a public toilet without a penny!

speaker: Bell
en: The longer we can keep Starrick from spewing out false information, the more we can awaken the people with the truth about his operations.

speaker: Evie
en: I agree. The sooner we can get there, the quicker we can act.

speaker: Bell
en: Would you believe, my mother says there are still some wives in her street that swear by that Soothing Syrup. So I took it upon myself to tell her neighbors the truth about the obnoxious draught.

speaker: Evie
en: That's good, Aleck, but you can't go 'round to every household in London town.

speaker: Bell
en: No... I wasn't always welcome... which shows how false information can be as difficult to stamp out as fishwives' profanities at Billingsgate.

speaker: Evie
en: Or vermin at .

speaker: Bell
en: But if we can eradicate the source that continually feeds such detrimental trash, then little by little, the truth will take the upper hand and the sham will be flushed out.

speaker: Evie
en: That's why we're here.

speaker: Bell
en: We will have to get in without being detected, mind.

speaker: Evie
en: I shall stun them while you get inside.

speaker: Bell
en: I shall destroy not one, but three parts of the transmitter. He'll be as good as dancing before a public toilet without a penny!

speaker: Bell
en: What a beautiful machine. A pity, it's been soiled by corrupt minds! Oh, well. I hope the guards don't come patrolling.

speaker: Bell
en: I say, this is becoming rather perilous to say the least! Golly gosh, I felt that! Jolly close shave, that!

speaker: Bell
en: Ha! Got you, you little bugger! We'll have to cross over here.

speaker: Bell
en: A tad fiddly, that one, but I've pulled it as well as a dentist pulls a rotten tooth! There.

speaker: Jacob
en: Move on to the next part, Aleck.

speaker: Evie
en: Move faster, if you can.

speaker: Bell
en: My dears, Jacob, Evie, thanks are once again in order, for supporting what is most dear to me and to our cause. Freedom of speech.

speaker: Evie
en: It's a blessing that you employ your genius for the common good, Aleck.

speaker: Jacob
en: However, I suggest you vacate your workshop.

speaker: Bell
en: No need, not now, you've given me sacksful of courage. And, besides, what with my little devices, I have all the protection I need. Uh, should you find yourselves with a moment to spare, do drop by!

speaker: Bell
en: Ah, Jacob, Miss Frye! How good to see you. Oh, have you seen Starrick's latest lies?

speaker: Jacob
en: Lies in a newspaper?

speaker: Evie
en: What transpired from the new line you were establishing?

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, the cables we ordered never arrived. And then, we intercepted this. A message mentioning cargo seized at College Wharf.

speaker: Evie
en: Then let's unseize it.

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, uh, wait! Another intercepted wire contained the recipe for a powerful hallucinogenic serum. I've adapted this dart mechanism to work with your bracers.

speaker: Jacob
en: Aleck, you're a genius.

speaker: Bell
en: Well that, patently, is untrue. Although... I've also discovered that the serum adopts the form of a gas when subjected to heat.

speaker: Jacob
en: Just when I think you can't surpass yourself...

speaker: Blighter
en: There's trouble on the docks, lads! We need to get this load to Starrick now!

speaker: Jacob
en: Poison! Bell must know what kind.

speaker: Evie
en: Poison! I'm sure Mr. Bell will find this most interesting.

speaker: Evie
en: Careful there, Mr. Bell.

speaker: Bell
en: Every worthwhile endeavor is fraught with dangers, my dear friends. None more so than yours. But you have triumphed once again.

speaker: Jacob
en: How do you know?

speaker: Bell
en: We have entered the age of communication, remember. We've already received word from Greenwich that the shipment has arrived safely. Thanks to you.

speaker: Evie
en: Have you discovered what else is in that shipment?

speaker: Bell
en: Indeed. Um, I'm afraid that Starrick's poison has found its way on to the open market.

speaker: Evie
en: If he believes that will stop us, he is mistaken.

speaker: Hargrave
en: No exceptions, you hear? No documentation, no entrance to the port.

speaker: Dock Worker 1
en: Aye, aye captain!

speaker: Hargrave
en: This is an important job we have, can't just have any old riff raff coming into our ports. You don't see papers, you throw them overboard, and I don't want anyone swimming to shore.

speaker: Dock Worker 1
en: Yes, Sir.

speaker: Dock Worker 2
en: You think it's a bit harsh?

speaker: Dock Worker 3
en: Making 'em disappear? I suppose.

speaker: Dock Worker 2
en: There has to be a more civilized way of dealing with... outsiders.

speaker: Dock Worker 3
en: I don't think it's wise to question Captain Hargrave.

speaker: Dock Worker 2
en: He seems a bit different than usual, the Captain does.

speaker: Dock Worker 3
en: How so? I haven't noticed anything.

speaker: Dock Worker 2
en: Doesn't he seem younger to you at all? I don't think he's actually Captain Hargrave we've always worked for.

speaker: Dock Worker 3
en: You've gone loony, mate. Should I send for bedlam?

speaker: Jacob
en: What have we here?

speaker: Letter
en: Boiler, this Dredge character's meddling will be the death of us. He was loitering around the exchange today asking far too many questions about the bank. Should he discover my plan, you will face a far worse fate than losing your job. Signed, Plutus.

speaker: Jacob
en: So this Plutus is Starrick's banker, hmm? I wager Dredge will lead me to him.

speaker: Evie
en: While you're out and about, do attempt not to destroy modern medicine or the London transportation network.

speaker: Jacob
en: Don't make me laugh.

speaker: Evie
en: Innocent lives hang in the balance. They depend on this city.

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm not the one who let Lucy Thorne walk away.

speaker: Evie
en: A mistake I intend to rectify immediately.

speaker: Paperboy
en: Bus feud ends in blood!

speaker: Jacob
en: I'll take one.

speaker: Paperboy
en: Here you go, sir?

speaker: Twopenny
en: I say we stop this goodwill toward strangers nonsense and focus on what London really needs, solid leadership whose hard work will raise everyone up to success. As go the titans of business, so goes the world.

speaker: Beggar
en: Oi, oi!

speaker: Twopenny
en: You weak fool, get a job!

speaker: Jacob
en: The best guards money can buy. Won't do Mr. Dredge any good.

speaker: Dredge
en: Pardon me. Do you do business at the bank? Anyone here visited the vault next door? Speak up if any here have heard of a man named Plutus mentioned in the bank next door. I have a couple of innocent questions. Who here has recently visited the Bank of England?

speaker: Dredge
en: What on Earth?!

speaker: Jacob
en: Keep your eyes ahead of you and walk.

speaker: Dredge
en: Come now, you are barking up the wrong tree, sir. Stupid pillock, I'll have you arrested, I'll

speaker: Jacob
en: The less you fight, the sooner you'll be released. Eyes front.

speaker: Dredge
en: Now wait a minute- I know that voice! Frye, is that you? Frye!

speaker: Dredge
en: Jacob, it's me! Sergeant Frederick Abberline!

speaker: Jacob
en: Freddy.

speaker: Abberline
en: Sergeant. Under cover. There's to be a robbery at the Bank of England, I'm sure of it.

speaker: Jacob
en: Robbery? It's a fortress.

speaker: Abberline
en: The boys at the station thought I was joking. Wouldn't be so funny if it was their life savings.

speaker: Jacob
en: Who's behind it?

speaker: Abberline
en: That's confidential.

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, come on, Freddy. I can help you. Imagine the headlines: "Thieves Caught in the Act! Abberline Right All Along."

speaker: Abberline
en: Well, I suppose I can fill you in a little. Every fiscal quarter, a branch of the bank is robbed, never the same branch. The thieves are supplied by... Cockham Merchants.

speaker: Jacob
en: Thanks for the info, Freddy.

speaker: Abberline
en: It's Sergeant! And, I-I'm keeping my eye on you.

scene: The Case of the Conflicted Courtship
speaker: Arthur
en: A tragedy in the park!

scene: The Case of the Conflicted Courtship
speaker: Henry
en: Another chance to sort out a diabolical conundrum! One that I'll turn into a for Purlock Publishing!

speaker: Policeman 1
en: For the last time, move on, or else!

speaker: Marx
en: You cannot frighten me! I insist on being heard!

speaker: Policeman 1
en: Has a crime been committed, sir?

speaker: Marx
en: Indeed! A crime against humanity! I demand you live up to your responsibilities!

speaker: Policeman 1
en: You're a fine one to talk about responsibility. You look like a bloody tramp! Listen to me! I have been ordered to keep your rallies off the street.

speaker: Marx
en: No, you must listen to me! The people in this city are in dire need of your assistance!

speaker: Marx
en: Ah, you are Jacob Frye, are you not? And Miss Frye?

speaker: Evie
en: We are at a disadvantage, sir...?

speaker: Marx
en: Karl Marx. Much like you, I am an activist of sorts.

speaker: Jacob
en: You've got the look of a man who wants something.

speaker: Marx
en: Indeed, you've done more for London's citizens lately than any endeavor has accomplished in a decade. But those citizens were already well provided for. I challenge you both to help those who REALLY need your assistance. The working people.

speaker: Evie
en: An interesting challenge. We accept.

speaker: Jacob
en: Shouldn't we at least talk about these things fir... sod it, we accept.

speaker: Marx
en: I am organizing a discreet meeting with some like-minded friends to discuss trades unions. Alas, the police seem to have noticed my activities. They've stuck to me like flies on Scheiße (shit). In any case, I need you to help me get to the meeting without the interference of the police. You see, there's one of their damned spies now.

speaker: Marx
en: Tonight. Sundown. The usual place.

speaker: Man 1
en: I'll be there.

speaker: Marx
en: You know, I had similar problems with the police in Paris. Well, Paris and Brussels. And also perhaps Cologne. Our next worthy ally awaits in a nearby pub! Onwards! No doubt the police already have agents stationed within. I'll wait here until the coast is clear.

speaker: Marx
en: The usual location. One hour.

speaker: Man 2
en: Right you are, Mr. Marx, sir.

speaker: Marx
en: I believe our work here is complete. Come, let's slip away and get to the meeting. I do appreciate your assistance in this matter. Only when workers are able to assemble freely and in strength will we be able to achieve the reforms we most assuredly deserve. Might I trouble you to stay nearby until the meeting is over? I fear we may yet meet with some mischief.

speaker: Simon
en: I told you, Marx will be here! Heard it from the man's own lips! Now about my payment.

speaker: Policeman 2
en: You'll get your thirty pieces, chum, don't you worry.

speaker: Marx
en: It seems the movement is ever doomed to be betrayed from within. Will you fetch the gentleman back here? I would look him in the eye and ask why he went back on his brethren.

speaker: Simon
en: Are you mad? You're making a big mistake!

speaker: Marx
en: Simon. My friend. What possessed you to do this thing? Has the Party not taken care of you?

speaker: Simon
en: The guv'nor at the mill say any man what joins a Union, he'll be put out of work come sunup. How long will the Party feed my family for?

speaker: Marx
en: If we do not stand together, we are lost. My heart is broken, Simon. Please go.

speaker: Marx
en: I thank you, my friend. I hope you will continue to aid the struggle when the opportunity presents itself.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Victor Lynch sent a runner with some very good news! For our excellent performance in controlling this borough, we'll receive between us an extra allowance.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Those who recently escorted the shipment of explosives to Mr. Lynch's lodgings will receive a reward of 30 pounds for their effort. He thanks you for your services and encourages you not to spend your entire allotment at the Fox and Bottle. (Laughs)

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: The Rooks do not have the same resources as us. We're protected under the watchful eye of Victor Lynch, and we must fight our hardest to do our leader justice for his overwhelming kindness.

speaker: Dickens
en: My dear friend, The Ghost Club has an extraordinary case for you. Spiritualist Thaddeus the Amazing has predicted his own death at his next séance! Could you have a look?

speaker: Thaddeus
en: I have foretold my own death. But first! You are about to witness an extraordinary event. Ah! We have a visitor. Approach, please.

speaker: Voice
en: Goodness! The lights! What is this? Help! Not yet! Someone light the lamps!

speaker: Wilburn
en: Oh! He's actually dead!

speaker: Darwin
en: "We are not apes"... If the circumstances were not so grave, I'd compliment the artist on the wonderful caricature. They are fools if they believe they can stop progress by printing leaflets and killing newsboys! We must find out who is behind this propaganda before more innocents are harmed. I should very much like it if you could find and remove these awful things. Perhaps you can catch one of the billposters red-handed?

speaker: Civilians
en: This a waste of paper, if you ask me! Not apes? Of course we're not apes! Look at us! Of course we are not apes! I don't need anyone to tell me that! God created us in his image! And he does not look like a monkey! Apes!? This is outrageous, I tell you! Outrageous!

speaker: Civilian
en: This is vandalism! Someone should inform the police!

speaker: Jacob
en: Oi! What are you doing over there?

speaker: Evie
en: You! What do you think you're doing?

speaker: Billposter
en: Stop it! Please! I beg you!

speaker: Jacob
en: Who are you working for? And why are they so violent against Mr. Darwin's theories?

speaker: Billposter
en: Darwin refused to cooperate with us! We wanted to recruit him, but he rebuffed all our offers. We've tried to intimidate him, blackmail him, but he's a stubborn old git.

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm going to take your operation apart.

speaker: Darwin
en: My young friend! I'm sorry to be so blunt, but I need to ask a favor of you. A delivery awaits me at the docks, a very rare orchid, all the way from the island of Madagascar. But there is a problem... One of my "associates" wants the flower for himself. He sent ruffians to collect it, if you can believe that. I need you to collect it for me first.

speaker: Darwin
en: Ah! Thank you, my young friend, thank you! This little orchid may seem inconsequential, but it holds secrets which could potentially change our very understanding of the world. It would have been a shame to lose it! A shame indeed! Thank you!

speaker: Matthew
en: Hear, hear.

speaker: Matthew
en: You hold a candle to the Devil, David.

speaker: Jacob
en: Quiet now, don't want to disturb the prayers.

speaker: Jacob
en: Out of every church in the district.

speaker: Jacob
en: Save it for the sergeant, would you?

speaker: Evie
en: Shh. You're making too much noise.

speaker: Evie
en: Stealing organ pipes, what else?

speaker: Evie
en: I haven't put as much thought into it as you.

speaker: Jacob
en: Keep your trap shut.

speaker: Evie
en: You're not getting away that easily.

speaker: Abberline
en: Thank you for bringing him in.

speaker: Dickens
en: You seem tired, friend. Everything all right?

speaker: Jacob
en: No rest for the wicked, Charlie.

speaker: Evie
en: There's always too much work to do.

speaker: Dickens
en: Today's Ghost Club investigation involves a carriage! It's said to be covered with gold leaf, dazzling passersby when the sun shines! Naturally, it's rumored to be haunted. Now let's see if we can find it!

speaker: Jacob
en: I presume this was once used to carry the mail. That actually looks remarkably comfortable.

speaker: Evie
en: The Royal Mall coaches vanished when the post began to be transported by rail. Oh, I'd rather enjoy a sit down. But duty calls.

speaker: Jacob
en: What the devil?

speaker: Evie

en: I grieve with you. But would your wife want to see your hands stained with the blood of so many?

speaker: Morris
en: I am trying to build a better world. To ensure that no one suffers what my son did. Pray tell me, "friend", how much blood do you consider that to be worth?

speaker: Jacob
en: These ones get to live, at least until they drive me to this factory.

speaker: Evie
en: I'll keep those ones alive until they take me to our destination.

speaker: Templar 1
en: Well, they'll never get hold of it now.

speaker: Templar 2
en: Bleedin' anarchists! Couldn't organize a piss up in a brewery!

speaker: Templar 1
en: About bloody time. What the hell took you so long?

speaker: Templar 2
en: Yeah, I'd like to see anyone try an' break in 'ere.

speaker: Morris
en: I'm sorry, but my need is greater than you know! Justice will be done!

speaker: Morris
en: Wait! Don't shoot! This is nitro!

speaker: Jacob
en: Morris! Poor sod. All right, better smash these crates before anyone else gets any bright ideas!

speaker: Evie
en: Mr. Morris! Poor man. I hope he finds some kind of peace. Now to destroy the crates! No one is getting their hands on this hellfire!

speaker: Marx
en: You're back. Mr. Morris? I see. I was afraid it would come to this. He was a good man, but even the best of us can lose our way when blinded by grief. Still, I thank you for preventing a greater tragedy.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Word has come down about a couple of meddling twins. Miss Nora is interested in meetin'em. If you hear word of their location, please come forward. You'll be sufficiently rewarded.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: The Blighters remain in control of London. Miss Nora informs me that the next move will be to retake Whitechapel.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Yes, Whitechapel's Mister Kaylock has died at the hands of some renegade group called the Rooks, but they're no match for us.

speaker: Henry
en: Ah! This is one that's most promising

speaker: Arthur
en: An important detective is missing! Skullduggery is surely afoot!

speaker: Henry
en: Solve it, and I'll quick as you please!

speaker: Vendor
en: Masks, over here!

speaker: Employee
en: This way to the Alhambra!

speaker: Jacob
en: Roth...

speaker: Usher
en: Masked guests this way. Masks only. I repeat, ladies and gentlemen, this entrance is masks only. Please put on your mask and join this group. I will escort the next group into the theater shortly. At this entrance, please. The doors will open shortly. Please don your mask. May I ask the masked guest to line up over here, please.

speaker: Usher
en: Let us enter the theatre for tonight's performance! Everyone ready? Then let's proceed!

speaker: Roth
en: Mesdames et Messieurs, ladies and gentlemen, welcome to the Alhambra Music Hall! Tonight, we have, for one night only, a very special performance of Corvus the Trickster. While some of the effects may be visceral and highly disturbing, do not be alarmed, my good people. Fear not! This is the purest form of entertainment! Tonight's performance immortalizes and is for the benefit of a young fellow very near and dear to my heart. Any concerns or complaints may be addressed to him, ha ha ha! Jacob, dear boy, tonight is for you.

speaker: Mary
en: I'll be serving you this evening, gentlemen.

speaker: Blighter 1
en: You still here, love? Last time, I swear, you nearly poisoned us!

speaker: Blighter 2
en: Scene two, stand by!

speaker: Machinist
en: Let me out! I need to lower the grid for the show!

speaker: Roth
en: We have a volunteer! A big round of applause for this brave, brave man! Our volunteer is about to die for you, Jacob. You lucky people are about to witness this gentleman being fired upon at point-blank range. Our performer will hit several targets placed around his head! Exciting, is it not? Oh ho ho! Will our honored guest go unharmed? We British are a hardy bunch. Let's put that hardiness to the test! What a thrill! Do not fret, my friends, it's all part of the show! Please stay with us as we prepare for the next turn! We found a suitably flat-headed gentleman for this one! You laugh, ladies and gentlemen, but I assure you that is the case! I have no doubt that you can hazard a guess as to what this one concerns, my friends. Our courageous participant hasn't even flinched! Standing a few feet away, our performer expertly throws his knives at the apple, slicing it in two. Will he or won't he?! Well! We werent' quite expecting that! How thrilling it is when life surprises us! I am not finished just yet! Stay right where you are and the show will continue shortly. You prefer tragedy to comedy. I knew you had exquisite taste. For this trick, ladies and gentleman, we have found a most courageous volunteer! With our courageous volunteer in the box, the celebrated illusionist will proceed to saw him in half! Watch as our esteemed guest emerges unharmed! Our skilled illusionist, "Sabertooth Jane", is performing this famous trick. She is said to have studied at the feet of the mysterious Torrini himself! The saw Miss Jane is using this evening is imported from the ancient city of , celebrated for manufacturing the finest steel in the world. Behold the grace with which Jane wields her saw. A diamond in the rough, I dare say! Marvelous, marvelous, marvelous! To thank our guest for participating in the show, we've invited him backstage to partake of some refreshment before returning to the audience. Our next turn will begin shortly. Please stay seated as we prepare. You won't want to miss this!

speaker: Machinist
en: Help! Help me! They've locked me in here!

speaker: Machinist
en: That's a daisy. Ta muchly.

speaker: Mary
en: Your drink, sir.

speaker: Decoy
en: Mary, you're a sweet, sweet girl.

speaker: Mary
en: Happens to be me job, sir.

speaker: Decoy
en: Thank you kindly.

speaker: Jacob
en: Excuse me, love. Just looking for the lavatory.

speaker: Mary
en: It's over there.

speaker: Jacob
en: Thanks.

speaker: Jacob
en: Where is he? If he's not Roth... Roth! Show yourself!

speaker: Roth
en: Oh my! Are your principles drifting, dear? The flavor intensifies the second time, the hunt now a search for want rather than need. The search consumes you, creed forgotten, prey visualized, mouth watering. Leaves a strange taste in your mouth, doesn't it? Like eating pork when expecting venison. Are you trying to repent, my dear? It is not too late to join me in my grand finale!

speaker: Roth
en: Ha ha ha! I hope you have enjoyed your evening so far, ladies and gentlemen. I know I have. Now, before our final act, I would like to toast all of you brave people who joined us tonight to celebrate life... and death. Go on, toast them!

speaker: Roth
en: Ha ha ha! Your move, Jacob, my dear! Burn! Burn! BURN! Over here, Jacob! Don't hide from me, darling! Come out, come out, wherever you are! Join me for the finale! Jacob, my dear! Where aaaare yooouuu?

speaker: Roth
en: Darling, what a night! The stuff of legends!

speaker: Jacob
en: Why did you do it? All of it?

speaker: Roth
en: What? Snap a baby crow's neck between my thumb and forefinger? Slice to bits the ones you deem innocent? Keep the world in its divine manic state? For the same reason I do anything!

speaker: Roth
en: Why not?

speaker: Jacob
en: I'll never make it out alive. What a nightmare! Damn this place from Hell to Hackney!

speaker: Starrick
en: Order has bred disorder. The sea rises to flood the pubs and extinguish the street-lamps. Our city will die. Twopenny has failed, Lucy has failed. Brudenell, Elliotson... Pearl. All have gone into the night. It is up to me now.

speaker: Starrick
en: The Assassins have brought nature's fury into our houses. Men have become monsters, barrelling toward us, teeth out.

speaker: Starrick
en: Our civilization must survive this onslaught.

speaker: Starrick
en: To prevent a return to the Dark Ages, I will start anew. London must be reborn.

speaker: Henry
en: Oh good, you're here. His highness seems to have caught a mild case of madness this morning.

speaker: Duleep
en: You were right when you said that this was our chance.

speaker: Jacob
en: I was?

speaker: Duleep
en: I propose we make a commotion, lure out the Templar-controlled British Indies Company.

speaker: Jacob
en: And do what? Put yourself in the line of fire?

speaker: Duleep
en: I need to send Ellsworth a message. This won't be over until we can draw him out. This is something I must do. I will make a scene, and then you need to rough them up a little.

speaker: Jacob
en: Well that shouldn't be a problem.

speaker: Duleep
en: I heard you Templars are a bunch of pansies.

speaker: Jacob
en: Here we go.

speaker: Templar 1
en: Please, spare me!

speaker: Duleep
en: I need you to send a message to Ellsworth.

speaker: Templar 1
en: I'll do anything!

speaker: Duleep
en: Tell him to meet me at Lambeth Cemetery tonight. And tell him to come alone.

speaker: Duleep
en: Meet me tonight at Lambeth cemetery. He'll never come alone, even if I ask him to.

speaker: Templar 2
en: Thought you could get away, did you?

speaker: Evie
en: That caused quite a commotion...

speaker: Jacob
en: He's gone mad! Greenie was right!

speaker: Evie
en: He isn't mad, Jacob. He's trying to take action, to do the right thing... Oh never mind. I'll take it from here.

speaker: Jacob
en: Fine by me... I could use a good pint right about now.

speaker: Duleep
en: Oh. I was expecting Jacob but I'm glad it's you who have come.

speaker: Evie
en: He thinks you've gone mad.

speaker: Duleep
en: I probably have.

speaker: Evie
en: What's your plan?

speaker: Duleep
en: I've asked Brinley to meet me here alone. In turn, he of course has sent a small army to secure the area. I need you to get rid of them and meet me back here. It's essential that when Brinley does arrive, I have him to myself.

speaker: Duleep
en: That will certainly help quite a bit, thank you.

speaker: Evie
en: He's here.

speaker: Duleep
en: I must talk to him.

speaker: Evie
en: Don't be absurd. This is dangerous.

speaker: Duleep
en: Miss Frye, this is something I must do, and I must do it alone. Remain hidden. I cannot afford to have him see you.

speaker: Brinley
en: You can't escape me forever, your Highness. Come out and face me.

speaker: Duleep
en: I told you to meet me here alone.

speaker: Brinley
en: I am not as silly as I once was, Singh. I wouldn't dare come to this meeting place alone. Not with your recently acquired friends.

speaker: Duleep
en: I am alone, Ellsworth. It doesn't have to be like this.

speaker: Brinley
en: You can't just walk this Earth like a free man. You are nothing more than a trophy, a stag's head above the mantelpiece. You have caused enough commotion as it is. It's time to put an end to this.

speaker: Duleep
en: If you kill me now, you will be a wanted man. Imagine the uprising when they find out the only son of Ranjit Singh has been murdered.

speaker: Brinley
en: Ah Ah Ah Ah... You think they remember you? You are a lost soul, a monarch who has abandoned his people. You are nothing.

speaker: Duleep
en: We were such good friends

speaker: Brinley
en: Friends? You were no more than a play-thing. A prisoner in prince's clothing. You're lucky to be alive. I admit, I'm surprised they let you live.

speaker: Brinley
en: I knew you were lying, Singh!

speaker: Duleep
en: Ellsworth, listen

speaker: Brinley
en: I've had enough of this.

speaker: Brinley
en: I knew you were lying!

speaker: Duleep
en: No! You mustn't!

speaker: Duleep
en: Miss Frye!

speaker: Evie
en: He will kill you!

speaker: Brinley
en: This is what I was sent here for. Be done with it, girl! I shall never forfeit my own mission.

speaker: Duleep
en: I will not allow it!

speaker: Brinley
en: The Logins', the Company, they all wanted your silence! Whether you spare me or end me, you won't escape the fate they have planned for you.

speaker: Duleep
en: It seems you have learned nothing of India, of its people... But killing you? That is something I cannot do. It would make me no better than that cursed, oppressive company you work for.

speaker: Brinley
en: You will die as you were raised, Singh. You will never be more than a trophy of war.

speaker: Brinley
en: We will bury you in English soil.

speaker: Duleep
en: You have done me much good. I am heavily indebted to you both.

speaker: Evie
en: We are happy to help.

speaker: Duleep
en: I fear that I cannot continue handling things in this manner. The Assassin way is not my way, as helpful as you have been. This Empire, this land, my people... The problem is so much bigger than death. I know I must devote my life to this cause, to put India, my home, back onto the map, return it to its people. It's a long and gruelling journey, but it is something I must do. Even if it takes me to my own death.

speaker: Evie
en: We understand, your highness.

speaker: Jacob
en: But, if you do change your mind, you know where to find us.

speaker: Duleep
en: That I do. Thank you, Assassins. Hopefully we never shall meet again.

speaker: Attaway
en: Those fiends!

speaker: Jacob
en: Ms. Attaway...

speaker: Attaway
en: Yes, may I- Oh, splendid, you're here to murder me.

speaker: Jacob
en: I- what?

speaker: Attaway
en: No matter. Everyone has a price. Is this enough?

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm not here to kill you.

speaker: Attaway
en: Then what's your game?

speaker: Jacob
en: Mr. Starrick and the Millner Company have blocked your ambitions long enough. I have a business proposition for you.

speaker: Attaway
en: Wonderful! Come with me, we have much to discuss, Mr...

speaker: Jacob
en: Jacob Frye, at your service.

speaker: Attaway
en: Truer words were never spoken! If you'd be so kind as to take the reins?

speaker: Attaway
en: You must understand, I've received threats against my life. Malcolm Millner has all but waged war on me since Mr. Starrick bought out his company. And, no offence, I hope, but you do look the killing type.

speaker: Jacob
en: I doubt I shall ever recover from such a slight.

speaker: Attaway
en: What, then, is your interest in my redemption, Mr. Frye?

speaker: Jacob
en: I sense an opportunity that will benefit us both.

speaker: Attaway
en: Do you?

speaker: Jacob
en: Is that so hard to believe?

speaker: Attaway
en: Whatever your intentions, it will be quite the tonic to strike back against Millner and Starrick. I have worked like a trooper to make Attaway Transport what it is today. I will not allow anyone to bring me to ruin.

speaker: Attaway
en: That's one of Millner's!

speaker: Attaway
en: I can't lose another bus! Get away from my bus! She can't take much more of this!

speaker: Message
en: Wiseman, Report to the storage yard tonight for a special task. Forbes

speaker: Attaway
en: Malcolm Millner, Starrick's puppet himself.

speaker: Millner
en: Careful, you twats! This has to make it to the Attaway depot!

speaker: Attaway
en: He thinks he can burn my buses?! Let's give him a taste of his own medicine.

speaker: Jacob
en: Let's give him the whole damn bottle. We'll turn Millner's parkesine against him. But I'll need help from my gang.

speaker: Attaway
en: Such entrepreneurial instinct, Mr. Frye! I shall leave you to it.

speaker: Thug 1
en: You can see that smoke from across the bloody river.

speaker: Thug 2
en: Settin' her buses on fire. It never gets old.

speaker: Thug 3
en: Serves Attaway right for thinking she has the right to compete with us.

speaker: Thug 4
en: I don't know what happened to the driver. I just passed him on to Millner. That was a week ago.

speaker: Thug 5
en: Millner wouldn't exactly treat one of Attaway's employees to tea and biscuits, now would he?

speaker: Thug 6
en: The end result is that she's got fewer people on her payroll. That's all I care about.

speaker: Thug 5
en: Not interested in how the meat pie's made, eh?

speaker: Thug 7
en: Why does Millner want us poisoning her horses? Wouldn't it be better to steal them?

speaker: Thug 8
en: Millner has enough horses. Besides, Attaway can prove a theft. She can't prove poisoning.

speaker: Thug 7
en: Right.

speaker: Jacob
en: Ugh... heave ho, Jacob.

speaker: Jacob
en: Primed and ready.

speaker: Jacob
en: How's that for a taste?

speaker: Attaway
en: I can see Millner's stock price plummeting already! You're hired! Oh, I have more business plans for us both. Drop a note to my secretary to make an appointment and I shall reveal the next step in our scheme.

speaker: Jacob
en: I don't actually work

speaker: Jacob
en: like that?

speaker: Roth
en: Ah! This way, my dear. I've something to show you! Hop in!

speaker: Jacob
en: Where are we going?

speaker: Roth
en: One of Starrick's workshops, where they build weapons for his army. When the world is full of nasty things, we must tear those things apart. A man like Starrick builds a world around his own desires, so we lose the ability to dream for ourselves. Therefore, we must

speaker: Jacob
en: Strike.

speaker: Roth
en: Precisely! No matter the cost... Every second of hesitation allows Starrick time to build.

speaker: Jacob
en: What a funk in here.

speaker: Roth
en: You must SEE the potential, dear Jacob. This workshop is one of Starrick's! Set the dynamite, and let's blow it to atoms. Together.

speaker: Jacob
en: That's one. There. Set. And done!

speaker: Jacob
en: All rigged up.

speaker: Roth
en: Perfect, let's put our plan into action... Stand back! Ready!

speaker: Jacob
en: Wait!

speaker: Roth
en: Whatever for?

speaker: Jacob
en: There are children in there!

speaker: Roth
en: Jacob, my dear, Starrick uses child labor to manufacture goods. We must put an end to his production line.

speaker: Jacob
en: But not like this.

speaker: Roth
en: Why not?! I can do whatever I damn well please! Soon, you will understand what it is to be free, as I am. Light 'em up, boys!

speaker: Jacob
en: No!

speaker: Roth
en: What the hell are you doing?!

speaker: Jacob
en: We're not playing games anymore, Roth!

speaker: Roth
en: No. We're not.

speaker: Jacob
en: Out you get, move quickly, no time to idle! Hurry along! Your shift's over!

speaker: Lewis
en: A gift, sir, from Mr. Roth. You should be warned, Mr. Frye, that when Roth is angry with one, he generally brings suffering to many.

speaker: Messenger
en: London's so-called "Bloody Nora" has challenged you to a gang war. All weapons permitted. Good luck to both sides.

speaker: Messenger
en: With Miss Nora gone, I'd say your chances of winning the fight have increased, but I'd still keep my eyes on those Blighters if I were you.

speaker: Evie
en: This borough is ours for the taking!

speaker: Frye
en: Fight!

speaker: Nora
en: All right! Step aside, you louts!

speaker: Frye
en: Ladies and gentlemen! We are Evie and Jacob Frye! And as of this moment, you all work, for us!

speaker: Messenger
en: Mister Cletus Strain and the Blighters have challenged the Rooks to a fight for territory in Lambeth. Defeat him and the borough is yours. Look sharp, he's a bit sadistic.

speaker: Evie
en: We will win the fight for Lambeth!

speaker: Jacob
en: Down with the Blighters!

speaker: Strain
en: Here we go round the mulberry bush/So early in the morning!

speaker: Evie
en: Ladies and gentlemen! We are Evie and Jacob Frye! And as of this moment, you all work for us!

speaker: Messenger
en: Miss Plumb has, although reluctantly, accepted your challenge. All weapons permitted. May the strongest brutes win.

speaker: Messenger
en: Miss Plumb is no longer head of the Southwark Blighters, and they go into this fight leaderless. Rooks have good odds.

speaker: Evie
en: Rooks! Southwark belongs to you!

speaker: Jacob
en: Show the Blighters who owns this borough!

speaker: Plumb
en: You... butchered my friends... And now I will butcher you!

speaker: Evie
en: Ladies and gentlemen! We are Evie and Jacob Frye! And as of this moment, you all work, for us!

speaker: Messenger
en: Mister Lynch has agreed to your terms. In exchange, he will be fighting with electrochemical bombs. He sends his highest regards and encourages you to bring your bravery.

speaker: Messenger
en: I hear you've dealt with Mr. Lynch on your own terms. Now all that stands between you and the Strand are his ever-loyal cronies. Good luck.

speaker: Evie
en: This borough is ours for the taking!

speaker: Frye
en: Down with the Blighters!

speaker: Lynch
en: Now to blow you to smithereens.

speaker: Frye
en: Ladies and gentlemen! We are Evie and Jacob Frye! And as of this moment, you all work, for us!

speaker: Messenger
en: Miss Swinebourne has agreed to your terms. Everything is permitted in this gang fight. The wager is ownership of the Thames. Good luck.

speaker: Messenger
en: The Rooks are in good standing, with Miss Swinebourne no longer leading the Thames Blighters. Good luck to both sides.

speaker: Evie
en: Show the Blighters who owns this borough!

speaker: Jacob
en: The city belongs to the Rooks!

speaker: Swinebourne
en: Outta the way!

speaker: Evie
en: Ladies and gentlemen! We are Evie and Jacob Frye! And as of this moment, you all work, for us!

speaker: Messenger
en: Miss Graves, known in London as "the Bludger", accepts the terms to this gang war. The fight shall permit the use of all weapons. May the best gang emerge victorious.

speaker: Messenger
en: I always knew the Rooks were strong, but I didn't think you stood a chance against The Bludger! There isn't much standing in your way now.

speaker: Evie
en: Westminster is ours for the taking!

speaker: Graves
en: You ain't gonna take me down!

speaker: Evie
en: Ladies and gentlemen! We are Evie and Jacob Frye! And as of this moment, you all work, for us!

speaker: Henry
en: Ah, there you are! All that stands between you and Whitechapel is the villain controlling the borough. Kaylock has demanded you settle the claim for territory in a gang fight.

speaker: Jacob
en: His loss.

speaker: Henry
en: Here. I'm sure you can put this to better use than I can.

speaker: Jacob
en: What's this Greenie, Assassin Christmas?

speaker: Henry
en: Gather your allies.

speaker: Messenger
en: Mr. Rexford Kaylock has agreed to your terms, and waits for you at the Whitechapel train station. He's bet his train on the fight.

speaker: Jacob
en: No Kaylock? Hmm... No matter.

speaker: Evie
en: Where are you, Kaylock? Perhaps this will draw you out...

speaker: Kaylock
en: Ah! There you are!

speaker: Evie
en: It appears to be broken.

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh well, at least we have a train now, it's not all bad.

speaker: Jacob
en: Kaylock is dead! Whitechapel is no longer in the hands of the Blighters!

speaker: Evie
en: You now have the chance to join our ranks! We welcome all who would stand up to Starrick and his cutthroats!

speaker: Jacob
en: Welcome to the Rooks!

speaker: Agnes
en: Ah, ya bastard. I'd rather throw me'sel to the tracks, than to run Bertha another mile fer that doaty bawbag.

speaker: Jacob
en: Kaylock? He's left the station.

speaker: Agnes
en: Well! Hallo, fancy pants! And who might you two be?

speaker: Evie
en: I'm Evie Frye and this is my brother, Jacob Frye.

speaker: Agnes
en: Pleased to meet ye. I'm Agnes MacBean.

speaker: Jacob
en: A delight.

speaker: Agnes
en: I thought I was gettin' a promotion. I suppose I'm out of work now.

speaker: Evie
en: Come work for us instead.

speaker: Agnes
en: Awa an bile yer heid (away and boil you head)! You pay better than scraps?

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm sure we can at least manage that.

speaker: Agnes
en: Then may I present to you Agnes and Bertha. Lady and locomotive, at your service. I'll be in the next car.

speaker: Henry
en: A hideout on the rails! What an excellent idea.

speaker: Evie
en: Yes, it all worked out rather well. Now, I would like to follow up a lead on

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob, this is serious.

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm not doing anything until this gets fixed.

speaker: Henry
en: I believe I know someone who can help with that.

speaker: Jacob
en: I knew you would, Greenie.

speaker: Agnes
en: You know, a mite o' money goes a mickle bit in this city. Think o' the power o' good you can do with the purse you bring!

speaker: Agnes
en: You talk of restoring London? Well, now's your chance. That there map shows who to speak to - old friends, if you will. Give 'em a wiff o' that sterling and maybe you can save us all from having to lay down our knife and fork afore we're ready!

speaker: Agnes
en: Now, enough shoptalk... Believe Mr. Green said there was someone he wanted you to meet?

speaker: Scrivens
en: Are we all set? The shipment should be arriving any minute now. I want this to go as smoothly as possible. Keep your wits about you, we don't want the police sticking their noses where they don't belong. And sure as the sky is grey in London, I know what you schemers are like. Keep your fingers to yourselves. This shipment is mine. I will take inventory with great scrutiny. So mind your desires. We will bring in coin with this new shipment of... goods.

speaker: Tess
en: That Mister Scrivens has another thing coming.

speaker: Margie
en: Oh, what d'you mean, Tess?

speaker: Tess
en: I mean, look at him, Margie! Never seen a thug dressed so well nor glow so much in me life! Whatever shipments he's bringing in these days is also bringing in a lot of money.

speaker: Scrivens
en: What in God's name! Get off me, you! Leave me alone!

speaker: Jacob
en: Now, now, Mister Scrivens. Keep quiet.

speaker: Scrivens
en: This is none of your business. Piss off!

speaker: Jacob
en: Your criminal activity has made it my business.

speaker: Scrivens
en: What criminal activity? Can't a fellow stand about the docks with his workers and wait for a shipment to come in?

speaker: Jacob
en: A shipment of narcotics? I think not.

speaker: Scrivens
en: What in God's name! Get off me, you! Leave me alone!

speaker: Evie
en: Be quiet, would you? Shhh.

speaker: Scrivens
en: Can't a man do his work without being interrupted?

speaker: Evie
en: Maybe, if that man's work didn't also involve the police.

speaker: Scrivens
en: What exactly has the police involved?

speaker: Evie
en: Does shipping and selling narcotics sound familiar?

speaker: Scrivens
en: Not this time! Help! A strange man is after me! Ha! Too slow! A strange woman is after me, help!

speaker: Scrivens
en: No! Let me go, I say!

speaker: Jacob
en: Come along, Mister Scrivens.

speaker: Scrivens
en: Let me go! I said, let me go!

speaker: Evie
en: Come along now, Mister Scrivens.

speaker: Scrivens
en: Help! I'm trapped! Somebody help me!

speaker: Abberline
en: Thank you, friend.

speaker: Fowler
en: Spread out! There has to be a weak spot somewhere. Find it! Then, we break in and burn everything! If the government won't help people like us to read, then no one shall read at all!

speaker: Fowler
en: Oi! What do you think you're doing?! I'm busy here!

speaker: Jacob
en: Hush, Mister Fowler. Quiet down.

speaker: Fowler
en: What in God's name was that for?

speaker: Jacob
en: Spying on another print house, are we?

speaker: Fowler
en: Was not! All right, maybe I was. But I'm tired of everyone getting what they want, besides me. Nobody ever asked ol' Gilbert what he wanted.

speaker: Jacob
en: Save it for the sergeant, Fowler.

speaker: Fowler
en: Oi! What do you think you're doing?! I'm busy here!

speaker: Evie
en: Keep quiet, Mister Fowler. Hush, now.

speaker: Fowler
en: Oh, let me go, will you?

speaker: Evie
en: Apologies, but the sergeant wants a word.

speaker: Fowler
en: It's about burning down print houses, I know. It was a terrible idea. I should never have done it, but I'm just so angry. I'm so angry and I want everyone to feel as angry as I do.

speaker: Evie
en: The world doesn't need more anger in it, Mister Fowler.

speaker: Fowler
en: Ha! I'm free! I'm being pursued! Help! Yes! Freedom! Oi! A little help over here?

speaker: Fowler
en: Oh, come now! Please let me go!

speaker: Jacob
en: Now where were we?

speaker: Fowler
en: No! Please, miss. Let me go free.

speaker: Evie
en: You were saying?

speaker: Fowler
en: Someone get me out of here!

speaker: Abberline
en: Good. Thank you. One less building burnt to ashes.

speaker: Duleep
en: I've discovered more information on our stolen gold. To my carriage.

speaker: Duleep
en: It's all quite strange: the British Indies Company working with the Templar Order. And for what? Perhaps we will never know. The accountant revealed they're hiding a shipment of gold, previously stolen from India, in a carriage at an old Starrick warehouse. We must find this carriage and steal it from them.

speaker: Jacob
en: And what will you be doing in the meantime?

speaker: Evie
en: And what of you?

speaker: Duleep
en: Why, I'm here to help you of course! They don't call me the fourth best shot in London for nothing!

speaker: Jacob
en: I need to find this gold.

speaker: Evie
en: The gold must be found.

speaker: Duleep
en: This is it, the gold is here somewhere. Return to me once you've found it, and I'll stay behind and keep an eye out for trouble. Be careful. What they think is theirs they won't easily part with.

speaker: Jacob
en: Maybe this warehouse holds the answers.

speaker: Evie
en: This is where the gold is located.

speaker: Templar 1
en: Don't they have enough men over there, keeping things quiet?

speaker: Templar 2
en: It's a big job keeping the colony in check. That's why they've got our help from this side of the pond.

speaker: Templar 1
en: Well I'm glad I'm not in India. Sounds like a jungle of a place.

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: This is it. The gold must be inside. Now to sneak it out of here.

speaker: Templar 3
en: What does he want with all this gold anyway?

speaker: Templar 4
en: We must take it. There will be trouble otherwise.

speaker: Templar 3
en: I'm afraid I don't quite get your meaning.

speaker: Templar 4
en: I mean, if we leave the money overseas with those brutes, who knows what they'll do. The Empire can't afford another riot.

speaker: Templar 5
en: We've got ourselves a rat! Thief! Stop them!

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: I need to get back to Mister Singh.

speaker: Duleep
en: Good. The Templars are not far away and we must lose them! I'll keep the wolves at bay.

speaker: Jacob
en: Are you sure?

speaker: Evie
en: Your highness

speaker: Duleep
en: Hurry, go!

speaker: Jacob
en: I need to lose those Templars.

speaker: Evie
en: I must get rid of these pursuers.

speaker: Jacob
en: Faster!

speaker: Evie
en: Make haste!

speaker: Duleep
en: Damn! My gun is jammed.

speaker: Jacob
en: Leave it to me. You take the reigns!

speaker: Evie
en: Take my place!

speaker: Duleep
en: I get the feeling you've done this before.

speaker: Duleep
en: Here. Take these, I have no use for these bullets now.

speaker: Duleep
en: I think we lost them. Good work.

speaker: Jacob
en: You were quite the hero out there!

speaker: Evie
en: You were quite impressive out there, if I may say.

speaker: Duleep
en: You're too kind. It was rather exhilarating, if I'm being honest... Now, I've hired a captain to escort the gold overseas. If you would kindly fetch the crate from the back.

speaker: Templar 6
en: You can't get away that easily, thief!

speaker: Duleep
en: Are you quite alright? You had me frightened.

speaker: Jacob
en: Nothing to worry about, your highness.

speaker: Evie
en: I'm all right. Really.

speaker: Duleep
en: I commend you for fighting them off. Really. With you at my side, it will be an almost simple task to send this gold back to where it belongs. Why don't you walk off that last fight, and come back to me when you are ready for the next leg of the journey. There's still work to be done.

speaker: Jacob
en: So, what's next, your greatness?

speaker: Evie
en: Where were we?

speaker: Duleep
en: We must return this gold to its people... My people... I've procured us a captain to transport it to its destination. But our next feat will be to get it out of London.

speaker: Jacob
en: And now it's up to you and me to protect it. Fancy that.

speaker: Evie
en: And we must protect it.

speaker: Duleep
en: Precisely. Now, if you would be so good as to bring the gold aboard, we can get going. Come aboard. It's time to leave. We have the gold, and now we must go. Climb aboard.

speaker: Captain
en: Off we go!

speaker: Duleep
en: I knew we wouldn't get far without another appearance from them. Look out!

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm on it!

speaker: Evie
en: Stand back!

speaker: Duleep
en: No. We're in this together.

speaker: Templar
en: Sink them! Don't let them get away with that cargo!

speaker: Captain
en: The engine's stalled! I'll need some time to fix it!

speaker: Duleep
en: The Templars are aboard the ship!

speaker: Jacob
en: They're trying to sink the boat! I must defend the back of the boat!

speaker: Evie
en: They're trying to sink the boat! I must head to the back! The Templars are inflicting serious damage!

speaker: Duleep
en: They're at the bow!

speaker: Jacob
en: Talk about high security.

speaker: Evie
en: They certainly put a strong effort into protecting this gold.

speaker: Duleep
en: How splendid! That should buy our captain enough time.

speaker: Duleep
en: Now we must escort this boat to the next dock where we may disembark. And then this vessel will be clear of enemy waters! We've done some good today. I can feel it.

speaker: Jacob
en: All part of the job.

speaker: Evie
en: I'm glad you feel that way, your highness.

speaker: Jacob
en: Let's see if I can take them out without them noticing.

speaker: Evie
en: We're not finished yet.

speaker: Duleep
en: I think that's the last of them... The gold is in safe hands. We did a good job today. May this not be the end of our adventures together.

speaker: Jacob
en: It would be a shame to part ways now.

speaker: Evie
en: No, let us not end this partnership just yet.

speaker: Duleep
en: We can only move forward from here! Good day.

speaker: Jacob
en: You

speaker: Evie
en: Your highness

speaker: Duleep
en: They are stubborn fellows, aren't they?... Now, if you would be so kind as to excuse me. I've had quite a bit of excitement today and must think on it. Do come see me again.

speaker: Henry
en: Your attempts to influence parliament for the Indian cause have failed. You must do more!

speaker: Duleep
en: I will not jeopardize my relationship with Queen and country to satisfy your crusade.

speaker: Henry
en: Your highness, you belong to India, not here acting the part of the noble foreigner!

speaker: Duleep
en: I have wasted enough time indulging in this nonsense.

speaker: Henry
en: If your mother could see you now, the last Maharajah of Punjab, basking inside his golden cage...

speaker: Duleep
en: How dare you.

speaker: Jacob
en: I always recommend bringing someone's mother into the argument.

speaker: Henry
en: If he doesn't help his people, he will regret it forever.

speaker: Evie
en: How may we help?

speaker: Henry
en: Will you talk to him? He won't listen to me.

speaker: Evie
en: We will do our best.

en: Your highness, you have guests.

speaker: Duleep
en: I suppose Mister Green sent you.

speaker: Jacob
en: Bringing up your mother was

speaker: Evie
en: Impolite and he was wrong to do so. We'd like to rectify the situation.

en: Then humour me, and join me in a shooting game. None of these people have any sense of enjoyment, and I am bored to death.

en: A shooting game? Singh, you haven't changed at all.
