speaker: Ellsworth
en: You've made new friends, I see.

speaker: Duleep
en: What brings you to this part of the Empire?

speaker: Ellsworth
en: Ah, company business, unfortunately. But I could not resist the chance of seeing you again, it's been far too long. I've heard nobody throws a party better than my dearest friend. I am eager to see if your reputation overseas holds any truth.

speaker: Duleep
en: My servant, Thomas, will be scoring the game. Acquire the most amount of points by shooting the bottles in front of you. Each bottle is worth one point. You have thirty seconds. May the best shot win. Start the timer.

speaker: Thomas
en: A perfect score! Nine points!

speaker: Duleep
en: Come, Thomas! This isn't enough of a challenge. Let's shorten the timer.

speaker: Thomas
en: Round two will now commence. Try and do as well, if not better, within a twenty second time limit. Timer at the ready... Begin.

speaker: Thomas
en: Time's up! Nine rounds shot, eight points won!

speaker: Ellsworth
en: Singh you have quite an opponent.

speaker: Thomas
en: Your turn, your highness.

speaker: Ellsworth
en: Come, let us see if you are better with a gun than you were with a slingshot.

speaker: Duleep
en: Allow me.

speaker: Ellsworth
en: Impressive! I am in awe, Singh! What they say of you is true!

speaker: Duleep
en: What on earth?

speaker: Thomas
en: Sir, I believe I heard a second shot.

speaker: Duleep
en: He's right. That sounded like a second gunshot. Strange.

speaker: Jacob
en: Strange, indeed. Let me investigate.

speaker: Evie
en: Let me see what I can find out.

speaker: Duleep
en: I'm sure it wasn't anything serious. Don't bother.

speaker: Duleep
en: You look terrible.

speaker: Evie
en: And you're late.

speaker: Jacob
en: Me? Never! I was simply retrieving the information you sent me to get. It was easy, really... Something about an event happening tonight at the Tower of London?

speaker: Duleep
en: The Gala? I will be attending.

speaker: Jacob
en: You're our in then.

speaker: Evie
en: We can't just barge in and steal the crown jewels.

speaker: Duleep
en: She's right, we need a plan.

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, bother.

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob, you can escort Mister Singh to tonight's event. This will give you a chance to slip away from the party and find the Koh-i-Noor. I will take care of the guards around the perimeter. Meet me at the top of the White Tower.

speaker: Jacob
en: Good! Another chance to wear the suit!

speaker: Evie
en: No weapons allowed.

speaker: Jacob
en: Where's the fun in that?!

speaker: Jacob
en: I should find Singh...

speaker: Duleep
en: The jewels are being held upstairs. But be careful, if this isn't one of the most heavily guarded places, then I'm a true Englishman!

speaker: Jacob
en: I may need your help to distract these guards.

speaker: Duleep
en: Just give me the signal.

speaker: Jacob
en: I should send a signal to Singh to distract the guards. I need Singh to distract those guards.

speaker: Duleep
en: Oh I do believe I've lost a button. Will somebody help me find it? Will you tell me, kind sir, where the lavatory is exactly?

speaker: Jacob
en: The diamond is on the second floor... It's awfully quiet up here.

speaker: Jacob
en: Guard's asleep. Wonder what's inside that crate...

speaker: Jacob
en: Someone got here before I did. Well, if the diamond's not here, I've got to find it before it leaves the building... If it hasn't already. Where could it have gone?

speaker: Templar 1
en: This plan was genius. We'll get him this time.

speaker: Templar 2
en: Friends with the Queen, pah! She won't be friends with him when she finds the diamond is in his pocket!

speaker: Templar 1
en: He'll never see it coming!

speaker: Templar 2
en: Once he tries to walk out that door, he'll kiss his royal title goodbye

speaker: Templar 1
en: And henceforth be known as prisoner Singh!

speaker: Jacob
en: They planted the diamond on Duleep? Not good. I need to lift the diamond from Singh's pocket. Subtlety isn't my strong suit.

speaker: Victoria
en: Oh, your friend is as charming as you are, Mister Singh.

speaker: Brinley
en: You flatter me, ma'am.

speaker: Victoria
en: Now, do tell me. How do you two know each other?

speaker: Duleep
en: We met at the missionary compound in Fategarh, your majesty. The Logins were quite fond of the Ellsworths.

speaker: Brinley
en: Mister Singh and I were quite close, your ladyship. It was a lonely time on foreign soil for me. I was more than happy to have a friend.

speaker: Victoria
en: I'm sure. And now the Company has sent you here on urgent business.

speaker: Brinley
en: I wish I could disclose the information, your ladyship. But alas, I cannot. I'm sure you will learn of it soon enough.

speaker: Jacob
en: Now to find my sister.

speaker: Evie
en: Now to reach the White Tower...

speaker: Evie
en: The place is crawling with Templars! I've got to secure the perimeter.

speaker: Evie
en: What took you so long?

speaker: Jacob
en: Bit of a mishap. Here it is.

speaker: Evie
en: What happened?

speaker: Jacob
en: Somebody stole it first. The safe had been robbed by the time I got there.

speaker: Evie
en: The British Indies Company will stop at nothing.

speaker: Jacob
en: There was a plan to frame Singh. I lifted it from him before the royal guards found it. Imagine the look on her Majesty's face if

speaker: Evie
en: They must know by now that their plan was foiled.

speaker: Jacob
en: You're welcome.

speaker: Evie
en: I think it's time to depart.

speaker: Evie
en: I need to find a way out of here. I hope they make it out all right.

speaker: Duleep
en: Did you get it to your sister?

speaker: Jacob
en: Just barely.

speaker: Duleep
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Jacob
en: I'll tell you about it another time.

speaker: Duleep
en: You encountered some trouble?

speaker: Jacob
en: We can't speak of this here. The British Indies Company is up to no good again.

speaker: Duleep
en: Outside, then.

speaker: Royal guard 1
en: You, sir. Halt for inspection.

speaker: Duleep
en: I beg your pardon.

speaker: Royal guard 1
en: Search him.

speaker: Royal guard 2
en: Nothing. The Koh-i-Noor isn't here.

speaker: Duleep
en: Of course there is nothing! What do you take me for, some sort of criminal?

speaker: Victoria
en: What was all that commotion about, Mister Singh?

speaker: Duleep
en: I do believe they thought I was trying to pinch the Koh-i-Noor, your ladyship.

speaker: Victoria
en: Ha! The Koh-i-Noor? Who on earth would want to steal that potato? Goodnight, your highness.

speaker: Jacob
en: We barely got out of there in one piece. The British Indies Company tried to plant the diamond on you and frame you for stealing it. Luckily, I was there just in the nick of time.

speaker: Duleep
en: We need to meet back at Mister Green's shop. I must see the diamond with my own two eyes.

speaker: Henry
en: The Koh-i-Noor! If I may?

speaker: Duleep
en: Glass?

speaker: Henry
en: The real Koh-i-Noor never left India. Had I known you planned to reclaim it, I would have stopped you. My father ensured it never fell into Templar hands.

speaker: Duleep
en: Your father, he has done a great service to me and my people.

speaker: Henry
en: My words to you earlier were unfair

speaker: Duleep
en: You were not wrong. I, too, have grown frustrated with my lack of progress. Shall we let bygones be bygones?

speaker: Evie
en: We need to find out who is behind all of this. And why have the Templars and the British Indies Company joined forces?

speaker: Jacob
en: What we should do is track them down and destroy their headquarters.

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob

speaker: Duleep
en: That... may not be such a terrible idea, Mister Frye.

speaker: Drake
en: How many crates do we have left to distribute?

speaker: Accomplice
en: Only about a dozen, Sir.

speaker: Drake
en: Good. Soon all of London's Blighters will be armed to the teeth.

speaker: Accomplice
en: No bobbies in sight.

speaker: Drake
en: Good. Distribute the dynamite then, and carefully.

speaker: Accomplice
en: Very good, Sir.

speaker: Drake
en: We want this to come into the Blighters' hands without harm. No mishaps.

en: Beg pardon? Unhand me, rascal! I said, let me go!

speaker: Jacob
en: Quiet down. That's enough out of you, Harley.

speaker: Harley
en: How do you know me? Rumors? The scandal sheets?

speaker: Jacob
en: Your fame reaches beyond scandal sheets, sir.

speaker: Harley
en: How's that?

speaker: Jacob
en: I read about you in the police files.

speaker: Harley
en: They're wrong! I'm an honorable man! I serve the interests of our Father!

speaker: Jacob
en: Save your excuses for the police.

speaker: Harley
en: Beg pardon? Unhand me, rascal! I said, let me go!

speaker: Evie
en: Keep your voice down. Quiet, Mister Harley.

speaker: Harley
en: Who sent you, woman?

speaker: Evie
en: The police.

speaker: Harley
en: Pah! Why would any sane person want to apprehend me! I do what I do for the greater good! This Abbey will not stand! Religion will be purified again!

speaker: Evie
en: And we're the ones putting an end to it.

speaker: Harley
en: Just try and catch me now! Nincompoop! I need some help here!

speaker: Harley
en: Ha! Too slow! I need some help here!

speaker: Harley
en: Damnit!

speaker: Jacob
en: You were saying?

speaker: Harley
en: Let me go!

speaker: Evie
en: Now, now Mister Harley.

speaker: Harley
en: Help! I'm trapped! Someone help me!

speaker: Abberline
en: Something out of a nightmare, that one. You did well.

speaker: Hughes
en: Don't let those crooks get the better of you. My rates are right fair. Did the Bank refuse you a loan? I'll take good care of you. I'm working class, same as you. I know the bank demands high interest rates. That's why I became a money lender!

speaker: Blighter
en: Harvey, we got 'im!

speaker: Man
en: I promise, I'll pay. Please, let me go!

speaker: Hughes
en: Oi! Get your hands off me! Who are you? You ain't some bobby, right?

speaker: Jacob
en: Quiet, you.

en: I was just working, mate.

speaker: Jacob
en: Is that so?

speaker: Hughes
en: There's nothing illegal about what I'm doing. I've got the right to lend money!

speaker: Jacob
en: And rob people with interest?

speaker: Hughes
en: Oi! Get your hands off me! Who are you? You ain't some bobby, right?

en: Hush now, no need for a fuss. I said quiet.

speaker: Hughes
en: There's nothing illegal about what I'm doing!

speaker: Evie
en: Why are you wanted by every bobby division in the city?

speaker: Hughes
en: It's their own fault for using my services unwisely.

speaker: Evie
en: Your "services" have landed more people in the poorhouse than not!

speaker: Hughes
en: Leave me alone! Help! Someone! This man's after me! Help! Get 'er off me!

speaker: Hughes
en: Hey, you need money? I can help you out!

speaker: Jacob
en: Settle down.

speaker: Hughes
en: Not you again!

speaker: Evie
en: Now now, Mister Hughes. It's not the time to play hide-and-seek.

speaker: Hughes
en: Someone! Anyone! Help!

speaker: Abberline
en: Thank you so much!

speaker: Abberline
en: What good will he do me dead?

speaker: Jacob
en: Robberies? In London? I never thought I'd see the day!

speaker: Evie
en: Robberies in London are hardly supernatural events.

speaker: Dickens
en: They looked like common robberies at first, but these perpetrators have all claimed to have been under the influence of some supernatural power. speaker: Jacob
en: What's this one in for?

speaker: Evie
en: What's that man done?

speaker: Policeman
en: Robbed the pawnbroker's down the road.

en: A demon made me do it! I can't remember much. That's what's so queer. I've never stolen anything in my life before!

en: Who do you think made you do this?

en: All I can recall is a silver watch, swinging in mid-air. It was held by someone, - or some thing! A dark presence whispering. I could only see its eyes. A demon!

en: Maybe the shopkeeper will make more sense.

en: A demon made me do it! I can't remember much. That's what's so queer. I've never stolen anything in my life before!

en: Not again! Stop her! Stop! Somebody stop that thief!

en: Where am I? What's happening?

en: You were just indulging in a little light theft.

en: It's all very hazy but - I remember something silver flashing in front of my eyes. Then I heard a sort of bell. Next thing I know, I'm here with you.

speaker: Jacob
en: Back on track. Now to find this buyer.

speaker: Thief 1
en: Where am I? What's happening?

en: It's all very hazy but - I remember something silver flashing in front of my eyes. Then I heard a sort of bell. Next thing I know, I'm here with you.

en: This chap might lead me to the "demon".

en: Yes. I want to give you the necklace now.

en: Would you care to tell me your plans?

speaker: Templar
en: Go to hell.

speaker: Jacob
en: Fair enough.

speaker: Evie
en: Now, now.

speaker: Templar
en: Starrick may be dead and gone, but the Templar Order will never die! We will rise again, like a phoenix from the ashes, and bring the world to its knees!

speaker: Jacob
en: Not exactly Grand Master material, are you?

speaker: Evie
en: Yes, well. Best of luck with that.

speaker: Fleming
en: Thank you. I'll carry on from here. My people are recovering their explosive cargo. You did fine work today. I will have a chat with our distinguished guest here to see what schemes he and his friends are brewing.

speaker: Jacob
en: Do get in touch when he spills his guts.

speaker: Evie
en: Do let me know if he says anything interesting.

speaker: Fleming
en: Of course.

speaker: Victoria
en: Mr. Fleming has attempted to force a confession from your prisoner. The miscreant refuses to talk. Will you speak to the villain and learn his secrets?

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, I'd be delighted, ma'am.

speaker: Evie
en: Leave it to me, your majesty.

speaker: Jacob
en: I don't suppose you'd like to spare yourself a tremendous beating and make a clean breast of it?

speaker: Evie
en: Must I pummel you severely about the head and shoulders? Or can we simply talk?

speaker: Templar
en: Might as well. The order was to load a train with explosives at Westminster. It'll detonate before reaching Southwark station and kill everyone aboard!

speaker: Jacob
en: I did not expect you to confess! Which train?

speaker: Evie
en: You people and your damned dynamite. When does it happen?

speaker: Templar
en: It's the next train! It should leave at any moment! You'll never make it in time!

speaker: Jacob
en: Damn! I can't reach the bomb. I'll detach the locomotive.

speaker: Evie
en: Locked! I'll separate the bomb from the other cars!

speaker: Victoria
en: The final group of upstarts are making their last, desperate stand. They have penetrated the House of Parliament and plan to detonate whatever explosives they have left. Please find Mr. Fleming so we might put an end to this once and for all.

speaker: Fleming
en: Multiple targets inside the palace. All armed and dangerous. Making matters worse—the Prime Minister has gone missing. I need you to deal with the Templars. Target one is in a nearby corridor, surrounded by civilians. He has explosives on his person. You need to take him by surprise. If he sees you, he'll detonate his bomb. In the meantime, I'll search for the Prime Minister.

speaker: Fleming
en: Well done. But there are still more bombers about. They must be removed--quickly and quietly.

speaker: Fleming
en: Catch the devil! He mustn't escape!

speaker: Templar
en: Don't come any closer!

speaker: Jacob
en: Mr. Fleming, I've located the Prime Minister!

speaker: Evie
en: Steady, Prime Minister, I'll have you free in a moment.

speaker: Templar
en: Not another step, Assassin! You've lost, don't you see? The Houses of Parliament are rigged to explode at the last stroke of twelve! There's nothing you or anyone else can do to stop it now. The Houses of Parliament will be leveled! Centuries of history are going to be blown away in a second!

speaker: Disraeli
en: I demand you kill this lunatic!

speaker: Disraeli
en: Find those bombs before they go off!

speaker: Disraeli
en: Thank you, my young friend. Now, please come with me. You and your sibling have been summoned.

speaker: Victoria
en: Approach. You have honored us with your loyalty and courage. Long may we strengthen the Empire together!

speaker: Jacob
en: Your Majesty. We will always work to ensure the safety of the people.

speaker: Evie
en: But with the greatest respect, our philosophy forbids us from assisting with the expansion of the Empire. Perhaps, ma'am, you could consider putting an end to your imperialist desires?

speaker: Victoria
en: I understand and respect your position, bound as you are by your Creed. You will indulge me one final time and receive these gifts. Goodbye and may God bless the noble Fryes!

speaker: Jacob
en: I don't suppose you'll be offered any more cake.

speaker: Dickens
en: Ah, my dear Darwin, do you think our young friend here, equipped with a multiplicity of talents, might be enough to ensure Mister Hammon safe passage?

speaker: Jacob
en: Who's Hammon when he's at home, then?

speaker: Evie
en: I do not believe I've had the pleasure of meeting a Mister Hammon.

speaker: Dickens
en: A mutual friend of ours. He arrives in London today.

speaker: Darwin
en: From South Africa no less!

speaker: Dickens
en: Mister Hammon is possessed of both tremendous wealth and charming innocence.

speaker: Darwin
en: Which makes him rather attractive prey for some of our great city's less savoury inhabitants. We fear he'll need a more robust escort than two old men might provide.

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm not a coachman, you know.

speaker: Evie
en: I'm actually rather busy.

speaker: Darwin
en: We have already told him to expect you!

speaker: Dickens
en: His train should have arrived ten minutes ago.

speaker: Jacob
en: Well then, I suppose a friend of yours, is a friend of mine.

speaker: Evie
en: Then I shan't keep him waiting.

speaker: Darwin
en: Splendid!

speaker: Dickens
en: Off you go.

speaker: Jacob
en: Mister John Hammon?

speaker: Evie
en: Mister Hammon, I believe?

speaker: Hammon
en: That is correct.

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: Jacob/Evie Frye. Mister Dickens sent me to meet you.

speaker: Hammon
en: Ah, good old Dickens. How very kind of him. Lead on, then.

speaker: Hammon
en: London... Can't say I've missed the weather. My father passed away recently and I have come home to settle his affairs. Also, I am to be married.

speaker: Jacob
en: You don't sound too keen on the idea.

speaker: Evie
en: You don't sound too eager for the happy event.

speaker: Hammon
en: I have never even met my future bride, Bella Wilton. It was all arranged for me. She may be a good woman. Or she may not. I stand to inherit a vast sum. Can I be certain that the lady is not simply in it for the money?

speaker: Blighter 1
en: Hand over your money, quick as quick.

speaker: Blighter 2
en: I like your togs. Care to trade 'em for mine?

speaker: Hammon
en: By Jove! You're handy to have around. I fear my wealth attracts too much attention.

speaker: Hammon
en: That did give me an idea. Perhaps I can test my bride's sincerity. I am now officially dead and have thus shed my fortune. I shall meet Bella Wilton as a nobody. We shall see if she'll have me now. Come, we must dispose of my body. Find us a carriage to take us to the river.

speaker: Hammon
en: Good work. How exciting! This is like something out of a novel!

speaker: Hammon
en: Excellent! Now let us go and meet my fiancee. I can't wait to see her response.

speaker: Hammon
en: I feel quite liberated. As if a great weight has been lifted from my shoulders. After this, just to be sure, would you take me to my fiancee's house? I shall deliver the sad news myself.

speaker: Jacob
en: Seems a bit risky to me.

speaker: Evie
en: Don't you think that's a little risky?

speaker: Hammon
en: She has never set eyes on me! Besides I need to ascertain whether I like her as well! And I want to see how she reacts to the news of my death... Come on, hurry up. This is taking far too long. You're going the wrong way. I'm sure of it. Please hurry. I'm very anxious to meet Miss Wilton.

speaker: Hammon
en: Miss Wilton?

speaker: Bella
en: Yes?

speaker: Hammon
en: My name is John Rokesmith. I am afraid I have some terrible news for you.

speaker: Bella
en: Oh?

speaker: Hammon
en: Your fiancé, John Hammon was found dead in the River Thames this morning.

speaker: Bella
en: Oh, how awful! Poor Mister Hammon. I am at a loss at what to say to you, sir, you must forgive me.

speaker: Hammon
en: She is delightful! Why I do believe I love her!

speaker: Jacob
en: Certainly an unu csual first meeting to talk about in your wedding speech!

speaker: Evie
en: I hope she's more intrigued than she is appalled!

speaker: Darwin
en: Mr. Frye! I trust that you had a productive meeting with Mr. Owen?

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh yes, we had a most wonderful chat. I've found that the man behind Starrick's Soothing Syrup is John Elliotson.

speaker: Darwin
en: Dr. Elliotson? I haven't heard that name in a long while. He was a brilliant heart specialist, until he became obsessed with and . It ruined his career. Well, how shall we proceed?

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, with all respect, Mr. Darwin, I believe I should proceed alone. After all, we wouldn't want to attract any... "unwanted attention".

speaker: Darwin
en: Sounds very wise. Good luck, my boy. Oh, and, Mr. Frye, should you find yourself with any free time, please, do call on me.

speaker: Jacob
en: Where would I find the doctor?...

speaker: Jacob
en: Hmm...

speaker: Elliotson
en: Well, as you've just witnessed, the application of too much pressure can sometimes result in... unexpected outcomes. Unfortunately, it appears I've... ruined the organ.

speaker: Elliotson
en: Send up a cadaver.

speaker: Doctor
en: At once, Dr. Elliotson.

speaker: Guard 1
en: I don't care about your ethics! And I care even less about your damned patients. Now hand over your keys!

speaker: Nurse
en: What are you doing?!

speaker: Guard 1
en: Haven't you heard? You're fired! Now bugger off.

speaker: Jacob
en: How to do it?

speaker: Elliotson
en: While we are waiting, I shall resume my discourse on phrenology, the only true science of the mind. The idea that one can point out connections and relations which exist between the conditions and development of the brain, and perhaps more importantly manifestations of the mind, is no longer a pervasive phenomenon, yet as we've previously studied, phrenology, when rigorously practiced, allows us to discover each criminal specimen. The science teaches us how to not only identify but also how to measure the mental faculties of a patient. For instance, this specimen's overdeveloped organs found on either side of the lower back of its head, the protuberances previously measured, establish the correctness of both police records and medical observation. I am, of course, referring to the specimen's tendency to provoke and assault, undesirable propensities which were wholly suppressed by the use of the Soothing Syrup. Despite the specimen's violent reaction to the procedure, the Soothing Syrup anesthetized its senses and it died without suffering. What you have just witnessed is nothing less than the undeniable effectiveness of the medicine of tomorrow.

speaker: Guard 2
en: So what's this I here about Dr. Elliotson's experiments?

speaker: Guard 3
en: That fellow holds a candle to the devil.

speaker: Nurse
en: Can anyone help me? I'm trapped in here? Is there anybody out there? Let me out of here!

speaker: Jacob
en: What's the matter?

speaker: Nurse
en: Young man, help... I must speak with Miss Nightingale at once! One of the brutes stole my key, and there's no one around, I can't get out of here.

speaker: Jacob
en: Stole your key? Don't go anywhere, I might be able to do something.

speaker: Nurse
en: Oh, quite, thank you, sir. Well, you'll know where to find me, sir. Go on now, sir, I will wait here. Dr. Elliotson cannot be allowed to continue his experimentations! I must speak to Nurse Nightingale. She will know what to do. There's something peculiar about that Dr. Elliotson. His experimentations are making our patients worse, I'm sure of it.

speaker: Guard 4
en: I wouldn't trust any of the doctors here. Especially that Elliotson fellow. I'm in the wrong line of work. I wonder why so few patients died this week.

speaker: Nurse
en: You have my gratitude, sir. I shall inform Miss Nightingale that I'll not be working for this asylum ever again!

speaker: Guard 5
en: Blimey, hold him down, will ya?

speaker: Guard 6
en: What's wrong with him?

speaker: Guard 5
en: Do I look like a doctor? He's barmy, is all.

speaker: Guard 6
en: Ah, nothing a little syrup won't cure.

speaker: Guard 5
en: Haven't you heard? Stocks are low, we can't administer Soothing Syrup without Dr. Elliotson's written consent.

speaker: Guard 6
en: Ah, bollocks.

speaker: Doctor
en: Of course not, Dr. Elliotson, it will only take a moment. Urgh, bloody rats! Get back, you filth! How hard can it be to fix a bloody crack in the wall? And don't come back!

speaker: Doctor
en: I'm sorry, sir, but you aren't allowed in here. I'm afraid I must ask you to leave, sir. Authorized personnel only. Please, go away.

speaker: Doctor
en: Here it is, Doctor.

speaker: Elliotson
en: We will continue our experiment shortly. In a moment, we will compare the brains of our two specimens. And since both specimens had a propensity towards violent behavior, we should see similar protrusions in specific parts of their brains—Corpses do not have boots.

speaker: Elliotson
en: Grand Master Starrick warned us about you, Assassin... Your presence in London has not gone unnoticed, especially since the destruction of our Syrup distillery. What a pitiful fool you are... What will the people rely on now to ease their troubled minds? To keep them happy in this bleak, modern world of ours? You are nothing, Assassin. Surrounded, outnumbered. We are everywhere. Our resources are inexhaustible, our reach limitless... What influence do you imagine that a handful of criminals have compared to the Templar Order? You are pathetic, obsolete, like the tenets of your Creed.

speaker: Elliotson
en: At last it ends... Yet I can only think of beginnings... A better tomorrow, forged with the blood of visionaries.

speaker: Jacob
en: All I see is the blood of a lunatic.

speaker: Elliotson
en: Do you truly believe murdering an old man will stop humanity's Great Architect? Crawford Starrick has a glorious design for mankind!

speaker: Jacob
en: Designs are meant to be broken.

speaker: Elliotson
en: You're a child... A child who believes he can solve all the world's woes with a flick of a blade... Have you ever pondered the consequences of your actions, Jacob Frye? Or did your father teach you nothing?

speaker: Students
en: Help! Help Guards! My god! Police! Police!

speaker: Guard 7
en: And then he tells her to bugger off, but she can't get out without her key.

speaker: Guard 8
en: She'll report him to Miss Nightingale, you know.

speaker: Philip Twopenny
en: Elliotson expired and Soothing Syrup production has ceased? Outrageous!

speaker: James Brudenell, 7th Earl of Cardigan
en: Frye intends to endanger all of London at the hands of the mob.

speaker: Philip
en: Or perhaps he doesn't intend much of anything at all, but is simply content to dice with our lives.

speaker: Crawford
en: Thank you.

speaker: James
en: The asylum is shut up, medical care throughout the city is in disarray. He does not, cannot, understand the consequences of his actions. The man is clearly an anarchist!

speaker: Crawford
en: Gentlemen. This tea was brought to me from India by a ship, then, up from the harbor to a factory, where it was packaged and ferried by carriage to my door, unpacked in the larder and brought upstairs to me. All by men and women who work for me. Who are indebted to me, Crawford Starrick, for their jobs, their time, the very lives they lead. They will work in my factories and so too shall their children. And you come to me with talk of this Jacob Frye? This insignificant blemish who calls himself Assassin? You disrespect the very city that works day and night so that we may drink this. This miracle. This tea.

speaker: Lucy
en: I am nearing the end of my research. Our beloved London shall not suffer such a bothersome fool for much longer.

speaker: Crawford
en: And what of this sister I've heard of? Miss Frye?

speaker: Lucy
en: Miss Frye shall be gutted. Soon enough.

speaker: Lucy
en: Delicious.

speaker: Needham
en: I will be as Achilles was. I will be great and powerful. And I will live on in the minds of the weak.

speaker: Needham
en: This is it, this is my moment!

speaker: Needham
en: From now on, everyone will remember Peter Needham. Peter the Strong, Peter the Conqueror, Peter the Great!

speaker: Needham
en: The ancient ruins below will rise and the old will be new again.

speaker: Beckinridge
en: Keep the wheels turning at all costs. Stop for nothing!

speaker: Beckinridge
en: Back to work! We can't fall behind schedule now!

speaker: Beckinridge
en: If we don't meet our quota, I'll dock all your pay!

speaker: Jacob
en: "Dear Mr. Starrick, Men hired. Strike tomorrow. Disraeli's death will stall indefinitely. Gladstone will be far more pliable. May the Father, etc., etc. – B" So Starrick's got his finger in politics, has he? I need to enter this Sinopean Club and find out who "B" is.

speaker: Evie
en: Tread delicately around Parliament.

speaker: Jacob
en: As if I don't usually.

speaker: Evie
en: Your indiscretion at the Bank of England caused British currency to nearly collapse.

speaker: Jacob
en: "Nearly" is the operative word. Speaking of collapses, what of the key you found that unlocks very little?

speaker: Evie
en: Henry took it for research. I am confident that the vault is ours.

speaker: Jacob
en: "Nearly" ours, Evie. Nearly.

speaker: Jacob
en: All right, "B", who are you and what's your game?

speaker: Jacob
en: Well, if it isn't my dear old chum, Mr. Disraeli. Now, Prime Minister, which of your friends is about to stab you in the back?

speaker: Disraeli
en: The Corrupt Practices Bill is a vital step in reforming our government. If the majority party is allowed to dictate the results of contested , we can scarcely call ourselves free.

speaker: Gladstone
en: If we yield up our rights bit by bit to the courts, we can scarcely call ourselves free, sir.

speaker: Disraeli
en: This is so like you, Gladstone! You would rather throw your body upon the gears of progress than surrender one iota of power!

speaker: Gladstone
en: By God, Disraeli, you are a fool! I'll not stand idly by and watch you drag Parliamentary privilege through the muck!

speaker: Disraeli
en: No, certainly not! You'd rather return us to the yoke of tyranny? Perhaps while we're at it, Mr. Gladstone, we could repeal and return the crown to the bloody !

speaker: Gladstone
en: How dare you, sir! Merely because I do not wish to see government placed in the hands of judges, you would make these slanderous accusations? I'll not stand for it!

speaker: Disraeli
en: Then I shall obviate the requirement. Good evening, sir.

speaker: Jacob
en: "B", I presume?

speaker: Jacob
en: Pleasure to meet you, "B".

speaker: Herbert
en: "B"? My name's Herbert!

speaker: Jacob
en: Then why are you following the Prime Minister?

speaker: Herbert
en: It's just a job, sir. Some old bloke paid me to

speaker: Jacob
en: Smug bastard.

speaker: Sniper
en: Yappy bastard! Mopsy bugger!

speaker: Sniper
en: Shite!

speaker: Sniper
en: Bloody hell! Where'd you come from?

speaker: Jacob
en: Well, I was born in Crawley, but that's by the by. Who are you working for?

speaker: Sniper
en: I-I never got his name. Old chap. Big moustache. Wore some kind of uniform. Hussars, maybe.

speaker: Jacob
en: What's his game?

speaker: Sniper
en: Please, he'll kill me.

speaker: Jacob
en: And a three-story drop will shatter your legs and send you to the workhouse, difference is, you can run from him.

speaker: Sniper
en: Tomorrow! My lads are going to attack the Prime Minister's carriage on the way to Parliament.

speaker: Jacob
en: Perfect.

speaker: Dickens
en: Have you truly no recollection of the events that landed you in a cell?

speaker: Jacob
en: I remember what the other victims remember. A silver watch, the sound of a bell and a sort of shadow.

speaker: Evie
en: My mind is blank, save for the glint of a silver object, the toll of a bell, and a presence of some sort.

speaker: Dickens
en: A glint of silver and a tolling bell, eh? I must say, you look very tired.

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: Yes. I am so very, very tired.

speaker: Enzio
en: Now you're going to do a little job of work for me, aren't you?

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: Now I'm going to do a little job of work for you.

speaker: Enzio
en: You cost me a bit of money, mate, so I think it's only fair that you replenish my coffers with donations from the good people of London. You will steal money for me, won't you?

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: Yes. I will steal money for you.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: How dare you! Leave me alone!

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Help! Thief!

speaker: Civilian 3
en: Oi, get away from me, you dodger!

speaker: Enzio
en: Good, very good. Now, we can't have criminals like you roaming the streets. You will surrender to the police, won't you?

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: Yes, I will surrender to the police.

speaker: Enzio
en: Oh, and when you do, you're going to do a silly little dance for them.

speaker: Dickens
en: I say, you gave me a terrible fright. Muttering about a man named "Ezio".

speaker: Jacob
en: Enzio Capelli. Not a demon, but a hypnotist. And he's not even Italian!

speaker: Evie
en: I was hypnotized by Enzio Capelli. Not a demon after all. Nor Italian, for that matter!

speaker: Dickens
en: I suspected hypnotism from the very start! You must find the villain.

speaker: Enzio
en: You're going to stand watch while I ransack this house, aren't you?

speaker: Enzio
en: You're going to obey the bell, aren't you?

speaker: Blighters 1
en: Yes. I'm going to obey the bell.

speaker: Blighters 2
en: Keep an eye out for valuables.

speaker: Enzio
en: What was that noise? Go take a look!

speaker: Enzio
en: Release me at once! I admit it! I'm not Italian! It was just for my act! Nobody wanted to see a British hypnotist!

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, shut up!

speaker: Evie
en: I don't care.

speaker: Enzio
en: I'll give you anything you want!

speaker: Jacob
en: I want you to shut your mouth. Do you know a Doctor John Elliotson?

speaker: Evie
en: I would like you to be quiet. Are you a contemporary of Dr. Elliotson?

speaker: Enzio
en: Never heard of the man.

speaker: Jacob
en: Do you really think mesmerism would work?

speaker: Evie
en: Mesmerism as a criminal enterprise was not a bright idea.

speaker: Enzio
en: How dare you! I'm a hypnotist!

speaker: Enzio
en: My body does not bend that way! This is really quite painful. Can we not work out an arrangement?

speaker: Jacob
en: Time to confess and free the people under your silly spell.

speaker: Evie
en: You will make reparation for your crimes and liberate the innocents you've used.

speaker: Attaway
en: Mr. Frye! I told you to make an appointment.

speaker: Jacob
en: My schedule was open.

speaker: Attaway
en: You're fortunate I like you.

speaker: Jacob
en: "Internal combustion engines"?

speaker: Attaway
en: Eight small syllables that mean a great deal of money. The engines will be delivered to Millner by train. Secure them for me and he will be... devastated.

speaker: Jacob
en: I'll need a second train to pull this off... And I think I know just the man.

speaker: Attaway
en: So we have a deal, Mr. Frye?

speaker: Jacob
en: "You're fortunate I like you", Miss Attaway.

speaker: Policeman
en: The Captain's been looking for you for some time, Wynert.

speaker: Ned
en: There are laws against arresting an innocent?

speaker: Policeman
en: Shut your trap!

speaker: Ned
en: What the hell's going on out there?

speaker: Jacob
en: A change of plans, that's what's going on!

speaker: Ned
en: Frye? God damn it! Where do you come off rescuing me?

speaker: Jacob
en: I believe it's pronounced "thank you", you ingrate!

speaker: Ned
en: I operate on a strict policy of keeping people indebted to me, not the other way around. I hate having to return favors!

speaker: Jacob
en: I could leave you here for the police to collect you.

speaker: Ned
en: No, it's too late now. Just get us out of here.

speaker: Ned
en: So, what do you want, Frye?

speaker: Jacob
en: What makes you so sure I want something? Perhaps I saved you out of the kindness of my own heart.

speaker: Jacob
en: Come on, let me tell you about the job.

speaker: Ned
en: Millner's pulling a lot of cargo there!

speaker: Jacob
en: Just be sure to make the transfer!

speaker: Ned
en: Give 'em hell! Hurry up, man! We don't have all day! Get cracking! Get a move on, Frye!

speaker: Jacob
en: Not this one! Not what I'm after! Here we go!

speaker: Ned
en: All right, boys and girls! You know what to do! What are you waiting for, friends? Get moving!

speaker: Jacob
en: The internal combustion engine. The end of horse-drawn transport. It's like gazing into the future.

speaker: Ned
en: And what is the going rate for the future, do you think?

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, we're not selling them.

speaker: Ned
en: You're giving them to your contact?

speaker: Jacob
en: You'll be paid all the same.

speaker: Ned
en: Who is this Pearl, anyway? How long have you been working with her?

speaker: Jacob
en: She's a business partner. That's all you need to know.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Bloody Nora sends word to remain on the lookout for this rebel gang. Nora urges us to remain vigilant, but we don't need warnings. The Blighters control this borough, this city. Warnings be damned!

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: With Kaylock gone, I suppose our plans for expansion will have to wait. Pity.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Do not speak to me about these so-called Rooks. I have no interest in them and neither should you.

speaker: Duleep
en: I spoke with Mister Green and we have discovered the location of the British Indies secret headquarters. You are to meet him, and he will give you the details. There is a foundry nearby where the Templars and B.I.C. members have been meeting on a regular basis. Mister Green waits for you there.

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: But we still don't understand why they tried to frame you.

speaker: Duleep
en: We don't but Mister Green seemed to think they're using the factory to develop something. It's a good place to start digging. Good luck.

speaker: Henry
en: You made it.

speaker: Jacob
en: You found the British Indies Company hideout?

speaker: Evie
en: His highness said you found the British Indies Company headquarters.

speaker: Henry
en: They've taken over an abandoned foundry. It's heavily fortified and word has it, they're shipping something precious overseas.

speaker: Jacob
en: My gut tells me that "something precious" is something bad.

speaker: Evie
en: Whatever it is, it can't be good.

speaker: Henry
en: My thoughts exactly. Go find out what they're protecting and destroy it. Maybe you'll discover why they're after Mister Singh.

speaker: Jacob
en: So this is where they've been keeping that sleeping gas... They can't leave London.

speaker: Evie
en: This is where they're hiding that elusive sleeping gas... These crates can't leave London.

speaker: Jacob
en: They're shipping this to India? No... What do they want this for? War? I must destroy them.

speaker: Evie
en: They're shipping this to India? It can't be... They're creating a biological weapon. I must destroy them.

speaker: Templar
en: Sir!... Somebody get the boss. We've got a problem.

speaker: Jacob
en: Yes, go fetch the manager.

speaker: Evie
en: This is it. We've got them now.

speaker: Templar
en: Sir! The bomb shipments! They've been destroyed!

speaker: Jacob

speaker: Henry
en: Brother George. It is as I feared. London has fallen. Thrice I have written to you, begging your aid. Thrice you've responded - with silence. And yet I write again, so desperate my need, so few my options. I need you. London needs you. You would say it is too great of a task. Or that it is not yet time to strike. Patience, you would counsel. But whilst you wait, the Templars consolidate their power. They have chosen a Grand Master so ruthless, so thorough, one might think Reginald Birch, himself, had returned. His name is Crawford Starrick. And he intends to rule the world. There is no aspect of society he does not control. No industry that escapes his grim touch. By day, it is corrupt merchants and venal politicians who hold court. Come night, a vicious street gang known as the Blighters strikes terror in the hearts of all. There is no business untainted by his poison. No person unexploited - be it by duplicity or force. Our enemy has designs on the highest office of them all. And so, as you look inward - and dare I say it - afraid - Crawford Starrick's ambition is fixed on the beyond: To kingdoms and continents as yet unconquered. Though not for long. For he knows - as I have warned you - time and time again - whosoever controls London, controls the world.

No time must be wasted! Profits and production must increase twofold, or your wages will be cut! Extra overseers have been appointed to ensure Ferris Ironworks remains second to none! en: A heavily guarded warehouse, hm? I wonder what they're heavily guarding.

speaker: Jack
en: Who are you to deny us our sport? The scum of London are as base as animals, and we treat them as such! We take our inspiration from Jack, who knows how to treat the lower classes.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: We've recently received a shipment of new pistols from our leader Mr. Lynch. After supper, please come and see me for your distribution. These new weapons will surely help us defeat those damned Rooks. I do so long to pluck their eyes out. They rather get on my nerves. We need to do away with these Frye twins. They're nothing but trouble to the Blighter organization.

speaker: Jacob
en: A dinner invitation.

speaker: Evie
en: And with whom are you dining this evening?

speaker: Jacob
en: Maxwell Roth.

speaker: Evie
en: The leader of the Blighters? You're not going.

speaker: Jacob
en: Of course not.

speaker: Jacob
en: Hmm. Better check the back.

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm here to see Mr. Roth.

speaker: Lewis
en: Weapons?

speaker: Jacob
en: No, thank you. I've got my own.

speaker: Lewis
en: You should be on the stage, sir. This way.

speaker: Roth
en: Ah! Our honored guest has arrived! Come sit.

speaker: Roth
en: I've had my eye on you for some time. I find your... heroics in battling the great Crawford Starrick quite magnificent.

speaker: Jacob
en: I've been picking off your soldiers one by one, doesn't that make you angry?

speaker: Roth
en: On the contrary. Surprise is the spice of life! Now, Mr. Starrick, that's a different story. I'm drowning in directives, all terribly boring. Let's say we work together and bring him down?

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm not so sure about that...

speaker: Roth
en: My friend, if I fail to provide you with the chance to cause Starrick some pain, well you can charge into this theatre and kill me yourself.

speaker: Jacob
en: What do YOU get out of all this?

speaker: Roth
en: The chance to have a little fun with the bravest man in London!

speaker: Jacob
en: You have a deal.

speaker: Roth
en: Lewis! My carriage! Shall we?

speaker: Roth
en: This way! Well, you don't expect me to go alone, do you? Take the reins.

speaker: Roth
en: Driver! To St. Pancras! And don't spare the horses.

speaker: Jacob
en: I thought you and Starrick would be fighting for the same ends. What happened?

speaker: Roth
en: Oh, you know. He required my services to train his gang leaders. But the man is dreadful.

speaker: Jacob
en: You don't say.

speaker: Roth
en: Freedom, Jacob. Stealing that is far more than a sin. It denies us our humanity.

speaker: Jacob
en: Right you are. And St. Pancras will ease our suffering?

speaker: Roth
en: The station contains a large shipment of explosives to be dispatched to Starrick & Co.

speaker: Jacob
en: And you intend to steal it?

speaker: Roth
en: What? No. I intend to blow it up!

speaker: Roth
en: There's a train parked inside St. Pancras.

speaker: Jacob
en: Then I am to do away with Starrick's merchandise, leaving chaos in my wake.

speaker: Roth
en: Why not, Jacob? Why not? As we speak, the up train is headed towards us. That may help you enter the station unseen.

speaker: Jacob
en: As long as it remains on the tracks.

speaker: Roth
en: I'd say good luck, but you don't need it. I shall make certain any reinforcements from Starrick are kept away from the station.

speaker: Blighter 1
en: Alright, let's load her up, boyos. Careful with those. We don't want any broken bones tonight. Watch nothing spills. Finally, we can take out those bloody Frye twins. Get a move on! We haven't got much time to get this shipment sorted.

speaker: Jacob
en: Someday, you Blighters will understand that I'm doing this for your own good. Two down. Be a shame to stop now... One shipment left... Now to find somebody to drive this hunk of metal...

speaker: Driver
en: Oi! Get your bleedin' hands off me! What d'you think you're up to?!

speaker: Jacob
en: Hush, now. Please. Do be quiet, sir. No need to make a fuss.

speaker: Driver
en: What do you want from me?

speaker: Jacob
en: I just need you to keep the engine stoked.

speaker: Driver
en: All right! I'll help you! Don't hurt me!

speaker: Jacob
en: Think of me as another passenger. I just happen to have a rather large blade pointed at your back.

speaker: Blighter 2
en: Mr. Starrick won't be happy.

speaker: Jacob
en: Would you be so kind as to get up some steam?

speaker: Roth
en: Splendid! Starrick will be on his knees in no time. My hat is off to you.

speaker: Roth
en: Apologies, I must run. Do come see me again.

speaker: Nightingale
en: The unspeakable has happened! A policeman arrested Mr. Darwin and carried him away as if he were nothing but a common criminal! That policeman... He is corrupt to the bones, I'm sure of it... Oh, I do so fear for Mr. Darwin's safety.

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: Miss Nightingale, do you know where they might have gone?

speaker: Nightingale
en: The policeman... He did mention a funeral. I believe I know where it is... Follow me. Poor Mr. Darwin has been through so much recently. Those people are trying to discredit a lifetime of work. It's disgraceful! And I fear Mr. Darwin is no longer the fit, young man who the world. Here we are. The obsequies are taking place here. Better hurry now. You can find me here afterwards. Go on. I will be waiting here. I will wait here.

speaker: Policeman
en: Oi! What are you doing?! Is this honestly what it feels like when I arrest someone? What do you want from me? There's no need for such brutality!

speaker: Jacob
en: Just need you to answer some questions.

speaker: Evie
en: I need you to be honest with a friend of mine.

speaker: Policeman
en: You're a brash one, aren't you?

speaker: Jacob
en: It's been said.

speaker: Evie
en: Desperate times call for desperate measures.

speaker: Nightingale
en: This is the culprit.

speaker: Policeman
en: I was just carrying out my orders.

speaker: Nightingale
en: Arresting an old man and dragging him off to Lord-knows-where is fine work, indeed, for a policeman. Now, sir, tell us where you have taken Mr. Darwin.

speaker: Policeman
en: A man paid me to bring him to his secret base.

speaker: Nightingale
en: How terrible!

speaker: Nightingale
en: We will need transportation.

speaker: Nightingale
en: Now, let us find Mr. Darwin, shall we?

speaker: Jacob
en: I don't think that's a

speaker: Evie
en: With all due respect, I think

speaker: Nightingale
en: Shall we?

speaker: Nightingale
en: He is very weak... We shouldn't move Mr. Darwin until I have seen to his wounds.

speaker: Templar 1
en: They're here! Attack!

speaker: Nightingale
en: Mr. Darwin's condition is stable. You may move him now.

speaker: Templar 2
en: Oh... Were you going somewhere, Assassin?

speaker: Jacob
en: Rest up, Mr. Darwin. My sister and I will be along shortly.

speaker: Evie
en: Please look after him, Miss Nightingale. My brother and I will visit soon.

speaker: Darwin
en: Well, look who's here!

speaker: Evie
en: We were very worried about you, sir.

speaker: Jacob
en: You're looking spry for a fossil, sir.

speaker: Darwin
en: A man's friends are the best measure of his worth. I'm proud to count you among mine.

speaker: Evie
en: The danger's passed, there's no need to leave, sir.

speaker: Nightingale
en: What Mr. Darwin needs now is rest. To that end, he is joining his family on the Isle of Wight.

speaker: Darwin
en: Rest? Indeed! I shall start work on my next book!

speaker: Nightingale
en: I must insist that you recuperate quietly, sir.

speaker: Darwin
en: The acquisition of knowledge is in itself sufficiently recuperative. Go, tell her.

speaker: Jacob
en: This is one fight I aim to avoid, sir.

speaker: Darwin
en: Thank you for everything, my friends. Ideas, like people, can only thrive when they are free.

speaker: Attaway
en: Jacob, darling! Do join me!

speaker: Jacob
en: To our fruitful partnership.

speaker: Attaway
en: And to the shiny new engines now in my possession!

speaker: Attaway
en: Back to business. Millner's fled to the Thames - occupied with securing his ferry. It's all he has left.

speaker: Jacob
en: Hm, protecting it with his life, no doubt.

speaker: Attaway
en: The very thing I want you to take. Just kill him!

speaker: Jacob
en: That's not your first glass of champagne, is it?

speaker: Attaway
en: Success is more intoxicating than alcohol, Mr. Frye.

speaker: Jacob
en: Then save a glass for me.

speaker: Jacob
en: Now to sink Millner's enterprise.

speaker: Millner
en: What the bloody hell?!

speaker: Millner
en: You were supposed to watch over them! What do I pay you oafs for?!

speaker: Millner
en: I knew this day would come... Mr. Starrick was furious I lost the engines. So this is my comeuppance...

speaker: Jacob
en: Pearl Attaway led me to you, not Starrick.

speaker: Millner
en: Then they're working together again. I should never have come between Mr. Starrick and Miss Attaway. Family always stay together in the end.

speaker: Jacob
en: What do you mean, they're family?

speaker: Jacob
en: Time for Pearl and I to have a real conversation.

speaker: Jacob
en: There you are. What are you up to now, Pearl?

speaker: Attaway
en: I was certain he knew that I belonged to the Order and was there to end me. Imagine my delight when he told me his true purpose. An Assassin helping the Templar cause! Isn't that delicious?

speaker: Starrick
en: It's sickening.

speaker: Attaway
en: It's business, cousin. Look at the big picture. With Millner gone, I own the only omnibus company left in London. We already have a monopoly English transportation; the moment your engines power my buses, we will be legends!

speaker: Starrick
en: That was my plan from the start, with Millner. You forced my hand with your clever little train robbery.

speaker: Attaway
en: Crawford, I thought a reconciliation was in order. Do you have no happy memories of our childhood? Summers in ? You and I, down by the brook...

speaker: Starrick
en: This is a formal meeting, Pearl. Your sentimentality is unbecoming.

speaker: Attaway
en: Unbecoming?! I've had to hear that odious word dribble from men's lips all my life. Refusing to marry is unbecoming. Refusing to allow a man to conduct my affairs is unbecoming. How unfortunate that I didn't accept your hand in marriage all those years ago. How easy things would be for you now. The omnibuses would be yours by right and I would be at home, acting as hostess to your guests instead of standing here being so... unbecoming!

speaker: Starrick
en: It always ends this way with you, Pearl. I wish it were not so.

speaker: Attaway
en: You glower too much, cousin. You will get your engines back. Our new motorized buses will bring us both a lot of money.

speaker: Starrick
en: I'll need to arrange proper transport for the engines to get back to my factory. I want you at Waterloo, personally, to ensure that nothing goes wrong.

speaker: Attaway
en: Of course. May the Father of Understanding guide us.

speaker: Starrick
en: Today and in all of our future endeavors, cousin.

speaker: Jacob
en: Waterloo station.

speaker: Blighter 1
en: Door's jammed.

speaker: Blighter 2
en: Again? Just give it a shove!

speaker: Duke
en: What do you think you're doing?! Get away from me!

speaker: Jacob
en: Hush. Quiet, Miss Duke. There's time for talking later.

speaker: Duke
en: And what do the coppers want from me this time?

speaker: Jacob
en: How do you know I'm with the police?

speaker: Duke
en: With all the tactics they've tried, nothing surprises me anymore. They want me for the countless crimes I've committed, but they never hold me for long.

speaker: Jacob
en: We'll see this time around.

speaker: Duke
en: What do you think you're doing?! Get away from me!

speaker: Evie
en: Now, Miss Duke, no need to fuss. Some quiet would be much appreciated.

speaker: Duke
en: I know Abberline sent you. He's been on my trail for a while.

speaker: Evie
en: Half my work here is done.

speaker: Duke
en: He won't keep me long, you know? I've been in and out of prisons more times than you can count. You can't keep me fenced in!

speaker: Evie
en: We'll see about that.

speaker: Duke
en: Aye, piss off! Get this idiot off my back! Some wench is chasing me down! A bit of help would be nice!

speaker: Duke
en: Oh, for crying out loud!

speaker: Jacob
en: Come now, Miss Duke. Enough of this nonsense.

speaker: Duke
en: I said, piss off!

speaker: Evie
en: Calm down, Miss Duke. There's business I need you to attend to.

speaker: Duke
en: Let me out! Get me out of here!

speaker: Abberline
en: Feisty one, she is.

speaker: Dickens
en: Thank goodness you're here! Impossible as it may sound, Spring Heeled Jack has returned! We need to do something before the unthinkable happens!

speaker: Jacob
en: I thought we'd already dealt with this nonsense.

speaker: Evie
en: He did say that we had not seen the last of the Spring-heeled villain...

speaker: Dickens
en: There may be more to this than we originally thought.

speaker: Victim
en: Get away from me you monster!

speaker: Jacob
en: You there! Stop what you're doing.

speaker: Evie
en: Stop!

speaker: Jack
en: You'll have to do better than that! I am a ghost. A fiend! A terror in the night! I am a ghost! The falling of feet of a devil on the air. Long have I stalked the streets of London I am the terror of London! No weapon forged by man can harm me! No one is safe from my beastly claws. You can't hurt me!

speaker: Jacob
en: What? How? Where?

speaker: Evie
en: Vanished! Impossible!

speaker: Jack
en: Spring Heeled Jack will never die!

speaker: Dickens
en: Thanks to you, the Ghost Club's reputation has grown tremendously! We are a beacon of reason in a world beguiled by superstition.

speaker: Evie
en: But I believe we have encountered one genuine spirit.

speaker: Dickens
en: Can you be certain? That's the question. One might surmise that the spirits that haunt us are simply our deepest fears, manifested as apparitions.

speaker: Jacob
en: Shame. I've always wanted to see a ghost. Or a goblin!

speaker: Dickens
en: I propose a toast! To the Ghost Club, and the virtuous twins that have aided it: Miss Evie and Mr. Jacob!

speaker: All
en: Cheers!

speaker: Josephine Fletcher
en: And what do we say afterwards?

speaker: Children
en: May the Father of Understanding guide us.

speaker: Josephine Fletcher
en: And who do you serve?

speaker: Children
en: The Grand Master.

speaker: Josephine Fletcher
en: Excellent! Run along now!

speaker: Francis Fletcher
en: Our plan is coming along splendidly, darling.

speaker: Josephine Fletcher
en: Where's our next recruitment, dearest?

speaker: Francis Fletcher
en: Charing Cross. No one looks for tourists' missing children.

speaker: Josephine Fletcher
en: We'll have an army for the Grand Master in no time.

speaker: Kent
en: Where've you been? I've been minding the docks for hours without a word from you.

speaker: Raphael
en: Miss Swinebourne dropped by for a quick about.

speaker: Kent
en: And you didn't think to tell me?

speaker: Raphael
en: It wasn't urgent.

speaker: Kent
en: Like hell it wasn't! It's not every day Miss Edith drops in for a cup of tea. We are in this together! This trading business is ours, not yours.

speaker: Raphael
en: Brother, please, I understand. She merely dropped by to thanks us for our efforts.

speaker: Kent
en: What?

speaker: Raphael
en: Thanks to us the Blighters are now fully equipped. She says our loyalty will not be forgotten.

speaker: Kent
en: Is that it then?

speaker: Raphael
en: And she kissed me! Right on my forehead!

speaker: Kent
en: What? Then I deserve one too!

speaker: Hiding civilian
en: I'm in trouble now, only God knows who's on the menu tonight. Oh God! I hope they don't notice me.

speaker: Ada
en: People sneer at the street cleaners but they have no idea how better things are because of us.

speaker: Clyde
en: Those dreaded turncoats are the next to go.

speaker: Ada
en: We'll feast on those Rooks tonight.

speaker: Ada
en: Tonight is the night of the full moon.

speaker: Clyde
en: Another hunt is on the rise, who should we target this time, Ada?

speaker: Ada
en: The order from Strain is that we go after the Rooks.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: I have spoken with Octavia. She requests that those willing to take up arms against the Rooks report to me for reassignment immediately. You Blighters make me proud. We will take those Rooks down, one by one if we have to. Those Rooks are little more than a nuisance. They are as powerful as they are pretty, which is to say not very.

speaker: Big Pete
en: Another brew, and two for Charlie

speaker: Charlie
en: You're too kind, you ugly bastard.

speaker: Big Pete
en: Your performance today was staggering, dear sister.

speaker: Charlie
en: I'm at my best when they struggle.

speaker: Big Pete
en: We need to thread lightly, for the next month maybe.

speaker: Charlie
en: We can't risk losing our supply.

speaker: Big Pete
en: If they find out I've been letting you lot in, I'll get sacked from the zoo.

speaker: Charlie
en: And that won't be the worst of it, either...

speaker: Blackroot
en: Lovely day, is it not, my beauties? Lovely, lovely day.

speaker: Blackroot
en: What a glorious shade of red.

speaker: Blackroot
en: Who knew such special ingredients could bring life so much joy?

speaker: Blackroot
en: You're hungry, aren't you? I'll make sure you're well fed tonight.

speaker: Evie
en: What is this place?

speaker: Clara
en: It's nice to meet you both at last. This is Babylon Alley. Here, we make it our business to know the streets, and provide children with the opportunity to control their own destinies.

speaker: Evie
en: Clara. Mister Green said we might be able to help one another?

speaker: Clara
en: In exchange for our services, we ask a small favor.

speaker: Jacob
en: Well, why not? You seem to have taken most of my money. Why not take a small favor, too?

speaker: Clara
en: There are several factories about the city that are powered almost entirely by child labor. Those children work long hours, with little pay, and most are not permitted even to leave the factory grounds. They suffer terribly. I need you to save them.

speaker: Jacob
en: A small favor?

speaker: Clara
en: In return, we offer you intelligence. Something YOU clearly need.

speaker: Jacob
en: Now hold on a minute

speaker: Clara
en: I'm late for an appointment. What of these terms?

speaker: Evie
en: We accept.

speaker: Clara
en: Pleasure doing business with you.

speaker: Tom Eccleston
en: was a virtual representation of one of Jacob Frye and Evie Frye's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Roth
en: Jacob! He is beautiful, isn't he? I've planned the perfect second outing for us!

speaker: Jacob
en: Have you?

speaker: Roth
en: There's borrowing to be done. Three of Starrick's henchmen are about to disappear.

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, you sly devil.

speaker: Roth
en: Oh! And I'm coming along this time. There is no sense in giving you all the glory. Off to my carriage we go! Lewis!

speaker: Roth
en: Jacob! Our carriage awaits! You know how it is. You drive. Let us away.

speaker: Roth
en: These cowardly fools under Starrick have built their own prisons. It's a dreadful waste.

speaker: Jacob
en: They could be building gangs instead?

speaker: Roth
en: No, no! Why build, when you can ebb and flow like the sea? I would not deign to pin them down.

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, you wouldn't, would you? What about your bird?

speaker: Roth
en: It's not building anything. It just is, my dear.

speaker: Roth
en: I dare say I shall never tire of the National Gallery.

speaker: Jacob
en: Why does Starrick interest himself with art?

speaker: Roth
en: He's hired a fiendishly talented woman, one Hattie Cadwallader, to procure works for him. She has excellent taste.

speaker: Jacob
en: We're kidnapping her for the sin of being Starrick's collector?

speaker: Roth
en: Oh my dear, no. We are kidnapping her, not because she loves art, but because she finances Starrick's enterprises by selling it. One must never mix art and money.

speaker: Jacob
en: Wait for me with the carriage. I'll pay her a visit.

speaker: Roth
en: Splendid. Be careful, my dear. When a deal falls through, Miss Cadwallader tends to poison future sales.

speaker: Jacob
en: Bring your carriage around and wait for the cargo. I shan't be very long.

speaker: Jacob
en: Someone around here must know Miss Hattie Cadwallader...

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm looking for Miss Hattie Cadwallader.

speaker: Girl
en: Ain't seen her... I knows what she's been up to, though.

speaker: Jacob
en: And what's that?

speaker: Girl
en: Prigging (stealing) art, sir. She pinched a statue not far from here.

speaker: Jacob
en: The statue must be around here somewhere. Now where is that statue...

speaker: Jacob
en: Hey, smallie! Know anything about what happened here?

speaker: Boy
en: I saw who pinched it, sir.

speaker: Jacob
en: Miss Cadwallader?

speaker: Boy
en: She hides down the sewers, sir.

speaker: Jacob
en: Of course it's sewers. Why the bloody sewers?

speaker: Cadwallader
en: Tell Mr. Starrick his next delivery is on its way. And tell him too that I'm growing tired of these working conditions.

speaker: Jacob
en: Wasn't Starrick who sent me.

speaker: Cadwallader
en: Then who?

speaker: Jacob
en: Maxwell Roth sends his regards.

speaker: Cadwallader
en: Oi! Leave off, or you'll be sorry! Take your hands off me, sir, or you'll be sorry! What do you want?

speaker: Jacob
en: Shh... Hush, madam. We're fast friends now, aren't we? Not a peep from you. Don't call for help.

speaker: Roth
en: Why, Miss Cadwallader! What a pleasant surprise!

speaker: Cadwallader
en: You'll be hearing from Mr. Starrick, Roth!

speaker: Roth
en: Ha! I look forward to it!

speaker: Jacob
en: Why the Alhambra?

speaker: Roth
en: Every good criminal needs a place to invest his ill-gotten gains. And what's better than distracting the world with a little light entertainment while you do so?

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, come now. You can't tell me you don't enjoy the triumph of a well-received play? The plaudits and praise? The reviews?

speaker: Roth
en: I enjoy being entertained, Jacob! If one the productions pleases me, I am over the moon. The theatre is in my blood. As you so astutely discerned, theatricality is... something of a Roth specialty.

speaker: Roth
en: Ah, the park. The dwelling place of Starrick's head of security, one Benjamin Raffles. Those who cross him tend to disappear without warning.

speaker: Jacob
en: Sounds like we'll be fast friends.

speaker: Roth
en: Be careful. His guards are never far away.

speaker: Raffles
en: What the meaning o' this?! Did Roth send you? The villain!

speaker: Jacob
en: You have your villains mixed up, Mr. Raffles. The man you work for is the real villain here.

speaker: Raffles
en: Let. Me. Go! Guards!

speaker: Jacob
en: Keep your voice down. Quiet, Mr. Raffles. Hush now.

speaker: Roth
en: My most fragrant Raffles! How very good to see you again!

speaker: Raffles
en: Go to hell, Roth!

speaker: Roth
en: It's into the back with you, then.

speaker: Jacob
en: Who is this Lewis that works for you?

speaker: Roth
en: Ha! A bit of an odd fish, isn't he? Came to me a few years past.

speaker: Jacob
en: He's very solemn.

speaker: Roth
en: But always so polite! And he has many other talents.

speaker: Jacob
en: Who am I looking for?

speaker: Roth
en: Chester Swinebourne. A copper by day and snitch by night. Remove him from the pack and you cut Starrick's ties to the police force.

speaker: Jacob
en: Must be good at what he does to keep the charade going for so long.

speaker: Roth
en: He is indeed, dear boy.

speaker: Jacob
en: All these bobbies give me gooseflesh.

speaker: Roth
en: Welcome to Scotland Yard.

speaker: Swinebourne
en: Huh?! What?!

speaker: Jacob
en: Now, now, Swinebourne. Let's not make a scene.

speaker: Swinebourne
en: You're not going to get away with this!

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, but I am.

speaker: Swinebourne
en: Where are you taking me?

speaker: Jacob
en: A friend would like to say a quick how d'ye do.

speaker: Swinebourne
en: Cease and desist!

speaker: Jacob
en: Hush! Quiet, please.

speaker: Roth
en: Chester!

speaker: Swinebourne
en: Roth? It's been a while.

speaker: Roth
en: You've really let yourself go. Shame. Now, it's into the back with you!

speaker: Roth
en: Excellent work. Do come find me at the Alhambra. I have more amusements planned for us!

speaker: Blighter 1
en: Keep a sharp eye out, lads. Someone's targeting our network. The distillery might be next.

speaker: Jacob
en: This will complicate things.

speaker: Blighter 2
en: Have you tried it? The Syrup, I mean?

speaker: Blighter 3
en: Are you daft?

speaker: Blighter 2
en: You don't know what you're missing.

speaker: Blighter 3
en: That poison'll kill ya.

speaker: Blighter 3
en: I think I'll have a taste.

speaker: Blighter 4
en: That's against the rules. You like your job, don't ya?

speaker: Blighter 3
en: I can't say I'm particularly fond of it, no.

speaker: Blighter 4
en: Shit, you had Syrup. I can tell!

speaker: Blighter 3
en: Just a nip, love.

speaker: Blighter 4
en: We have strict orders not to do that!

speaker: Blighter 3
en: Ah, no harm done.

speaker: Darwin
en: You should not go about frightening respectable gentlemen, young man.

speaker: Jacob
en: I didn't realize snooping around was considered gentlemanly.

speaker: Darwin
en: Snooping? Sir, I assure you

speaker: Blighter 2
en: Keep vigilant!

speaker: Jacob
en: Quick! Inside.

speaker: Darwin
en: That was too close a call. You, young man, gave me quite a fright! I thought you were one of them, but I realize now why you're here. Same reason I am, I imagine...

speaker: Jacob
en: "I imagine"?

speaker: Darwin
en: You should see this.

speaker: Darwin
en: A rather impressive contraption, wouldn't you say?

speaker: Jacob
en: I've seen bigger.

speaker: Darwin
en: Datura stramonium. Or Devil's snare, as it is commonly called... That goes into the Syrup? And opium, no less. Revolting! Absolutely sickening!

speaker: Darwin
en: A favorable way to proceed, wouldn't you agree?

speaker: Marx
en: Workers, Comrades. Thank you for your most generous welcome. I come before you today with a heavy heart. England stands at the head of commercial and industrial Europe. In the last two decades there has been an unheard of development of industry and unprecedented increase in exports and imports. While these are facts to be celebrated by the provident classes, for the workers very little has changed. You well know under what conditions of shattered health, damaged morals and spiritual ruin this increase of wealth and power was produced for the upper classes, by the working class. It has become a truce that no perfecting of machinery, no application of science to industry, no improvement on the means of communication, no new colonies, no immigration, no opening out of new markets, no free trade and not all these things put together can do away with the misery of the toiling masses. But rather, on the contrary, that upon the present false basis, every new development of the productive power of labour must lead to the widening of the gap between the classes and to the heightening of social antagonisms. During this epoch of economic progress, death from starvation has raised itself almost to the rank of a social institution, here in London, the capital of the British Empire. In the annals of world history, this age will be characterized by the more impetuous force, the more expanded range and the deadlier effects of the social plague known as the commercial and industrial crisis. I believe that it is not necessary that the means of labour should be monopolized as a means of dominating the workers and exploiting them. That just like slavery and serfdom, so also wage labour is only a transitory subordinate social form, which is destined to vanish before associated labour, which will accomplish its work with willing hands, vigorous mind and cheerful heart. It has been said that the is a House of Landlords. I put it to you today, that to capture political power is now the great duty of the working class! We must attempt the political reorganization of the workers if we are to improve their lot. The workers must go forward in a united fashion, with the simultaneous demand that the simple laws of morality and justice, which are considered right in the relations of private persons, shall be recognized as the supreme law governing labour in this country! The struggle for such a policy is embraced in the universal struggle for the emancipation of the working class. And so I say to you, proletarians of all lands, unite! In order to free the workers, the cooperative system of labour requires to develop on a national scale. And following from that, must be furthered by national means. For their part, the lords of the land and the lords of capital will continue steadily to use their political privileges for the defense and perpetuation of their monopoly. Instead of furthering the emancipation of the workers, they will act so as to bring every possible obstacle in the way.

You shall be sorely disappointed if you think you shall profit from this. Why are you doing this? Can you not say anything? I demand you explain yourself at once!

speaker: Jacob
en: I promise I won't hurt you! I'm abducting you for a friend! No, that still sounds terrible.

speaker: Evie
en: I knew this was a bad idea. I can't believe I agreed to this nonsense! I have a good reason for doing this! I hope.

speaker: Bella
en: Help! This brute has abducted me!250px|thumb|Hammon announcing himself

speaker: Hammon
en: Unhand her, ruffian! I shall save you, madam! For I am John Hammon, your fiance!

speaker: Bella
en: ...what?

speaker: Hammon
en: En garde!

speaker: Hammon
en: Take this, you rogue! Take your punishment! Ha! Clearly I am your better. I say, this is getting a little too real! I say, you're not actually trying to kill me are you? This has gone too far. Please stop!

speaker: Bella
en: This is all rather suspicious. Will someone explain what is happening? What? A ruse! I suspected as much from the beginning!

speaker: Bella
en: What a happy coincidence that you were here to save me.

speaker: Hammon
en: Wasn't it? And if you will allow me, my dearest Bella, I shall forever be by your side to protect you from this day forth. Come, my dear. Let us be gone from this terrible place and I shall explain all.

speaker: Jacob
en: I should return to Charlie and Charlie to tell them the happy news.

speaker: Evie
en: I'm certain Mister Dickens and Mister Darwin would like to know of their friend's good fortune.

speaker: Dickens
en: And so all's well that ends well! Our young lovers are united at last and will soon marry.

speaker: Jacob
en: No accounting for taste, I suppose.

speaker: Evie
en: I, too, hope to meet a man who will fake his own death and arrange my abduction just to see if I can be trusted.

speaker: Darwin
en: And by the looks of you they really "hit it off"! Ha, ha!

speaker: Dickens
en: I must say it's all rather exciting. I do love these sorts of tales.

speaker: Darwin
en: It all feels strangely familiar. I wonder why? We should drink to John Hammon and his unconventional idea of courtship!

speaker: Dickens
en: Indeed! To John Hammon! Our mutual friend!

speaker: Abberline
en: Miss Frye.

speaker: Evie
en: Inspector Abberline. Why exactly have you had me escorted here?

speaker: Abberline
en: My men and I have been hunting the Ripper 'round the clock for months now, and we've nothing to show for it... At least nothing I can tell the public.

speaker: Evie
en: What has the 'Ripper' to do with me? My brother has had me summoned here from India—can't this wait?

speaker: Abberline
en: As far as I know, you may be the last Assassin in London...

speaker: Evie
en: What do you mean? Where is Jacob?

speaker: Abberline
en: I wish I knew... Your brother is nowhere to be found even as an elusive shadow is committing the most hideous crimes this city has ever seen.

speaker: Evie
en: And you believe this is no coincidence.

speaker: Abberline
en: The killer is selective and dispassionate, and has left not a single trace of his passage. I have seen such talent for assassination and avoiding detection only once before... When I worked with the two of you. And that is why your brother summoned you, before he disappeared...

speaker: Evie
en: You think Jacob is dead.

speaker: Abberline
en: I dare not believe it. But if he is, you may be the only person who can stop the Ripper now. Follow me.

speaker: Abberline
en: I'll take you to the site where the Ripper first struck... The journalists always seem to get the word first—we get there, they've trampled the evidence, and next day's headlines are dripping with blood. The few hundred yards between Flower and Dean Street have become so dangerous that even my best constables are afraid to patrol Whitechapel at night. Let's take a carriage, shall we? I'd rather not get egg on my face again today.

speaker: Evie
en: I'll drive.

speaker: Evie
en: What has become of this borough?

speaker: Abberline
en: Whitechapel is a cesspool of crime, Miss Frye, where terror reigns supreme. Elsewhere, the rich get richer, but here, the poor are living on the living, fighting to survive each day... Reporters share a view of Whitechapel as a lair of savages, monsters, and werewolves who hold honest citizens in a state of terror...

speaker: Evie
en: The Ripper's terror.

speaker: Abberline
en: We are not far from where Mary Ann Nichols was murdered. I knew her as Polly, that's what her friends called her. But the woman who died here is not the woman I met a few times at the Frying Pan pub...

speaker: Evie
en: Then who was she?

speaker: Abberline
en: I was hoping you could tell me. Go see for yourself.

speaker: Evie
en: This is where 'the Ripper' committed his first murder. Was Miss Nichols' body identified?

speaker: Abberline
en: Her husband hadn't seen her in 11 years; he barely glanced at the poor, mutilated woman before he had the gall to 'forgive her for what she'd done to him'. The press reported widely that Miss Nichol's finger bore the mark of a ring. It was forcibly removed, and the same is true for his other victims...

speaker: Abberline
en: What did you discover?

speaker: Evie
en: Give me a moment.

speaker: Evie
en: I found Miss Nichols' ring. An Assassin's ring... She must have tossed it away during the struggle—a desperate act to protect the Brotherhood. You think they were targeted.

speaker: Abberline
en: Yes. And the newspapers are accusing the police—me—of letting 'the first city of the world lapse into primeval savagery'. I must take my leave, Miss Frye. I have other business in Whitechapel.

speaker: Evie
en: Good day, Inspector. Thank you for your discretion.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Mister Strain has written to our stronghold with words of encouragement: "To my most favoured Blighters. We're not daft enough to remain ignorant of the threat that these so-called Rooks pose on our territory. I urge you to clip their wings but keep their brains intact for my own enjoyment. I will be in touch. Cletus." There you have it! Keep a close eye on your surroundings, they're a sneaky bunch.

speaker: Gribble
en: Better suited than I? Pff. Who's better suited than Miss Beatrice Gribble? Who? I've good blood in my veins, royal ancestry in Spain and no one bats an eyelash. I'll shred them to pieces and then we'll see who's worthy of serving the Queen. Do they know how hard I worked to get where I am today? What have they done? Nothing! In their entire existence, those rich women have done nothing! And yet they believe themselves entitled to everything.

speaker: Darwin
en: , commonly known as "Harlequin Blueflag". ... ... ... ... Ah... Er... Oh, what is it called again... erm... ! There it is!

speaker: Darwin
en: I didn't know you had a twin sister, Mr. Frye.

speaker: Evie
en: Evie Frye, sir. It's a pleasure.

speaker: Darwin
en: Usually, I would reciprocate the sentiment, Miss Frye, but today I am afraid nothing will bring me pleasure.

speaker: Evie
en: What's troubling you, sir?

speaker: Darwin
en: I am used to people challenging my ideas, in fact, I live for it... The cut and thrust of spirited debate! Lately, however, attacks against my reputation have taken a darker turn. Threats of violence against my person and against my colleagues. I do not wish anyone to be hurt because of my research...

speaker: Jacob
en: You helped me with Starrick's Syrup. I am in your debt.

speaker: Darwin
en: We help each other, sir.

speaker: Evie
en: My brother and I will make sure that you can continue your work in peace.

speaker: Darwin
en: What do you know of bones?

speaker: Jacob
en: I know how much pressure it takes to shatter, snap, or splinter one.

speaker: Evie
en: Only a few of their names, learned from books.

speaker: Darwin
en: Mmm... Perhaps it would be simpler if I just explained the situation... A few days ago, a German colleague, Dr. Schwartz, sent me a telegram. He informed me he was on his way to London to deliver a fossil, you see. In fact, he should arrive at Charing Cross any moment now. Would you ensure no harm comes to him?

speaker: Jacob
en: I'll bring Dr. Schwartz and that fossil to you, Mr. Darwin.

speaker: Evie
en: I'll ensure Dr. Schwartz's safety and makes sure you get that fossil.

speaker: Darwin
en: Splendid! But please do be careful... Do hurry to Charing Cross, please. Please hurry. I fear Dr. Schwartz might be in danger. You'll find Dr. Schwartz at Charing Cross Station.

speaker: Schwartz
en: What is the meaning of this?

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm collecting you and your precious cargo for our friend, Mr. Darwin. Just act naturally.

speaker: Evie
en: Mr. Darwin has sent me to ensure you reach him safely, with your cargo intact. Just act naturally.

speaker: Schwartz
