en: Right... So how is your father? By which I mean my dear brother Franck, with whom I grew up, of course. Oh, splendid! Wonderful to hear. I'll do my best not to call attention to how remiss he was in forgetting to warn me about the delicate situation which brings me here today.

speaker: Blighter 1
en: Wouldn't hurt to know what the bugger looks like.

speaker: Blighter 2
en: How am I going to find him among all these people?

speaker: Blighter 3
en: Like finding a needle in a haystack, this is.

speaker: Blighter 4
en: What's a German doctor supposed to look like anyway?

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: Doctor Schwartz?

speaker: Schwartz
en: ... never got on the train. Darwin's fate is sealed! Goodbye, Assassin. I did so enjoy meeting you.

speaker: Imposter
en: Darwin must be silenced! will destroy the very fabric of our society! Do you not see how dangerous Darwin's theories are?! We cannot allow Darwin to destroy what we have built!

speaker: Jacob
en: Where do you think you're going?! Stop, and I might let you live. I'll run you off the road! Your choice, imposter: we do this the hard way, or we do it the very hard way!

speaker: Evie
en: Stop and hand over the specimen. Now! Don't force me to kill you! Don't make me do anything you'll regret! You can't escape! You must realize that!

speaker: Jacob
en: Now to take this fossil to Darwin.

speaker: Evie
en: I should deliver this to Mr. Darwin.

speaker: Darwin
en: At last! My heart hasn't stopped pounding. You have it? Wonderful? But... where is Dr. Schwartz?

speaker: Jacob
en: Most likely dead, I'm afraid. He never left Germany. At least I managed to get the fossil back.

speaker: Evie
en: I'm afraid he was intercepted, sir, in Germany. However, I have recovered the fossil.

speaker: Darwin
en: Dear Lord... I should tell you I was recently approached by men who sought to purchase all my research, on the condition I work only for them. Obviously, I refused. Scientific knowledge cannot be bought, it belongs to everyone. Let these villains do their worst!

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Bloody Nora asked us to keep a close eye on activity here in the City of London. Says there's a rebel group rising up in Whitechapel.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: The Blighters are more than just a bunch of rebels. We are a well-thought through organization, a family. These Rooks will never understand that concept.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: We need to show the other boroughs what it means to be a true Blighter. We must take out those Rooks and make them sorry they ever crossed us.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: We bow our heads for our fallen brothers and sisters but this fight is far from over, we will crush those Rooks under our feet and march our way back to city wide domination.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Miss Graves will show them the meaning of brutality. This borough belongs to us. To the Blighters!

speaker: Bell
en: Argh! Oh, Jacob, Evie, it's you. Thank goodness.

speaker: Evie
en: Experimenting, are we, Aleck?

speaker: Bell
en: Correct.

speaker: Jacob
en: And looking a bit frazzled.

speaker: Bell
en: Nerves. It's those great oafs Starrick keeps sending 'round to coax me. He is offering a ridiculous amount of money.

speaker: Jacob
en: Aleck, you're not thinking of jumping ship, are you?

speaker: Bell
en: Never! I've been working on something in case they get too insistent. It's meant to stun an assailant, should the need arise.

speaker: Evie
en: Are you certain that it works?

speaker: Bell
en: Not as such. I've made three of them with varying degrees of acidity and whatnot. One must be the right formula.

speaker: Jacob
en: Let's find some Starrick lackeys to target then, shall we?

speaker: Bell
en: Speaking of Starrick, he is still transmitting false information.

speaker: Evie
en: We could simply destroy his transmitters...

speaker: Bell
en: His company's too well guarded. The bombs will help, but it would be awkward to produce bombs that potentially do not stun...

speaker: Bell
en: Oh- Wait a minute, looks like opportunity has come knocking. Oh, dear. They never looked so angry before.

speaker: Jacob
en: Stand clear, Aleck.

speaker: Bell
en: Let us instead play a little linguistic game with them. Um, take the bombs and climb onto the roof. When I say the name of a-a fruit, toss one near the thugs.

speaker: Evie
en: Right, then.

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, uh, wait! Uh, I nearly forgot...

speaker: Bell
en: Slip these into your boots and you will henceforth be immune to all voltaic discharge! I think.

speaker: Bell
en: Good day, gentlemen. Uh, I would ask you in for tea, but I'm afraid I'm running rather late...

speaker: Bill
en: Enough of the niceties. We've come to smash your place up, in't we, Baz?

speaker: Baz
en: You've got one of them tele-whatsit in there, ain't ya? And you've been reading messages from the Starrick Company?

speaker: Bell
en: That is as untrue as the notion that the Starrick Telegraph Company is emitting impartial information, sir.

speaker: Baz
en: Come again?

speaker: Bell
en: Your employer's promises are nothing but hot air. And his operations are about to turn... Pear-shaped!

speaker: Bill
en: Whatcha going on about air and pears for?

speaker: Baz
en: Aw, I don't alf feel rough...

speaker: Bill
en: That's disgusting... Uh!

speaker: Bill
en: Gawd blimey...

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, kids, eh! Those playful young scamps get everywhere...

speaker: Bill
en: Listen up, Bell, or I'll thump you till your ears are ringing.

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, a pun. Your wordplay delights me! And to think I worried you had the mental capacity of a dollop of donkey's apples.

speaker: Baz
en: Apples?

speaker: Bill
en: I think he's trying to be funny.

speaker: Baz
en: Pwah! You dropped another one, Bill, you little sod...

speaker: Bill
en: Ain't me, Baz. Gor blimey, it's got me froat...

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, those rascals throwing stink bombs again. It happens all the time around here.

speaker: Baz
en: Right, tell us where you keep that tele-whatsit. I'll count to three.

speaker: Bell
en: Three? Well, well, let's see how far you get!

speaker: Baz
en: One...

speaker: Bell
en: Do you really think I would keep it here? Do you see a cable? A telegraph without a cable is about as useful as a bell without a clapper.

speaker: Baz
en: I'll give you a bleedin' clapper!

speaker: Bell
en: Well, bless my boots, you're as purple as... a plum!

speaker: Baz
en: A plum?

speaker: Jacob
en: Bravo, Aleck!

speaker: Bell
en: Thanks to you, Jacob. Your mere presence gave me courage and resolve I never knew I had. I found myself rather witty, too.

speaker: Jacob
en: Well... make some more bombs and let's sort out Starrick's propaganda machine, shall we?

speaker: Evie
en: Good show, Aleck!

speaker: Bell
en: Thanks to you, Evie. Your mere presence gave me courage and resolve I never knew I had.

speaker: Evie
en: I'm glad I could help. Now it's time to shut down Starrick's Empire of Propaganda.

speaker: Bell
en: Come on, we haven't got all day!

speaker: Bell
en: The longer we can keep Starrick from spewing out false information, the more we can awaken the people with the truth about his operations.

speaker: Jacob
en: Let's get to it, then.

speaker: Bell
en: Would you believe, my mother says there are still some wives in her street that swear by that Soothing Syrup. So I took it upon myself to tell her neighbors the truth about the obnoxious draught.

speaker: Jacob
en: Good on you, Aleck, but you can't go knocking on everyone's door.

speaker: Bell
en: No... I wasn't always welcome... which shows how false information can be as difficult to stamp out as fishwives' profanities at .

speaker: Jacob
en: Or rats in the sewers.

speaker: Bell
en: But if we can eradicate the source that continually feeds such detrimental trash, then little by little, the truth will take the upper hand and the sham will be flushed out.

speaker: Jacob
en: Let's crack on, then. Here we are!

speaker: Bell
en: We will have to get in without being detected, mind.

speaker: Jacob
en: While I stun them, you sneak inside.

speaker: Bell
en: I shall destroy not one, but three parts of the transmitter. He'll be as good as dancing before a public toilet without a penny!

speaker: Bell
en: The longer we can keep Starrick from spewing out false information, the more we can awaken the people with the truth about his operations.

speaker: Evie
en: I agree. The sooner we can get there, the quicker we can act.

speaker: Bell
en: Would you believe, my mother says there are still some wives in her street that swear by that Soothing Syrup. So I took it upon myself to tell her neighbors the truth about the obnoxious draught.

speaker: Evie
en: That's good, Aleck, but you can't go 'round to every household in London town.

speaker: Bell
en: No... I wasn't always welcome... which shows how false information can be as difficult to stamp out as fishwives' profanities at Billingsgate.

speaker: Evie
en: Or vermin at .

speaker: Bell
en: But if we can eradicate the source that continually feeds such detrimental trash, then little by little, the truth will take the upper hand and the sham will be flushed out.

speaker: Evie
en: That's why we're here.

speaker: Bell
en: We will have to get in without being detected, mind.

speaker: Evie
en: I shall stun them while you get inside.

speaker: Bell
en: I shall destroy not one, but three parts of the transmitter. He'll be as good as dancing before a public toilet without a penny!

speaker: Bell
en: What a beautiful machine. A pity, it's been soiled by corrupt minds! Oh, well. I hope the guards don't come patrolling.

speaker: Bell
en: I say, this is becoming rather perilous to say the least! Golly gosh, I felt that! Jolly close shave, that!

speaker: Bell
en: Ha! Got you, you little bugger! We'll have to cross over here.

speaker: Bell
en: A tad fiddly, that one, but I've pulled it as well as a dentist pulls a rotten tooth! There.

speaker: Jacob
en: Move on to the next part, Aleck.

speaker: Evie
en: Move faster, if you can.

speaker: Bell
en: My dears, Jacob, Evie, thanks are once again in order, for supporting what is most dear to me and to our cause. Freedom of speech.

speaker: Evie
en: It's a blessing that you employ your genius for the common good, Aleck.

speaker: Jacob
en: However, I suggest you vacate your workshop.

speaker: Bell
en: No need, not now, you've given me sacksful of courage. And, besides, what with my little devices, I have all the protection I need. Uh, should you find yourselves with a moment to spare, do drop by!

speaker: Evie
en: Those poor girls don't look free anymore.

speaker: Thug 1
en: Right, you tight slugs, shake a leg! First man puts a bullet in Miss Frye gets to spend a full hour wit' one a Lady O's 'beauties'...

speaker: Thug 2
en: You have no business here! Be gone before I kill these whores! I will kill these whores! I swears I will!

speaker: Evie
en: You're safe now.

speaker: Leader
en: EVIE FRYE! You have just signed your death warrant! FACE ME!

speaker: Nellie
en: Those thugs won't be beatin' us or stealin' our ha'pennies anymore... thanks to you, Miss Evie.

speaker: Bell
en: Ah, Jacob, Miss Frye! How good to see you. Oh, have you seen Starrick's latest lies?

speaker: Jacob
en: Lies in a newspaper?

speaker: Evie
en: What transpired from the new line you were establishing?

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, the cables we ordered never arrived. And then, we intercepted this. A message mentioning cargo seized at College Wharf.

speaker: Evie
en: Then let's unseize it.

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, uh, wait! Another intercepted wire contained the recipe for a powerful hallucinogenic serum. I've adapted this dart mechanism to work with your bracers.

speaker: Jacob
en: Aleck, you're a genius.

speaker: Bell
en: Well that, patently, is untrue. Although... I've also discovered that the serum adopts the form of a gas when subjected to heat.

speaker: Jacob
en: Just when I think you can't surpass yourself...

speaker: Blighter
en: There's trouble on the docks, lads! We need to get this load to Starrick now!

speaker: Jacob
en: Poison! Bell must know what kind.

speaker: Evie
en: Poison! I'm sure Mr. Bell will find this most interesting.

speaker: Evie
en: Careful there, Mr. Bell.

speaker: Bell
en: Every worthwhile endeavor is fraught with dangers, my dear friends. None more so than yours. But you have triumphed once again.

speaker: Jacob
en: How do you know?

speaker: Bell
en: We have entered the age of communication, remember. We've already received word from Greenwich that the shipment has arrived safely. Thanks to you.

speaker: Evie
en: Have you discovered what else is in that shipment?

speaker: Bell
en: Indeed. Um, I'm afraid that Starrick's poison has found its way on to the open market.

speaker: Evie
en: If he believes that will stop us, he is mistaken.

speaker: Hargrave
en: No exceptions, you hear? No documentation, no entrance to the port.

speaker: Dock Worker 1
en: Aye, aye captain!

speaker: Hargrave
en: This is an important job we have, can't just have any old riff raff coming into our ports. You don't see papers, you throw them overboard, and I don't want anyone swimming to shore.

speaker: Dock Worker 1
en: Yes, Sir.

speaker: Dock Worker 2
en: You think it's a bit harsh?

speaker: Dock Worker 3
en: Making 'em disappear? I suppose.

speaker: Dock Worker 2
en: There has to be a more civilized way of dealing with... outsiders.

speaker: Dock Worker 3
en: I don't think it's wise to question Captain Hargrave.

speaker: Dock Worker 2
en: He seems a bit different than usual, the Captain does.

speaker: Dock Worker 3
en: How so? I haven't noticed anything.

speaker: Dock Worker 2
en: Doesn't he seem younger to you at all? I don't think he's actually Captain Hargrave we've always worked for.

speaker: Dock Worker 3
en: You've gone loony, mate. Should I send for bedlam?

scene: The Case of the Conflicted Courtship
speaker: Arthur
en: A tragedy in the park!

scene: The Case of the Conflicted Courtship
speaker: Henry
en: Another chance to sort out a diabolical conundrum! One that I'll turn into a for Purlock Publishing!

speaker: Policeman 1
en: For the last time, move on, or else!

speaker: Marx
en: You cannot frighten me! I insist on being heard!

speaker: Policeman 1
en: Has a crime been committed, sir?

speaker: Marx
en: Indeed! A crime against humanity! I demand you live up to your responsibilities!

speaker: Policeman 1
en: You're a fine one to talk about responsibility. You look like a bloody tramp! Listen to me! I have been ordered to keep your rallies off the street.

speaker: Marx
en: No, you must listen to me! The people in this city are in dire need of your assistance!

speaker: Marx
en: Ah, you are Jacob Frye, are you not? And Miss Frye?

speaker: Evie
en: We are at a disadvantage, sir...?

speaker: Marx
en: Karl Marx. Much like you, I am an activist of sorts.

speaker: Jacob
en: You've got the look of a man who wants something.

speaker: Marx
en: Indeed, you've done more for London's citizens lately than any endeavor has accomplished in a decade. But those citizens were already well provided for. I challenge you both to help those who REALLY need your assistance. The working people.

speaker: Evie
en: An interesting challenge. We accept.

speaker: Jacob
en: Shouldn't we at least talk about these things fir... sod it, we accept.

speaker: Marx
en: I am organizing a discreet meeting with some like-minded friends to discuss trades unions. Alas, the police seem to have noticed my activities. They've stuck to me like flies on Scheiße (shit). In any case, I need you to help me get to the meeting without the interference of the police. You see, there's one of their damned spies now.

speaker: Marx
en: Tonight. Sundown. The usual place.

speaker: Man 1
en: I'll be there.

speaker: Marx
en: You know, I had similar problems with the police in Paris. Well, Paris and Brussels. And also perhaps Cologne. Our next worthy ally awaits in a nearby pub! Onwards! No doubt the police already have agents stationed within. I'll wait here until the coast is clear.

speaker: Marx
en: The usual location. One hour.

speaker: Man 2
en: Right you are, Mr. Marx, sir.

speaker: Marx
en: I believe our work here is complete. Come, let's slip away and get to the meeting. I do appreciate your assistance in this matter. Only when workers are able to assemble freely and in strength will we be able to achieve the reforms we most assuredly deserve. Might I trouble you to stay nearby until the meeting is over? I fear we may yet meet with some mischief.

speaker: Simon
en: I told you, Marx will be here! Heard it from the man's own lips! Now about my payment.

speaker: Policeman 2
en: You'll get your thirty pieces, chum, don't you worry.

speaker: Marx
en: It seems the movement is ever doomed to be betrayed from within. Will you fetch the gentleman back here? I would look him in the eye and ask why he went back on his brethren.

speaker: Simon
en: Are you mad? You're making a big mistake!

speaker: Marx
en: Simon. My friend. What possessed you to do this thing? Has the Party not taken care of you?

speaker: Simon
en: The guv'nor at the mill say any man what joins a Union, he'll be put out of work come sunup. How long will the Party feed my family for?

speaker: Marx
en: If we do not stand together, we are lost. My heart is broken, Simon. Please go.

speaker: Marx
en: I thank you, my friend. I hope you will continue to aid the struggle when the opportunity presents itself.

speaker: Evie
en: Please tell me again where we are going.

speaker: Henry
en: I found a letter from the Prince Consort among Lucy Thorne's research. Marked with the same insignia as your key. Dated 1847.

speaker: Henry
en: The same year the Prince began renovations to Buckingham Palace.

speaker: Evie
en: You think he added a vault for the Shroud!

speaker: Henry
en: And since there is no map of the palace with a room marked "secret vault"...

speaker: Henry
en: Your Highness, may I present Miss Evie Frye. Miss Frye, Maharajah Duleep Singh.

speaker: Evie
en: A pleasure, Your Highness.

speaker: Duleep
en: My friend, the plans you asked for have been removed.

speaker: Henry
en: Removed? By whom?

speaker: Duleep
en: Crawford Starrick. Or someone employed by him.

speaker: Duleep
en: Yes, I thought you might recognize the name. I know where they are, but it is heavily guarded.

speaker: Evie
en: That part will not be a problem.

speaker: Duleep
en: I thought not.

speaker: Evie
en: We're going to need a plan.

speaker: Henry
en: I can provide a distraction for the guards while you find a safe way inside.

speaker: Evie
en: Oh. Really?

speaker: Henry
en: For you, Evie, certainly.

speaker: Evie
en: Well... once I'm inside, I'll find someone who knows where the papers are stored...

speaker: Henry
en: And we will meet back on the train.

speaker: Evie
en: Be careful.

speaker: Evie
en: What's the plan?

speaker: Henry
en: When you give the signal, I'll draw the guards into a fight and then use a smoke bomb to get away.

speaker: Evie
en: And I'll take advantage of the confusion. Ready?

speaker: Henry
en: Absolutely.

speaker: Henry
en: Hey! I will put you all in jail! Crawford Starrick is a fool! Catch me at your peril! Are you prepared for my attack? An Assassin in your midst! Hey! I'm standing right over here! Some guards you are!

speaker: Templars
en: I've had quite enough of you! That way! I'll show you, you little meddler... Looks like there's a fly we need to swat. You're clearly asking to lose some teeth! You'll pipe down if you know what's good for you! You'll regret sticking your nose in! I'll have your tongue! Move along, you! I'll shut your mouth right quick!

speaker: Evie
en: That's not them. Nothing here. Looks like I'll have to ask someone where the plans are.

speaker: Templar 1
en: I swear, Miss, I don't know where they've taken him.

speaker: Evie
en: Taken who?

speaker: Templar 1
en: The man dressed like you. The guards dragged him off...

speaker: Evie
en: Henry. The plans you stole, where are they?

speaker: Templar 1
en: I don't know anything about that!

speaker: Evie
en: The plans... The mission...

speaker: Girl
en: Miss Frye!

speaker: Evie
en: You're some of Clara's children.

speaker: Girl
en: They took Mr. Henry! We couldn't stop 'em!

speaker: Boy
en: I bit one of them good, though!

speaker: Girl
en: They dragged him off in a red carriage.

speaker: Boy
en: They won't get far, though. One wheel looked like it was about ready to fall off. You can see the cart tracks—it looks all wobbly-like.

speaker: Evie
en: That cart's been run off the road. They must be driving quickly. They're knocking people over, too. And destruction of public property. I must be on the right track. That must be the carriage. Found you! Now to find Henry.

speaker: Merchant 1
en: Yeah, I saw them draggin' someone out of the carriage after the wheel fell off. They said he'd hit his head. Not sure why they needed to take him to the church, but that's where they went.

speaker: Merchant 2
en: I don't know anything about the carriage, but there's been some strange happenings around here today. All kinds of unsavory types wandering around. Armed to the teeth. I don't like it one bit.

speaker: Merchant 3
en: Yes, they pulled someone out of that carriage. Dead drunk, he was. They carried him into the church yard. Maybe he wanted a quiet place to sleep it off.

speaker: Monk
en: I could have sworn I'd locked this gate... This is supposed to be locked! Bloody urchins opened it again, no doubt.

speaker: Evie
en: Henry.

speaker: Templar 2
en: Is he coming around?

speaker: Templar 3
en: I dunno... we knocked him around pretty good. Wouldn't be surprised if it took a while...

speaker: Templar 2
en: Well, I hope you haven't addled his brain.

speaker: Templar 4
en: He's an Assassin! How much more addled can he get?

speaker: Templar 2
en: Why did you bring him here?

speaker: Templar 4
en: The man's an Assassin. We didn't want him getting away before you had a chance to question him, now did we?

speaker: Templar 2
en: He was more secure where he was before! I told you not to come here!

speaker: Henry
en: Evie, they sent someone to move the architectural plans. Do you have them?

speaker: Evie
en: Did they hurt you?

speaker: Henry
en: I'm fine.

speaker: Evie
en: Let's go.

speaker: Henry
en: What about the plans?

speaker: Evie
en: The plans are lost.

speaker: Henry
en: Evie, I'm sorry.

speaker: Evie
en: Just concentrate on escaping, please!

speaker: Evie
en: Gunmen on the rooftops!

speaker: Evie
en: Get Miss Nightingale to look at that. I must find the vault before Starrick secures the Shroud.

speaker: Henry
en: We'll talk to the Maharajah again.

speaker: Evie
en: I will talk to the Maharajah, you will get your head looked at.

speaker: Henry
en: I'm sorry my capture has undone your plans.

speaker: Evie
en: You'd be safer on the train.

speaker: Henry
en: Even if you find the vault, you can't just walk into Buckingham Palace alone.

speaker: Evie
en: I won't be alone! I'll see you back at the train, Mr. Green.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Victor Lynch sent a runner with some very good news! For our excellent performance in controlling this borough, we'll receive between us an extra allowance.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Those who recently escorted the shipment of explosives to Mr. Lynch's lodgings will receive a reward of 30 pounds for their effort. He thanks you for your services and encourages you not to spend your entire allotment at the Fox and Bottle. (Laughs)

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: The Rooks do not have the same resources as us. We're protected under the watchful eye of Victor Lynch, and we must fight our hardest to do our leader justice for his overwhelming kindness.

speaker: Leader
en: You want a fight to to death? Come on then lass, that's where the really money is! Who's with me!

speaker: Frederick Abberline
en: Thank you for taking another dangerous criminal off the streets, Miss Frye.

speaker: Dickens
en: My dear friend, The Ghost Club has an extraordinary case for you. Spiritualist Thaddeus the Amazing has predicted his own death at his next séance! Could you have a look?

speaker: Thaddeus
en: I have foretold my own death. But first! You are about to witness an extraordinary event. Ah! We have a visitor. Approach, please.

speaker: Voice
en: Goodness! The lights! What is this? Help! Not yet! Someone light the lamps!

speaker: Wilburn
en: Oh! He's actually dead!

speaker: Henry
en: This Soothing Syrup has become the only medicine available in Lambeth. It bears the Templar Grand Master's name.

speaker: Jacob
en: About time for a visit to the doctor.

speaker: Evie
en: I don't see that cure arriving any time soon.

speaker: Jacob
en: And what exactly will you be doing, might I ask?

speaker: Evie
en: You know very well, tracking down the Piece of Eden.

speaker: Jacob
en: Enjoy your studies. I'll be out killing Templars.

speaker: Jacob
en: Ah, another exciting night home for Evie Frye.

speaker: Evie
en: Just on my way out, actually. I've found the Piece of Eden.

speaker: Jacob
en: What's this one going to do, hm? Heal the sick? Deflect bullets? Control the populace?

speaker: Evie
en: They're dangerous objects, Jacob, especially in Templar hands.

speaker: Jacob
en: Huh, you sound exactly like Father.

speaker: Evie
en: If only. Lucy Thorne is expecting a shipment tonight. She's Starrick's expert in the occult. I'm nearly certain she is receiving the Piece of Eden Sir David Brewster mentioned.

speaker: Jacob
en: Sounds like fun. Mind if I join you?

speaker: Evie
en: Promise you will stick to the mission.

speaker: Jacob
en: I swear.

speaker: Thorne
en: The contents of that box are worth more than your life and those of your entire family. Do you understand?

speaker: Templar
en: Yes, Miss Thorne.

speaker: Templar
en: Careful, there! And double the guard on that cart! Now, Miss Thorne, there's the matter of some papers for Mr. Starrick. If you'll just come this way...

speaker: Thorne
en: Very well, but make it quick.

speaker: Evie
en: Whatever it is she's after, it's in that chest.

speaker: Jacob
en: There are gunmen on the rooftops.

speaker: Evie
en: Can you dispose of them before I reach the cart?

speaker: Jacob
en: I was hoping for a challenge.

speaker: Jacob
en: Did you find it?

speaker: Evie
en: Actually...

speaker: Templar
en: There he is!

speaker: Jacob
en: I think it's best we leave.

speaker: Evie
en: What did you do?

speaker: Jacob
en: It's hardly the time for questions.

speaker: Evie
en: Whoa!

speaker: Thorne
en: Come on!

speaker: Evie
en: We need to get this crate back to a safe place!

speaker: Jacob
en: What do you think I'm trying to do?

speaker: Evie
en: At a guess, I'd say "kill us both"!

speaker: Jacob
en: If you really want to fight, come over here!

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob!

speaker: Jacob
en: Wager you can't hit my sister!

speaker: Evie
en: Stop it!

speaker: Jacob
en: Come over here and get us, then!

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob, stop it!

speaker: Jacob
en: My sister will give you a walloping!

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob! Careful!

speaker: Jacob
en: What is it?

speaker: Evie
en: It's papers, Jacob. Documents. Research!

speaker: Jacob
en: What are we supposed to do with papers?

speaker: Evie
en: Read them. If only we had the time.

speaker: Jacob
en: Then where's your Piece of Eden?

speaker: Evie
en: Get us out of this and I might find out!

speaker: Evie
en: Would you drive a little more carefully? You're endangering the documents!

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, poor documents! Perhaps you'd rather I just stop right here?

speaker: Evie
en: I need cartridges!

speaker: Jacob
en: Use mine!

speaker: Evie
en: I'm out of bullets!

speaker: Jacob
en: Take my cartridge!

speaker: Evie
en: I don't have enough bullets!

speaker: Jacob
en: I've got more - just keep shooting!

speaker: Jacob
en: We're going to have to jump.

speaker: Evie
en: What about the chest?

speaker: Jacob
en: Leave it! Jump! Now!

speaker: Jacob
en: Well that was fun! Thanks for the invitation. Must do it again. Ha ha!

speaker: Evie
en: Damn it.

speaker: Agnes
en: We fixed up the train for ye. Lick of paint, new rugs from Camden Lock and mah wee sister, the seamster, did a discount on the curtains.

speaker: Darwin
en: "We are not apes"... If the circumstances were not so grave, I'd compliment the artist on the wonderful caricature. They are fools if they believe they can stop progress by printing leaflets and killing newsboys! We must find out who is behind this propaganda before more innocents are harmed. I should very much like it if you could find and remove these awful things. Perhaps you can catch one of the billposters red-handed?

speaker: Civilians
en: This a waste of paper, if you ask me! Not apes? Of course we're not apes! Look at us! Of course we are not apes! I don't need anyone to tell me that! God created us in his image! And he does not look like a monkey! Apes!? This is outrageous, I tell you! Outrageous!

speaker: Civilian
en: This is vandalism! Someone should inform the police!

speaker: Jacob
en: Oi! What are you doing over there?

speaker: Evie
en: You! What do you think you're doing?

speaker: Billposter
en: Stop it! Please! I beg you!

speaker: Jacob
en: Who are you working for? And why are they so violent against Mr. Darwin's theories?

speaker: Billposter
en: Darwin refused to cooperate with us! We wanted to recruit him, but he rebuffed all our offers. We've tried to intimidate him, blackmail him, but he's a stubborn old git.

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm going to take your operation apart.

speaker: Darwin
en: My young friend! I'm sorry to be so blunt, but I need to ask a favor of you. A delivery awaits me at the docks, a very rare orchid, all the way from the island of Madagascar. But there is a problem... One of my "associates" wants the flower for himself. He sent ruffians to collect it, if you can believe that. I need you to collect it for me first.

speaker: Darwin
en: Ah! Thank you, my young friend, thank you! This little orchid may seem inconsequential, but it holds secrets which could potentially change our very understanding of the world. It would have been a shame to lose it! A shame indeed! Thank you!

speaker: David Jack-Emmings
en: I'm just finishin' off the good work the Ripper started, see? Once the whores are all dead, this borough'll be the better for it...

speaker: Abberline
en: Thank you for taking another dangerous criminal off the streets, Miss Frye.

speaker: Abberline
en: What good will he do me dead?

speaker: Matthew
en: Hear, hear.

speaker: Matthew
en: You hold a candle to the Devil, David.

speaker: Jacob
en: Quiet now, don't want to disturb the prayers.

speaker: Jacob
en: Out of every church in the district.

speaker: Jacob
en: Save it for the sergeant, would you?

speaker: Evie
en: Shh. You're making too much noise.

speaker: Evie
en: Stealing organ pipes, what else?

speaker: Evie
en: I haven't put as much thought into it as you.

speaker: Jacob
en: Keep your trap shut.

speaker: Evie
en: You're not getting away that easily.

speaker: Abberline
en: Thank you for bringing him in.

speaker: Dickens
en: You seem tired, friend. Everything all right?

speaker: Jacob
en: No rest for the wicked, Charlie.

speaker: Evie
en: There's always too much work to do.

speaker: Dickens
en: Today's Ghost Club investigation involves a carriage! It's said to be covered with gold leaf, dazzling passersby when the sun shines! Naturally, it's rumored to be haunted. Now let's see if we can find it!

speaker: Jacob
en: I presume this was once used to carry the mail. That actually looks remarkably comfortable.

speaker: Evie
en: The Royal Mall coaches vanished when the post began to be transported by rail. Oh, I'd rather enjoy a sit down. But duty calls.

speaker: Jacob
en: What the devil?

speaker: Evie
en: That's curious.

speaker: Woman
en: Help! Please, someone, help me! Please, someone help me! I have been torn from my home and family by these villains! This will not work, sir! You may kidnap me but you will never have me!

speaker: Woman
en: Who's there? Are you a friend?

speaker: Jacob
en: Yes, madam, don't worry, you're safe.

speaker: Evie
en: Yes, you're safe. You don't have to worry any more.

speaker: Woman
en: Oh, you've saved me. That wretch would have forced me to marry him within the hour. I must return home. Oh! His accomplices will surely murder you! Quickly, we have not a moment to lose.

speaker: Jacob
en: Right you are, miss.

speaker: Evie
en: Of course.

speaker: Woman
en: We've lost them. Thank you, you have been a great help. Will you please take me home? I owe you my thanks, you have gone to a great deal of trouble for someone you don't even know! What is your name?

speaker: Jacob
en: Jacob Frye, Miss.

speaker: Evie
en: Evie Frye.

speaker: Woman
en: You have preserved my honour and saved my life. I am Elizabeth. Won't you climb down and sit beside me, so that I may see your face?

speaker: Jacob
en: Miss? Where are you?

speaker: Evie
en: Where is she?

speaker: Dickens
en: You look as though you're just about to collapse! What on Earth has happened?

speaker: Jacob
en: You wouldn't believe me if I told you.

speaker: Evie
en: Just a dream... Or so I think...

speaker: Arthur Weaversbrook
en: Miss Frye... I have helped spread the Ripper's terror through my newspapers. I want to make amends for my part in forging this monster's legend. Whether or not is a fake, we cannot ignore the chance that a lunatic, and not some misguided newspaperman wrote it...

speaker: Suspect
en: The Ripper has captured the world's attention, maybe some good will come out of it... the east end needs to change...

speaker: Suspect
en: All right, yes! I know it was not a good idea, but I thought I'd galvanize the public in order to help the poor citizens of this city!

speaker: Henry
en: There you are! This could be interesting. There's no shortage of firearms in this neighborhood!

speaker: Arthur
en: I suspect the solution will turn on geometry, timing and human nature!

speaker: Henry
en: There may be a in it! Look into it, won't you?

speaker: Darwin
en: My young friend! Today's papers carry a rebuttal of Mr. Owen's slanderous and ignorant remarks about . However, I'm feeling quite like a fossil today. Would you be a dear and get me a copy of the newspaper?

speaker: Vendor
en: Take whatever you want! Help me!

speaker: Jacob
en: Hey! you!

speaker: Evie
en: Stop that!

speaker: Thug
en: You... You saved my life!

speaker: Jacob
en: Yes. Now here's a question for you: Why would you attack a newsboy?

speaker: Thug
en: A man paid me and my mates to force newsboys to display this leaflet! Here! Take the bloody thing and leave me alone!

speaker: Jacob
en: This spells trouble for Mr. Darwin.

speaker: Thug
en: You... You saved my life!

speaker: Evie
en: Correct... Now tell me: why have you attacked the newsboy?

speaker: Thug
en: A man paid me and my mates to force newsboys to display this leaflet! Here! Take the bloody thing and leave me alone!

speaker: Evie
en: Mr. Darwin will want to hear about this...

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: I can smell a handsome reward if we take out those Frye twins and their renegade Rooks. What say you?

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: I have all the faith that Miss Graves will put an end to this upstart nonsense. She was given the name ‘the Bludger' for a reason, after all.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Hopefully we can meet these Rooks soon. I'm dying to sink my claws into some fresh meat.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Mister Strain has sent us a letter. It reads: "Tom, word has reached my ears of a couple of rogue twins sparking an uprising in the underworld of London. Keep the Blighters in check. Who knows how many borough leaders they've taken out now. I warn you, stay level headed, leave the brutalities to me. If they want to play, we'll play. Hopefully this will save me from the constant boredom that plagues me. Stay in touch. Cletus."

speaker: Collicott
en: I can't believe them.

speaker: Bodyguard
en: Who, Sir?

speaker: Collicott
en: The Order, of course! Everything I've ever done was for the Order! And now they pretend I don't exist. Of course, as soon as I get into trouble, they stop supporting me

speaker: Bodyguard
en: I'm sorry, Sir.

speaker: Collicott
en: Where would they be if they didn't have me to clean up their messes? In the ground, that's where. This is the last time I do a mission for them.

speaker: Bodyguard
en: We can't leave the Order, Sir. They'll hunt us down.

speaker: Collicott
en: You'd rather be a slave to them all your life? I won't stand for it.

speaker: Egyptian Spoils
en: was a virtual representation of one of Evie Frye's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Sedgwick
en: What? What do you think you're doing? Where are you taking me, rat?

speaker: Jacob
en: Quiet, you. Calm down. Act normal.

speaker: Sedgwick
en: I was just minding my own business.

speaker: Jacob
en: There's been a warrant out for your arrest for nearly a decade.

speaker: Sedgwick
en: So that's what you do? You work for the cops?

speaker: Jacob
en: You could say that.

speaker: Sedgwick
en: It's about time! I've been at this for YEARS, and gotten away with every single crime I've committed.

speaker: Jacob
en: The police have been after you for how long?

speaker: Sedgwick
en: What? Where are you taking me, rat?

speaker: Evie
en: Hush. Quiet down, you'll give someone a fright.

speaker: Sedgwick
en: This is about the good old days, isn't it? They finally want me to cash in my lengthy term of imprisonment?

speaker: Evie
en: That's right.

speaker: Sedgwick
en: It's about damn time! Those cops have been after me for years, and even as an old man I've been able to get away from those lazy buggers. I've committed nearly every crime in the book and they let me get away with it.

speaker: Evie
en: At least you're honest about it.

speaker: Sedgwick
en: Ha-ha! Still got it! Help! Who would attack a poor old man?

speaker: Sedgwick
en: Smarter than you look! Here, take me in. I'm all yours, chap.

speaker: Sedgwick
en: Old King Cole was a merry old soul / And a merry old soul was he / He called for his pipe, and he called for his bowl / And he called for his fiddlers three!

speaker: Abberline
en: ... Charming...

speaker: Dipper
en: That's a nice watch you have there. Mind if I take a gander?

speaker: Customer 1
en: This belonged to my grandfather.

speaker: Dipper
en: Old thing doesn't even tick.

speaker: Customer 1
en: Not anymore, no. It's just for show, really.

speaker: Dipper
en: Could I interest you in a trade? Maybe you fancy something pretty and useful.

speaker: Dipper
en: Looking for anything in particular?

speaker: Customer 2
en: Where the crabshells from, dearie?

speaker: Dipper
en: A fella back in Whitechapel gave them to me.

speaker: Customer 2
en: Gave them to ya?

speaker: Dipper
en: Oh, yes. Kind fella he was. Too many shoes, he said.

speaker: Customer 2
en: What's this red mark here?

speaker: Dipper
en: Oh, that? Nothing, bit of wine is all.

speaker: Morris
en: They're moving the shipment, but we must go now. There's a carriage on the next corner. If we hide within, they'll drive us right to it!

speaker: Jacob
en: I'll hide inside it. You're going home.

speaker: Morris
en: Home? Back to a cold and cheerless house? Where I'll wear black gloves and sport a weed on my hat for a year? Then I'll return to the factory like a small cog in the great wheel of capital? No! I want justice! I must have those explosives!

speaker: Jacob
en: Nobody's laying their hands on the , chum. Not you, not them. Nobody. Enough blood's been spilled already.

speaker: Morris
en: I am trying to build a better world. To ensure that no one suffers what my son did. Pray tell me, "friend", how much blood do you consider that to be worth?

speaker: Morris
en: They're moving the shipment, but we must go now. There's a carriage on the next corner. If we hide within, they'll drive us right to it!

speaker: Evie
en: It's time you went home. I'll hide in the carriage alone.

speaker: Morris
en: Home? Back to a cold and cheerless house? Where I'll wear black gloves and sport a weed on my hat for a year? Then I'll return to the factory like a small cog in the great wheel of capital? No! I want justice! I must have those explosives!

speaker: Evie
en: I grieve with you. But would your wife want to see your hands stained with the blood of so many?

speaker: Morris
en: I am trying to build a better world. To ensure that no one suffers what my son did. Pray tell me, "friend", how much blood do you consider that to be worth?

speaker: Jacob
en: These ones get to live, at least until they drive me to this factory.

speaker: Evie
en: I'll keep those ones alive until they take me to our destination.

speaker: Templar 1
en: Well, they'll never get hold of it now.

speaker: Templar 2
en: Bleedin' anarchists! Couldn't organize a piss up in a brewery!

speaker: Templar 1
en: About bloody time. What the hell took you so long?

speaker: Templar 2
en: Yeah, I'd like to see anyone try an' break in 'ere.

speaker: Morris
en: I'm sorry, but my need is greater than you know! Justice will be done!

speaker: Morris
en: Wait! Don't shoot! This is nitro!

speaker: Jacob
en: Morris! Poor sod. All right, better smash these crates before anyone else gets any bright ideas!

speaker: Evie
en: Mr. Morris! Poor man. I hope he finds some kind of peace. Now to destroy the crates! No one is getting their hands on this hellfire!

speaker: Marx
en: You're back. Mr. Morris? I see. I was afraid it would come to this. He was a good man, but even the best of us can lose our way when blinded by grief. Still, I thank you for preventing a greater tragedy.

speaker: Duleep
en: Delighted to see you again, Miss Frye.

speaker: Evie
en: Your Highness, the plans detailing the renovations to Buckingham Palace have gone astray.

speaker: Duleep
en: I suppose you will have to make do with the copies.

speaker: Evie
en: There are copies? Where?

speaker: Duleep
en: Not so fast. First, I have a matter of some urgency. Carrying out my plan would require stealth and speed, qualities I know you possess.

speaker: Evie
en: Time is of the essence, Your Highness.

speaker: Duleep
en: Then make this quick, my dear. The most influential men in Parliament remain beyond my reach. But these very men have sent for carriages to prepare for the ball tonight. Acquire an official carriage, and we shall drive the politicians to their destinations. Along the way, I will meet with them. And, afterward, I shall tell you where to find the plans.

speaker: Evie
en: You're a shrewd negotiator.

speaker: Duleep
en: One must be, when one is so often underestimated.

speaker: Evie
en: "Don't allow personal feelings to compromise the mission". What a mistake.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Sounds like they'll be having quite a party tonight.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Don't get too excited. It just means the toffs will be puking in the bushes at 3 am, and we'll be the ones cleaning it up.

speaker: Guard 1
en: God save the Queen...

speaker: Guard 3
en: Do you think we'll get a glimpse of anyone important?

speaker: Guard 4
en: If we're lucky, we'll keep well away from it and have a nice, boring night.

speaker: Guard 5
en: Thank God my shift ends early tonight.

speaker: Guard 6
en: You sound like you want a nap more than you want your job!

speaker: Guard 5
en: When you're my age, you'll feel the same.

speaker: Guard 6
en: We're the same age!

speaker: Duleep
en: Shall we lobby our cause, Miss Frye?

speaker: Evie
en: Climb up, Your Highness.

speaker: Evie
en: Where are we headed?

speaker: Duleep
en: Belgrave Square.

speaker: Politician 1
en: I must pick up my son to be on time for the ball tonight! Why the blazes is everything so slow? My carriage is late! Victoria station, please, and on the double! My son is anticipating my arrival.

speaker: Duleep
en: Welcome, sir.

speaker: Politician 1
en: Your Highness. What a surprise.

speaker: Duleep
en: Ha, is life not about embracing the unexpected? I shall take but a few moments of your time. A matter of utmost importance must be discussed. When the Commonwealth seized the Punjab from my people

speaker: Politician 1
en: It was not a seizure, but a rightful transaction.

speaker: Duleep
en: Britain promised to protect me. By robbing me of my kingdom, Parliament acted in violation of the signed with my family. Here, read it.

speaker: Politician 1
en: I—I was not aware.

speaker: Duleep
en: Read. That is all I ask. You are one of the few in a position to help.

speaker: Politician 1
en: I will do what I can.

speaker: Duleep
en: Thank you, sir.

speaker: Duleep
en: I trust you and your son will enjoy the ball this evening.

speaker: Politican 1
en: He is newly returned from . I will share what we have discussed. It is most disconcerting.

speaker: Duleep
en: That proved quite valuable.

speaker: Evie
en: Where to now?

speaker: Duleep
en: St James' Park. I notice Mr. Green did not accompany you.

speaker: Evie
en: He has other things to attend to.

speaker: Duleep
en: Ah. A pity. You two seemed to get along nicely.

speaker: Evie
en: Well, that was a problem, you see. "One must not allow personal feelings to compromise one's mission".

speaker: Duleep
en: That sounds like a quotation.

speaker: Evie
en: It is. From my father.

speaker: Duleep
en: Ethan Frye.

speaker: Evie
en: You knew him?

speaker: Duleep
en: No, unfortunately. But Mr. Green spoke of him. He sounded like an extraordinary man.

speaker: Evie
en: He was, Your Highness.

speaker: Duleep
en: And your mother as well. Cecily Frye. She and your father were partners, inseparable. The only duo that came close to challenging Mr. Starrick. And very much in love, at least, from the small amount I have been told.

speaker: Evie
en: Cecily. I wish I could have met her.

speaker: Duleep
en: From what Mr. Green gathered, you share much in common. Your intelligence, for one.

speaker: Evie
en: Father never spoke of her. What would Mr. Green know? He was only a boy when he trained with my father.

speaker: Duleep
en: Children can be quite perceptive, Miss Frye.

speaker: Politician 2
en: To Parliament, please, on the double!

speaker: Evie
en: Yes, sir.

speaker: Duleep
en: Good day, sir.

speaker: Politician 2
en: Why, what are you doing here, Your Highness?

speaker: Duleep
en: I know how busy your days have been of late. A few moments of your time is all I require.

speaker: Politician 2
en: This is all rather unorthodox, but continue.

speaker: Duleep
en: Britain was to protect me according to the treaty my family signed. Instead, she took my land. And now, I hear Britain intends to strengthen her ties to India. Perhaps it is time to return the Punjab to her people.

speaker: Politician 2
en: The Queen has supplied you with an annual income for God knows how long, and now you bite the hand that feeds you?

speaker: Duleep
en: It is not a matter of money. I cannot stand idle and watch my homeland subjected to the yoke of an outsider's rule. My people are treated as slaves. I will die poor a thousand times over if only to see them free.

speaker: Politician 2
en: Your passion moves me, Your Highness. What would you have me do?

speaker: Duleep
en: Take this copy of the wrongful treaty and defend my claim to the throne. Help disengage the Punjab from British rule.

speaker: Politician 2
en: I shall speak up, but I am only one voice. I cannot promise anything but a show of support.

speaker: Duleep
en: That is more than enough. Thank you, sir.

speaker: Politician 2
en: My pleasure, Your Highness.

speaker: Politician 2
en: Good day, sir.

speaker: Duleep
en: May God bless you. Only one more remains. To the Gladstone residence.

speaker: Evie
en: Do you miss India?

speaker: Duleep
en: I remember... that my mother smelled of cinnamon. And when she cradled me in her arms in the summer heat, I would hold so still that she fell asleep. When I lost my kingdom, it hurt, but truly, when they took my mother away... I saw her again two years before she died. The summer long since faded. I miss her, I miss India. I love India because I love my mother.

speaker: Evie
en: Will you ever return?

speaker: Duleep
en: I have petitioned the government several times, but they withhold their permission. Do not be fooled by appearances, Miss Frye. I am in many ways a prisoner.

speaker: Evie
en: Perhaps we may work together more closely for your cause in the future.

speaker: Duleep
en: I would like that very much, Miss Frye.

speaker: Gladstone
en: What else can go wrong? This day is a disaster! Where in the blazes is my carriage? To the Sinopean Club, straight away.

speaker: Duleep
en: Good day, Mr. Gladstone.

speaker: Gladstone
en: Mr. Singh?

speaker: Duleep
en: You are a hard man to pin down.

speaker: Gladstone
en: I know what this is about. Your parlor tricks have worn off. Her Majesty has tired of you, so now you come begging for scraps.

speaker: Duleep
en: You wound me deeply, sir. My people deserve freedom. I am here to fight for them.

speaker: Gladstone
en: Why did you lose the Punjab? I shall tell you, "Your Highness". You were outgunned, outmaneuvered and simply outclassed. Yes, the Sikhs deserve freedom. I hope with British help and progress, they shall achieve it.

speaker: Duleep
en: Then why do they cry out for their king?

speaker: Gladstone
en: Britain has a duty to bring about peace. It is an enormous responsibility, and I value your guidance and advice, along with that of Parliament. But it's our burden to rule India, and certainly not the duty of a forgotten leader who has not seen his country for twenty years. I apologize for being so frank, but one must not tell lies to a king.

speaker: Duleep
en: Your honesty is most enlightening.

speaker: Gladstone
en: When I become Prime Minister, I intend to push for peace, but it will be a long and slow process. And I am afraid I can almost guarantee you will never see India again.

speaker: Duleep
en: If my people are free, then my imprisonment shall be no burden.

speaker: Gladstone
en: Perhaps your idealism is real. Although, after observing the tigers wandering the grounds of your lush, expensive estate, forgive me for doubting it.

speaker: Gladstone
en: Much luck, Your Highness, with your lobbying. I hope my advice has done some good.

speaker: Duleep
en: Far more than your policies, thus far. But I hold out hope that you will make progress. My people are counting on it.

speaker: Duleep
en: Thank you, Miss Frye, for forwarding my cause.

speaker: Evie
en: Oh, you are welcome. I hope some good comes of it, despite Mr. Gladstone's vitriol.

speaker: Duleep
en: Those of us with the largest hearts protect them the most. Your father, for instance. From what I understand, he was extraordinarily sad, broken even, after your mother's passing. That kind of pain can blind us, can cause us to say outlandish things to protect the ones we love. It's time you returned this carriage and recovered those plans. They are located in Buckingham Palace. The Queen keeps them among her personal papers in the White Drawing Room. I wish you a good evening, Miss Evie Frye.

speaker: Evie
en: And to you, Your Highness.

speaker: Evie
en: Those coppers won't believe their eyes.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Word has come down about a couple of meddling twins. Miss Nora is interested in meetin'em. If you hear word of their location, please come forward. You'll be sufficiently rewarded.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: The Blighters remain in control of London. Miss Nora informs me that the next move will be to retake Whitechapel.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Yes, Whitechapel's Mister Kaylock has died at the hands of some renegade group called the Rooks, but they're no match for us.

speaker: Henry
en: Ah! This is one that's most promising

speaker: Arthur
en: An important detective is missing! Skullduggery is surely afoot!

speaker: Henry
en: Solve it, and I'll quick as you please!

speaker: Henry
en: Oh good, you're here. His highness seems to have caught a mild case of madness this morning.

speaker: Duleep
en: You were right when you said that this was our chance.

speaker: Jacob
en: I was?

speaker: Duleep
en: I propose we make a commotion, lure out the Templar-controlled British Indies Company.

speaker: Jacob
en: And do what? Put yourself in the line of fire?

speaker: Duleep
en: I need to send Ellsworth a message. This won't be over until we can draw him out. This is something I must do. I will make a scene, and then you need to rough them up a little.

speaker: Jacob
en: Well that shouldn't be a problem.

speaker: Duleep
en: I heard you Templars are a bunch of pansies.

speaker: Jacob
en: Here we go.

speaker: Templar 1
en: Please, spare me!

speaker: Duleep
en: I need you to send a message to Ellsworth.

speaker: Templar 1
en: I'll do anything!

speaker: Duleep
en: Tell him to meet me at Lambeth Cemetery tonight. And tell him to come alone.

speaker: Duleep
en: Meet me tonight at Lambeth cemetery. He'll never come alone, even if I ask him to.

speaker: Templar 2
en: Thought you could get away, did you?

speaker: Evie
en: That caused quite a commotion...

speaker: Jacob
en: He's gone mad! Greenie was right!

speaker: Evie
en: He isn't mad, Jacob. He's trying to take action, to do the right thing... Oh never mind. I'll take it from here.

speaker: Jacob
en: Fine by me... I could use a good pint right about now.

speaker: Duleep
en: Oh. I was expecting Jacob but I'm glad it's you who have come.

speaker: Evie
en: He thinks you've gone mad.

speaker: Duleep
en: I probably have.

speaker: Evie
en: What's your plan?

speaker: Duleep
en: I've asked Brinley to meet me here alone. In turn, he of course has sent a small army to secure the area. I need you to get rid of them and meet me back here. It's essential that when Brinley does arrive, I have him to myself.

speaker: Duleep
en: That will certainly help quite a bit, thank you.

speaker: Evie
en: He's here.

speaker: Duleep
en: I must talk to him.

speaker: Evie
en: Don't be absurd. This is dangerous.

speaker: Duleep
en: Miss Frye, this is something I must do, and I must do it alone. Remain hidden. I cannot afford to have him see you.

speaker: Brinley
en: You can't escape me forever, your Highness. Come out and face me.

speaker: Duleep
en: I told you to meet me here alone.

speaker: Brinley
en: I am not as silly as I once was, Singh. I wouldn't dare come to this meeting place alone. Not with your recently acquired friends.

speaker: Duleep
en: I am alone, Ellsworth. It doesn't have to be like this.

speaker: Brinley
en: You can't just walk this Earth like a free man. You are nothing more than a trophy, a stag's head above the mantelpiece. You have caused enough commotion as it is. It's time to put an end to this.

speaker: Duleep
en: If you kill me now, you will be a wanted man. Imagine the uprising when they find out the only son of Ranjit Singh has been murdered.

speaker: Brinley
en: Ah Ah Ah Ah... You think they remember you? You are a lost soul, a monarch who has abandoned his people. You are nothing.

speaker: Duleep
en: We were such good friends

speaker: Brinley
en: Friends? You were no more than a play-thing. A prisoner in prince's clothing. You're lucky to be alive. I admit, I'm surprised they let you live.

speaker: Brinley
en: I knew you were lying, Singh!

speaker: Duleep
en: Ellsworth, listen

speaker: Brinley
en: I've had enough of this.

speaker: Brinley
en: I knew you were lying!

speaker: Duleep
en: No! You mustn't!

speaker: Duleep
en: Miss Frye!

speaker: Evie
en: He will kill you!

speaker: Brinley
en: This is what I was sent here for. Be done with it, girl! I shall never forfeit my own mission.

speaker: Duleep
en: I will not allow it!

speaker: Brinley
en: The Logins', the Company, they all wanted your silence! Whether you spare me or end me, you won't escape the fate they have planned for you.

speaker: Duleep
en: It seems you have learned nothing of India, of its people... But killing you? That is something I cannot do. It would make me no better than that cursed, oppressive company you work for.

speaker: Brinley
en: You will die as you were raised, Singh. You will never be more than a trophy of war.

speaker: Brinley
en: We will bury you in English soil.

speaker: Duleep
en: You have done me much good. I am heavily indebted to you both.

speaker: Evie
en: We are happy to help.

speaker: Duleep
en: I fear that I cannot continue handling things in this manner. The Assassin way is not my way, as helpful as you have been. This Empire, this land, my people... The problem is so much bigger than death. I know I must devote my life to this cause, to put India, my home, back onto the map, return it to its people. It's a long and gruelling journey, but it is something I must do. Even if it takes me to my own death.

speaker: Evie
en: We understand, your highness.

speaker: Jacob
en: But, if you do change your mind, you know where to find us.

speaker: Duleep
en: That I do. Thank you, Assassins. Hopefully we never shall meet again.

speaker: Bell
en: Ah, blast 'em!

speaker: Henry
en: Aleck, whatever is the matter?

speaker: Bell
en: I have been intercepting nothing but poppycock propaganda about Soothing Syrup and whatnot. No, I swear to high heavens, if Starrick's monopoly continues

speaker: Henry
en: Aleck, I beg your pardon, these are friends of mine, Evie Frye and her brother, Jacob.

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, um... Alexander Graham Bell.

speaker: Henry
en: Linguist, inventor and technical expert. Aleck, I have something of a favor to ask of you.

speaker: Jacob
en: Can you fix this?

speaker: Bell
en: Hmmm, looks like the casing is cracked...

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, it comes apart. I say, I could have used one of these to fix my fuses on top of Big Ben.

speaker: Henry
en: Aleck is installing a new telegraph line for our Free Press Association.

speaker: Bell
en: To combat the Starrick Telegraph Company. Now, if I can mend the fuses connecting independent lines from Big Ben, Starrick will be weakened. Only, we are somewhat at a handicap.

speaker: Bell
en: And, there. Oh, I've removed the mechanism so it may work with your bracer.

speaker: Jacob
en: I'll put it to use immediately.

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob, wait. Mr. Bell, allow me to help with your fuses.

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, you will not find me too proud to accept, Miss Frye. We can use my carriage. If you'd be so good as to hold the reins, though.

speaker: Evie
en: I'll take that.

speaker: Bell
en: Erm, I can help you.

speaker: Bell
en: Ah, Miss Frye, I am so glad you could assist me. You really ought to be here by now.

speaker: Evie
en: So, Mr. Bell, what inventions are you concocting?

speaker: Bell
en: I intend to develop a phonetic telegraph that does not just convey dots and dashes, Miss Frye, but the human voice!

speaker: Evie
en: Phonetic telegraph? Hmmm, sounds a bit of a mouthful. You could just call it a... telephone.

speaker: Bell
en: Telephone. Hah! How bizarre! Anyway, as I was saying earlier, the press has become entirely dependent on the Starrick Telegraph Company.

speaker: Evie
en: Which is why Mr. Green has asked you to set up a free line.

speaker: Bell
en: Yes. What is more, other small independent companies have had their lines sabotaged, and they have little means of finding any broken fuses, which are...

speaker: Evie
en: To be found on top of Big Ben.

speaker: Bell
en: Correct. Especially as one needs a special government pass to get through the guards.

speaker: Evie
en: They will not be a problem. I'll repair the fuses.

speaker: Evie
en: Lovely view. All set. That should do it.

speaker: Guard 1
en: That Starrick's got it well sorted.

speaker: Guard 2
en: I've heard he's got a brilliant brain on him.

speaker: Guard 1
en: He'd outwit a troop of wolves! And if he controls the telegraphs, he controls the news!

speaker: Bell
en: Thank you very much, Miss Frye. I will now be able to continue with the installation of the new line!

speaker: Evie
en: If there's anything else I can do to help...

speaker: Bell
en: Certainly! Please do come by and visit. Oh! Erh, I was just toying with this device and have noted down the formula for you. It's not perfect yet, but by golly, it works!

speaker: Bell
en: Whoa whoa whoa!! Maybe a little too well! Whoa!!

speaker: Blighter 1
en: What's that shipment of cables for, then?

speaker: Blighter 2
en: The Starrick telegraph network, didn't you know? The boss says it'll be even bigger than the Electric and International.

speaker: Blighter 1
en: Oh yeah? Well I've heard the government wanna get their grobby hands on all the telegraph companies.

speaker: Blighter 2
en: I wouldn't worry about politicians. We know who really pulls the strings, don't we?

speaker: Blighter 1
en: But knowledge is power!

speaker: Blighter 2
en: And news is control of power!

speaker: Blighter 3
en: You can make or break any man with news. Even the top knobs.

speaker: Blighter 4
en: And how'd you work that out?

speaker: Blighter 3
en: Take Mr. Gladstone. Everyone knows he's a night walker, right? But what if news spreads he does more than walking and talking to your Lillies and your Mollies?

speaker: Blighter 4
en: Can't find fault in Mr. Disraeli, though. And bold as brass, he is.

speaker: Blighter 3
en: Ah, but dig deep enough... A man of sixty will have a whole garden full of buried bones... Keep it to yourself, but I heard Mr. Starrick say Disraeli had a secret daughter.

speaker: Blighter 4
en: Nah. The crafty old goat!

speaker: Blighter 3
en: Mum's the word, eh, about Disraeli and Gladstone.

speaker: Blighter 4
en: Count on me, I wouldn't wanna spoil the surprise for the country's most illustrious men of power!

speaker: Blighter 3
en: So you see, Billy boy, parliament won't be getting in the way of our Mr. Starrick. Cunning as a weasel, he is.

speaker: Bell
en: Ah, Miss Frye, I was just showing Jacob the first messages received via the mended lines. Oh, and you can keep the rope launcher by the way, we have managed to procure another one for your brother. Excellent work, thank you again.

speaker: Evie
en: You're very welcome, Mr. Bell.

speaker: Bell
en: We can now defend the principle of impartial news and free speech.

speaker: Jacob
en: Free is fair, but free and brief is far better!

speaker: Bell
en: Haha, Frye, such caustic wit.

speaker: Evie
en: And on that note, we must depart.

speaker: Bell
en: Oh, uh, good fortune to you both. Call on me anytime.

speaker: Evie
en: Now that we've finished with that distraction

speaker: Jacob
en: Who is that?

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, you mean... you don't know?

speaker: Ned
en: Beautiful train you've got here. Miss MacBean was just telling me all about her. Name's Ned.

speaker: Henry
en: How do you do?

speaker: Ned
en: I won't take up more of your time. If you want to learn a thing or two about the finest transit, you can find me at this address.

speaker: Evie
en: Let us return to locating the Piece of Eden.

speaker: Jacob
en: We need to reclaim London from Starrick. Who are my targets?

speaker: Evie
en: It's not time for that yet.

speaker: Jacob
en: I didn't come to London to hunt curios!

speaker: Evie
en: "First understand the dance, only then become the dancer."

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh? So you're taking over where Father left off?

speaker: Evie
en: Someone has to.

speaker: Henry
en: Evie, finding the Precursor artifact will give us an insight into what the Templars intend. Jacob, I have information about Starrick's associates that should be of use to you. Here.

speaker: Arthur Weaversbrook
en: Miss Frye... I have helped spread the Ripper's terror through my newspapers. I want to make amends for my part in forging this monster's legend. The central newspaper agency has received . Handwriting experts have identified a suspect this time... We must be sure it is not him. Miss Frye, it's about a new Ripper letter. I hope it's nothing but a hoax, but we cannot afford to ignore it.

speaker: Suspect
en: Can you believe it! The front page of London's biggest newspaper... I fooled those rozzers, ha ha ha!

speaker: Suspect
en: I was just having a lark! Wanted to see if I could get away with it... I don't know who the Ripper is, but it ain't me, ask me wife...

speaker: Messenger
en: London's so-called "Bloody Nora" has challenged you to a gang war. All weapons permitted. Good luck to both sides.

speaker: Messenger
en: With Miss Nora gone, I'd say your chances of winning the fight have increased, but I'd still keep my eyes on those Blighters if I were you.

speaker: Evie
en: This borough is ours for the taking!

speaker: Frye
en: Fight!

speaker: Nora
en: All right! Step aside, you louts!

speaker: Frye
en: Ladies and gentlemen! We are Evie and Jacob Frye! And as of this moment, you all work, for us!

speaker: Messenger
en: Mister Cletus Strain and the Blighters have challenged the Rooks to a fight for territory in Lambeth. Defeat him and the borough is yours. Look sharp, he's a bit sadistic.

speaker: Evie
en: We will win the fight for Lambeth!

speaker: Jacob
en: Down with the Blighters!

speaker: Strain
en: Here we go round the mulberry bush/So early in the morning!

speaker: Evie
en: Ladies and gentlemen! We are Evie and Jacob Frye! And as of this moment, you all work for us!

speaker: Messenger
en: Miss Plumb has, although reluctantly, accepted your challenge. All weapons permitted. May the strongest brutes win.

speaker: Messenger
en: Miss Plumb is no longer head of the Southwark Blighters, and they go into this fight leaderless. Rooks have good odds.

speaker: Evie
en: Rooks! Southwark belongs to you!

speaker: Jacob
en: Show the Blighters who owns this borough!

speaker: Plumb
en: You... butchered my friends... And now I will butcher you!

speaker: Evie
en: Ladies and gentlemen! We are Evie and Jacob Frye! And as of this moment, you all work, for us!

speaker: Messenger
en: Mister Lynch has agreed to your terms. In exchange, he will be fighting with electrochemical bombs. He sends his highest regards and encourages you to bring your bravery.

speaker: Messenger
en: I hear you've dealt with Mr. Lynch on your own terms. Now all that stands between you and the Strand are his ever-loyal cronies. Good luck.

speaker: Evie
en: This borough is ours for the taking!

speaker: Frye
en: Down with the Blighters!

speaker: Lynch
en: Now to blow you to smithereens.

speaker: Frye
en: Ladies and gentlemen! We are Evie and Jacob Frye! And as of this moment, you all work, for us!

speaker: Messenger
en: Miss Swinebourne has agreed to your terms. Everything is permitted in this gang fight. The wager is ownership of the Thames. Good luck.

speaker: Messenger
en: The Rooks are in good standing, with Miss Swinebourne no longer leading the Thames Blighters. Good luck to both sides.

speaker: Evie
en: Show the Blighters who owns this borough!

speaker: Jacob
en: The city belongs to the Rooks!

speaker: Swinebourne
en: Outta the way!

speaker: Evie
en: Ladies and gentlemen! We are Evie and Jacob Frye! And as of this moment, you all work, for us!

speaker: Messenger
en: Miss Graves, known in London as "the Bludger", accepts the terms to this gang war. The fight shall permit the use of all weapons. May the best gang emerge victorious.

speaker: Messenger
en: I always knew the Rooks were strong, but I didn't think you stood a chance against The Bludger! There isn't much standing in your way now.

speaker: Evie
en: Westminster is ours for the taking!

speaker: Graves
en: You ain't gonna take me down!

speaker: Evie
en: Ladies and gentlemen! We are Evie and Jacob Frye! And as of this moment, you all work, for us!

speaker: Henry
en: Ah, there you are! All that stands between you and Whitechapel is the villain controlling the borough. Kaylock has demanded you settle the claim for territory in a gang fight.

speaker: Jacob
en: His loss.

speaker: Henry
en: Here. I'm sure you can put this to better use than I can.

speaker: Jacob
en: What's this Greenie, Assassin Christmas?

speaker: Henry
en: Gather your allies.

speaker: Messenger
en: Mr. Rexford Kaylock has agreed to your terms, and waits for you at the Whitechapel train station. He's bet his train on the fight.

speaker: Jacob
en: No Kaylock? Hmm... No matter.

speaker: Evie
en: Where are you, Kaylock? Perhaps this will draw you out...

speaker: Kaylock
en: Ah! There you are!

speaker: Evie
en: It appears to be broken.

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh well, at least we have a train now, it's not all bad.

speaker: Jacob
en: Kaylock is dead! Whitechapel is no longer in the hands of the Blighters!

speaker: Evie
en: You now have the chance to join our ranks! We welcome all who would stand up to Starrick and his cutthroats!

speaker: Jacob
en: Welcome to the Rooks!

speaker: Agnes
en: Ah, ya bastard. I'd rather throw me'sel to the tracks, than to run Bertha another mile fer that doaty bawbag.

speaker: Jacob
en: Kaylock? He's left the station.

speaker: Agnes
en: Well! Hallo, fancy pants! And who might you two be?

speaker: Evie
en: I'm Evie Frye and this is my brother, Jacob Frye.

speaker: Agnes
en: Pleased to meet ye. I'm Agnes MacBean.

speaker: Jacob
en: A delight.

speaker: Agnes
en: I thought I was gettin' a promotion. I suppose I'm out of work now.

speaker: Evie
en: Come work for us instead.

speaker: Agnes
en: Awa an bile yer heid (away and boil you head)! You pay better than scraps?

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm sure we can at least manage that.

speaker: Agnes
en: Then may I present to you Agnes and Bertha. Lady and locomotive, at your service. I'll be in the next car.

speaker: Henry
en: A hideout on the rails! What an excellent idea.

speaker: Evie
en: Yes, it all worked out rather well. Now, I would like to follow up a lead on

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob, this is serious.

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm not doing anything until this gets fixed.

speaker: Henry
en: I believe I know someone who can help with that.

speaker: Jacob
en: I knew you would, Greenie.

speaker: Agnes
en: You know, a mite o' money goes a mickle bit in this city. Think o' the power o' good you can do with the purse you bring!

speaker: Agnes
en: You talk of restoring London? Well, now's your chance. That there map shows who to speak to - old friends, if you will. Give 'em a wiff o' that sterling and maybe you can save us all from having to lay down our knife and fork afore we're ready!

speaker: Agnes
en: Now, enough shoptalk... Believe Mr. Green said there was someone he wanted you to meet?

speaker: Scrivens
en: Are we all set? The shipment should be arriving any minute now. I want this to go as smoothly as possible. Keep your wits about you, we don't want the police sticking their noses where they don't belong. And sure as the sky is grey in London, I know what you schemers are like. Keep your fingers to yourselves. This shipment is mine. I will take inventory with great scrutiny. So mind your desires. We will bring in coin with this new shipment of... goods.

speaker: Tess
en: That Mister Scrivens has another thing coming.

speaker: Margie
en: Oh, what d'you mean, Tess?

speaker: Tess
en: I mean, look at him, Margie! Never seen a thug dressed so well nor glow so much in me life! Whatever shipments he's bringing in these days is also bringing in a lot of money.

speaker: Scrivens
en: What in God's name! Get off me, you! Leave me alone!

speaker: Jacob
en: Now, now, Mister Scrivens. Keep quiet.

speaker: Scrivens
en: This is none of your business. Piss off!

speaker: Jacob
en: Your criminal activity has made it my business.

speaker: Scrivens
en: What criminal activity? Can't a fellow stand about the docks with his workers and wait for a shipment to come in?

speaker: Jacob
en: A shipment of narcotics? I think not.

speaker: Scrivens
en: What in God's name! Get off me, you! Leave me alone!

speaker: Evie
en: Be quiet, would you? Shhh.

speaker: Scrivens
en: Can't a man do his work without being interrupted?

speaker: Evie
en: Maybe, if that man's work didn't also involve the police.

speaker: Scrivens
en: What exactly has the police involved?

speaker: Evie
en: Does shipping and selling narcotics sound familiar?

speaker: Scrivens
en: Not this time! Help! A strange man is after me! Ha! Too slow! A strange woman is after me, help!

speaker: Scrivens
en: No! Let me go, I say!

speaker: Jacob
en: Come along, Mister Scrivens.

speaker: Scrivens
en: Let me go! I said, let me go!

speaker: Evie
en: Come along now, Mister Scrivens.

speaker: Scrivens
en: Help! I'm trapped! Somebody help me!

speaker: Abberline
en: Thank you, friend.

speaker: Fowler
en: Spread out! There has to be a weak spot somewhere. Find it! Then, we break in and burn everything! If the government won't help people like us to read, then no one shall read at all!

speaker: Fowler
en: Oi! What do you think you're doing?! I'm busy here!

speaker: Jacob
en: Hush, Mister Fowler. Quiet down.

speaker: Fowler
en: What in God's name was that for?

speaker: Jacob
en: Spying on another print house, are we?

speaker: Fowler
en: Was not! All right, maybe I was. But I'm tired of everyone getting what they want, besides me. Nobody ever asked ol' Gilbert what he wanted.

speaker: Jacob
en: Save it for the sergeant, Fowler.

speaker: Fowler
en: Oi! What do you think you're doing?! I'm busy here!

speaker: Evie
en: Keep quiet, Mister Fowler. Hush, now.

speaker: Fowler
en: Oh, let me go, will you?

speaker: Evie
en: Apologies, but the sergeant wants a word.

speaker: Fowler
en: It's about burning down print houses, I know. It was a terrible idea. I should never have done it, but I'm just so angry. I'm so angry and I want everyone to feel as angry as I do.

speaker: Evie
en: The world doesn't need more anger in it, Mister Fowler.

speaker: Fowler
en: Ha! I'm free! I'm being pursued! Help! Yes! Freedom! Oi! A little help over here?

speaker: Fowler
en: Oh, come now! Please let me go!

speaker: Jacob
en: Now where were we?

speaker: Fowler
en: No! Please, miss. Let me go free.

speaker: Evie
en: You were saying?

speaker: Fowler
en: Someone get me out of here!

speaker: Abberline
en: Good. Thank you. One less building burnt to ashes.

speaker: Duleep
en: I've discovered more information on our stolen gold. To my carriage.

speaker: Duleep
en: It's all quite strange: the British Indies Company working with the Templar Order. And for what? Perhaps we will never know. The accountant revealed they're hiding a shipment of gold, previously stolen from India, in a carriage at an old Starrick warehouse. We must find this carriage and steal it from them.

speaker: Jacob
en: And what will you be doing in the meantime?

speaker: Evie
en: And what of you?

speaker: Duleep
en: Why, I'm here to help you of course! They don't call me the fourth best shot in London for nothing!

speaker: Jacob
en: I need to find this gold.

speaker: Evie
en: The gold must be found.

speaker: Duleep
en: This is it, the gold is here somewhere. Return to me once you've found it, and I'll stay behind and keep an eye out for trouble. Be careful. What they think is theirs they won't easily part with.

speaker: Jacob
en: Maybe this warehouse holds the answers.

speaker: Evie
en: This is where the gold is located.

speaker: Templar 1
en: Don't they have enough men over there, keeping things quiet?

speaker: Templar 2
en: It's a big job keeping the colony in check. That's why they've got our help from this side of the pond.

speaker: Templar 1
en: Well I'm glad I'm not in India. Sounds like a jungle of a place.

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: This is it. The gold must be inside. Now to sneak it out of here.

speaker: Templar 3
en: What does he want with all this gold anyway?

speaker: Templar 4
en: We must take it. There will be trouble otherwise.

speaker: Templar 3
en: I'm afraid I don't quite get your meaning.

speaker: Templar 4
en: I mean, if we leave the money overseas with those brutes, who knows what they'll do. The Empire can't afford another riot.

speaker: Templar 5
en: We've got ourselves a rat! Thief! Stop them!

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: I need to get back to Mister Singh.

speaker: Duleep
en: Good. The Templars are not far away and we must lose them! I'll keep the wolves at bay.

speaker: Jacob
en: Are you sure?

speaker: Evie
en: Your highness

speaker: Duleep
en: Hurry, go!

speaker: Jacob
en: I need to lose those Templars.

speaker: Evie
en: I must get rid of these pursuers.

speaker: Jacob
en: Faster!

speaker: Evie
en: Make haste!

speaker: Duleep
en: Damn! My gun is jammed.

speaker: Jacob
en: Leave it to me. You take the reigns!

speaker: Evie
en: Take my place!

speaker: Duleep
en: I get the feeling you've done this before.

speaker: Duleep
en: Here. Take these, I have no use for these bullets now.

speaker: Duleep
en: I think we lost them. Good work.

speaker: Jacob
en: You were quite the hero out there!

speaker: Evie
en: You were quite impressive out there, if I may say.

speaker: Duleep
en: You're too kind. It was rather exhilarating, if I'm being honest... Now, I've hired a captain to escort the gold overseas. If you would kindly fetch the crate from the back.

speaker: Templar 6
en: You can't get away that easily, thief!

speaker: Duleep
en: Are you quite alright? You had me frightened.

speaker: Jacob
en: Nothing to worry about, your highness.

speaker: Evie
en: I'm all right. Really.

speaker: Duleep
en: I commend you for fighting them off. Really. With you at my side, it will be an almost simple task to send this gold back to where it belongs. Why don't you walk off that last fight, and come back to me when you are ready for the next leg of the journey. There's still work to be done.

speaker: Jacob
en: So, what's next, your greatness?

speaker: Evie
en: Where were we?

speaker: Duleep
en: We must return this gold to its people... My people... I've procured us a captain to transport it to its destination. But our next feat will be to get it out of London.

speaker: Jacob
en: And now it's up to you and me to protect it. Fancy that.

speaker: Evie
en: And we must protect it.

speaker: Duleep
en: Precisely. Now, if you would be so good as to bring the gold aboard, we can get going. Come aboard. It's time to leave. We have the gold, and now we must go. Climb aboard.

speaker: Captain
en: Off we go!

speaker: Duleep
en: I knew we wouldn't get far without another appearance from them. Look out!

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm on it!

speaker: Evie
en: Stand back!

speaker: Duleep
en: No. We're in this together.

speaker: Templar
en: Sink them! Don't let them get away with that cargo!

speaker: Captain
en: The engine's stalled! I'll need some time to fix it!

speaker: Duleep
en: The Templars are aboard the ship!

speaker: Jacob
en: They're trying to sink the boat! I must defend the back of the boat!

speaker: Evie
en: They're trying to sink the boat! I must head to the back! The Templars are inflicting serious damage!

speaker: Duleep
en: They're at the bow!

speaker: Jacob
en: Talk about high security.

speaker: Evie
en: They certainly put a strong effort into protecting this gold.

speaker: Duleep
en: How splendid! That should buy our captain enough time.

speaker: Duleep
en: Now we must escort this boat to the next dock where we may disembark. And then this vessel will be clear of enemy waters! We've done some good today. I can feel it.

speaker: Jacob
en: All part of the job.

speaker: Evie
en: I'm glad you feel that way, your highness.

speaker: Jacob
en: Let's see if I can take them out without them noticing.

speaker: Evie
en: We're not finished yet.
