speaker: Duleep
en: I think that's the last of them... The gold is in safe hands. We did a good job today. May this not be the end of our adventures together.

speaker: Jacob
en: It would be a shame to part ways now.

speaker: Evie
en: No, let us not end this partnership just yet.

speaker: Duleep
en: We can only move forward from here! Good day.

speaker: Jacob
en: You

speaker: Evie
en: Your highness

speaker: Duleep
en: They are stubborn fellows, aren't they?... Now, if you would be so kind as to excuse me. I've had quite a bit of excitement today and must think on it. Do come see me again.

speaker: Henry
en: Your attempts to influence parliament for the Indian cause have failed. You must do more!

speaker: Duleep
en: I will not jeopardize my relationship with Queen and country to satisfy your crusade.

speaker: Henry
en: Your highness, you belong to India, not here acting the part of the noble foreigner!

speaker: Duleep
en: I have wasted enough time indulging in this nonsense.

speaker: Henry
en: If your mother could see you now, the last Maharajah of Punjab, basking inside his golden cage...

speaker: Duleep
en: How dare you.

speaker: Jacob
en: I always recommend bringing someone's mother into the argument.

speaker: Henry
en: If he doesn't help his people, he will regret it forever.

speaker: Evie
en: How may we help?

speaker: Henry
en: Will you talk to him? He won't listen to me.

speaker: Evie
en: We will do our best.

speaker: Thomas
en: Your highness, you have guests.

speaker: Duleep
en: I suppose Mister Green sent you.

speaker: Jacob
en: Bringing up your mother was

speaker: Evie
en: Impolite and he was wrong to do so. We'd like to rectify the situation.

speaker: Duleep
en: Then humour me, and join me in a shooting game. None of these people have any sense of enjoyment, and I am bored to death.

speaker: Ellsworth
en: A shooting game? Singh, you haven't changed at all.

speaker: Duleep
en: Ellsworth? My word, how good it is to see you! The mother country has treated you well. Jacob and Evie Frye, this is Brinley Ellsworth. A friend from a past life.

speaker: Ellsworth
en: You've made new friends, I see.

speaker: Duleep
en: What brings you to this part of the Empire?

speaker: Ellsworth
en: Ah, company business, unfortunately. But I could not resist the chance of seeing you again, it's been far too long. I've heard nobody throws a party better than my dearest friend. I am eager to see if your reputation overseas holds any truth.

speaker: Duleep
en: My servant, Thomas, will be scoring the game. Acquire the most amount of points by shooting the bottles in front of you. Each bottle is worth one point. You have thirty seconds. May the best shot win. Start the timer.

speaker: Thomas
en: A perfect score! Nine points!

speaker: Duleep
en: Come, Thomas! This isn't enough of a challenge. Let's shorten the timer.

speaker: Thomas
en: Round two will now commence. Try and do as well, if not better, within a twenty second time limit. Timer at the ready... Begin.

speaker: Thomas
en: Time's up! Nine rounds shot, eight points won!

speaker: Ellsworth
en: Singh you have quite an opponent.

speaker: Thomas
en: Your turn, your highness.

speaker: Ellsworth
en: Come, let us see if you are better with a gun than you were with a slingshot.

speaker: Duleep
en: Allow me.

speaker: Ellsworth
en: Impressive! I am in awe, Singh! What they say of you is true!

speaker: Duleep
en: What on earth?

speaker: Thomas
en: Sir, I believe I heard a second shot.

speaker: Duleep
en: He's right. That sounded like a second gunshot. Strange.

speaker: Jacob
en: Strange, indeed. Let me investigate.

speaker: Evie
en: Let me see what I can find out.

speaker: Duleep
en: I'm sure it wasn't anything serious. Don't bother.

speaker: Evie
en: Looks like Lady Owers' thugs have taken over the place.

speaker: Thug
en: Right, you tight slugs, shake a leg! First man puts a bullet in Miss Frye gets to spend a full hour wit' one a Lady O's 'beauties'... If you lot likes all the nice jam we gets free 'round here, cut off Miss Frye's head for Lady O.

speaker: Evie
en: You're safe now.

speaker: Leader
en: Get down here you whore-lover! I'm going to skin you alive!

speaker: Nellie
en: We shan't forget what you done fer us, Miss Evie. Us girls'll breathe a bit easier without those bastards controllin' our lives.

speaker: Duleep
en: You look terrible.

speaker: Evie
en: And you're late.

speaker: Jacob
en: Me? Never! I was simply retrieving the information you sent me to get. It was easy, really... Something about an event happening tonight at the Tower of London?

speaker: Duleep
en: The Gala? I will be attending.

speaker: Jacob
en: You're our in then.

speaker: Evie
en: We can't just barge in and steal the crown jewels.

speaker: Duleep
en: She's right, we need a plan.

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, bother.

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob, you can escort Mister Singh to tonight's event. This will give you a chance to slip away from the party and find the Koh-i-Noor. I will take care of the guards around the perimeter. Meet me at the top of the White Tower.

speaker: Jacob
en: Good! Another chance to wear the suit!

speaker: Evie
en: No weapons allowed.

speaker: Jacob
en: Where's the fun in that?!

speaker: Jacob
en: I should find Singh...

speaker: Duleep
en: The jewels are being held upstairs. But be careful, if this isn't one of the most heavily guarded places, then I'm a true Englishman!

speaker: Jacob
en: I may need your help to distract these guards.

speaker: Duleep
en: Just give me the signal.

speaker: Jacob
en: I should send a signal to Singh to distract the guards. I need Singh to distract those guards.

speaker: Duleep
en: Oh I do believe I've lost a button. Will somebody help me find it? Will you tell me, kind sir, where the lavatory is exactly?

speaker: Jacob
en: The diamond is on the second floor... It's awfully quiet up here.

speaker: Jacob
en: Guard's asleep. Wonder what's inside that crate...

speaker: Jacob
en: Someone got here before I did. Well, if the diamond's not here, I've got to find it before it leaves the building... If it hasn't already. Where could it have gone?

speaker: Templar 1
en: This plan was genius. We'll get him this time.

speaker: Templar 2
en: Friends with the Queen, pah! She won't be friends with him when she finds the diamond is in his pocket!

speaker: Templar 1
en: He'll never see it coming!

speaker: Templar 2
en: Once he tries to walk out that door, he'll kiss his royal title goodbye

speaker: Templar 1
en: And henceforth be known as prisoner Singh!

speaker: Jacob
en: They planted the diamond on Duleep? Not good. I need to lift the diamond from Singh's pocket. Subtlety isn't my strong suit.

speaker: Victoria
en: Oh, your friend is as charming as you are, Mister Singh.

speaker: Brinley
en: You flatter me, ma'am.

speaker: Victoria
en: Now, do tell me. How do you two know each other?

speaker: Duleep
en: We met at the missionary compound in Fategarh, your majesty. The Logins were quite fond of the Ellsworths.

speaker: Brinley
en: Mister Singh and I were quite close, your ladyship. It was a lonely time on foreign soil for me. I was more than happy to have a friend.

speaker: Victoria
en: I'm sure. And now the Company has sent you here on urgent business.

speaker: Brinley
en: I wish I could disclose the information, your ladyship. But alas, I cannot. I'm sure you will learn of it soon enough.

speaker: Jacob
en: Now to find my sister.

speaker: Evie
en: Now to reach the White Tower...

speaker: Evie
en: The place is crawling with Templars! I've got to secure the perimeter.

speaker: Evie
en: What took you so long?

speaker: Jacob
en: Bit of a mishap. Here it is.

speaker: Evie
en: What happened?

speaker: Jacob
en: Somebody stole it first. The safe had been robbed by the time I got there.

speaker: Evie
en: The British Indies Company will stop at nothing.

speaker: Jacob
en: There was a plan to frame Singh. I lifted it from him before the royal guards found it. Imagine the look on her Majesty's face if

speaker: Evie
en: They must know by now that their plan was foiled.

speaker: Jacob
en: You're welcome.

speaker: Evie
en: I think it's time to depart.

speaker: Evie
en: I need to find a way out of here. I hope they make it out all right.

speaker: Duleep
en: Did you get it to your sister?

speaker: Jacob
en: Just barely.

speaker: Duleep
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Jacob
en: I'll tell you about it another time.

speaker: Duleep
en: You encountered some trouble?

speaker: Jacob
en: We can't speak of this here. The British Indies Company is up to no good again.

speaker: Duleep
en: Outside, then.

speaker: Royal guard 1
en: You, sir. Halt for inspection.

speaker: Duleep
en: I beg your pardon.

speaker: Royal guard 1
en: Search him.

speaker: Royal guard 2
en: Nothing. The Koh-i-Noor isn't here.

speaker: Duleep
en: Of course there is nothing! What do you take me for, some sort of criminal?

speaker: Victoria
en: What was all that commotion about, Mister Singh?

speaker: Duleep
en: I do believe they thought I was trying to pinch the Koh-i-Noor, your ladyship.

speaker: Victoria
en: Ha! The Koh-i-Noor? Who on earth would want to steal that potato? Goodnight, your highness.

speaker: Jacob
en: We barely got out of there in one piece. The British Indies Company tried to plant the diamond on you and frame you for stealing it. Luckily, I was there just in the nick of time.

speaker: Duleep
en: We need to meet back at Mister Green's shop. I must see the diamond with my own two eyes.

speaker: Henry
en: The Koh-i-Noor! If I may?

speaker: Duleep
en: Glass?

speaker: Henry
en: The real Koh-i-Noor never left India. Had I known you planned to reclaim it, I would have stopped you. My father ensured it never fell into Templar hands.

speaker: Duleep
en: Your father, he has done a great service to me and my people.

speaker: Henry
en: My words to you earlier were unfair

speaker: Duleep
en: You were not wrong. I, too, have grown frustrated with my lack of progress. Shall we let bygones be bygones?

speaker: Evie
en: We need to find out who is behind all of this. And why have the Templars and the British Indies Company joined forces?

speaker: Jacob
en: What we should do is track them down and destroy their headquarters.

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob

speaker: Duleep
en: That... may not be such a terrible idea, Mister Frye.

speaker: Drake
en: How many crates do we have left to distribute?

speaker: Accomplice
en: Only about a dozen, Sir.

speaker: Drake
en: Good. Soon all of London's Blighters will be armed to the teeth.

speaker: Accomplice
en: No bobbies in sight.

speaker: Drake
en: Good. Distribute the dynamite then, and carefully.

speaker: Accomplice
en: Very good, Sir.

speaker: Drake
en: We want this to come into the Blighters' hands without harm. No mishaps.

speaker: Harley
en: Beg pardon? Unhand me, rascal! I said, let me go!

speaker: Jacob
en: Quiet down. That's enough out of you, Harley.

speaker: Harley
en: How do you know me? Rumors? The scandal sheets?

speaker: Jacob
en: Your fame reaches beyond scandal sheets, sir.

speaker: Harley
en: How's that?

speaker: Jacob
en: I read about you in the police files.

speaker: Harley
en: They're wrong! I'm an honorable man! I serve the interests of our Father!

speaker: Jacob
en: Save your excuses for the police.

speaker: Harley
en: Beg pardon? Unhand me, rascal! I said, let me go!

speaker: Evie
en: Keep your voice down. Quiet, Mister Harley.

speaker: Harley
en: Who sent you, woman?

speaker: Evie
en: The police.

speaker: Harley
en: Pah! Why would any sane person want to apprehend me! I do what I do for the greater good! This Abbey will not stand! Religion will be purified again!

speaker: Evie
en: And we're the ones putting an end to it.

speaker: Harley
en: Just try and catch me now! Nincompoop! I need some help here!

speaker: Harley
en: Ha! Too slow! I need some help here!

speaker: Harley
en: Damnit!

speaker: Jacob
en: You were saying?

speaker: Harley
en: Let me go!

speaker: Evie
en: Now, now Mister Harley.

speaker: Harley
en: Help! I'm trapped! Someone help me!

speaker: Abberline
en: Something out of a nightmare, that one. You did well.

speaker: Hughes
en: Don't let those crooks get the better of you. My rates are right fair. Did the Bank refuse you a loan? I'll take good care of you. I'm working class, same as you. I know the bank demands high interest rates. That's why I became a money lender!

speaker: Blighter
en: Harvey, we got 'im!

speaker: Man
en: I promise, I'll pay. Please, let me go!

speaker: Hughes
en: Oi! Get your hands off me! Who are you? You ain't some bobby, right?

speaker: Jacob
en: Quiet, you.

speaker: Hughes
en: I was just working, mate.

speaker: Jacob
en: Is that so?

speaker: Hughes
en: There's nothing illegal about what I'm doing. I've got the right to lend money!

speaker: Jacob
en: And rob people with interest?

speaker: Hughes
en: Oi! Get your hands off me! Who are you? You ain't some bobby, right?

speaker: Evie
en: Hush now, no need for a fuss. I said quiet.

speaker: Hughes
en: There's nothing illegal about what I'm doing!

speaker: Evie
en: Why are you wanted by every bobby division in the city?

speaker: Hughes
en: It's their own fault for using my services unwisely.

speaker: Evie
en: Your "services" have landed more people in the poorhouse than not!

speaker: Hughes
en: Leave me alone! Help! Someone! This man's after me! Help! Get 'er off me!

speaker: Hughes
en: Hey, you need money? I can help you out!

speaker: Jacob
en: Settle down.

speaker: Hughes
en: Not you again!

speaker: Evie
en: Now now, Mister Hughes. It's not the time to play hide-and-seek.

speaker: Hughes
en: Someone! Anyone! Help!

speaker: Abberline
en: Thank you so much!

speaker: Abberline
en: What good will he do me dead?

speaker: Dickens
en: There's been a spate of rather intriguing thefts about town recently.

speaker: Jacob
en: Robberies? In London? I never thought I'd see the day!

speaker: Evie
en: Robberies in London are hardly supernatural events.

speaker: Dickens
en: They looked like common robberies at first, but these perpetrators have all claimed to have been under the influence of some supernatural power. I'm not so foolish as to forget that criminals will spin any yarn to avoid the law. However, these thieves all proffer the same defense: they say they were being controlled by a demon. Will you make some inquiries? One of our demon-possessed mobsmen is being held behind bars at this very moment. You may want to begin your search there.

speaker: Jacob
en: What's this one in for?

speaker: Evie
en: What's that man done?

speaker: Policeman
en: Robbed the pawnbroker's down the road.

speaker: Criminal
en: A demon made me do it! I can't remember much. That's what's so queer. I've never stolen anything in my life before!

speaker: Jacob
en: Who do you think made you do this?

speaker: Criminal
en: All I can recall is a silver watch, swinging in mid-air. It was held by someone, - or some thing! A dark presence whispering. I could only see its eyes. A demon!

speaker: Jacob
en: Maybe the shopkeeper will make more sense.

speaker: Criminal
en: A demon made me do it! I can't remember much. That's what's so queer. I've never stolen anything in my life before!

speaker: Evie
en: Let's pretend that I believe you. Tell me who made you do it.

speaker: Criminal
en: All I can recall is a silver watch, swinging in mid-air. It was held by someone, - or some thing! A dark presence whispering. I could only see its eyes. A demon!

speaker: Evie
en: I'll need to verify this with the shopkeeper.

speaker: Jacob
en: May I ask you about the robbery?

speaker: Evie
en: What can you tell me about the robbery?

speaker: Owner
en: There's not much to say. Most of the items did come from the same seller. Enzio Capelli, sorcerer supreme, a famous showman, from Italy. Several weeks ago he was forced to pawn his family heirlooms. Debts. I have address of the last person who redeemed something of his. A lovely pearl necklace. That helpful?

speaker: Owner
en: Not again! Stop her! Stop! Somebody stop that thief!

speaker: Thief 1
en: Where am I? What's happening?

speaker: Jacob
en: You were just indulging in a little light theft.

speaker: Thief 1
en: It's all very hazy but - I remember something silver flashing in front of my eyes. Then I heard a sort of bell. Next thing I know, I'm here with you.

speaker: Jacob
en: Back on track. Now to find this buyer.

speaker: Thief 1
en: Where am I? What's happening?

speaker: Evie
en: You took something from a pawn shop.

speaker: Thief 1
en: It's all very hazy but - I remember something silver flashing in front of my eyes. Then I heard a sort of bell. Next thing I know, I'm here with you.

speaker: Evie
en: My only lead is this mysterious buyer.

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed

speaker: Jack
en: Welcome to the reunion, Miss Frye!

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Jack
en: There is a sickness in this world, Miss Frye. It made our creed weak. But I am here now. I will tear into all sickness, all the rot and shit of this city and rip it out. We shall be pure again. The Assassins shall rise and we shall rule.

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Jack
en: Do you think you can kill me that way? Try something else perhaps? That's useless... Pathetic. Don't make me laugh. Is that intended to scare me?

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Evie
en: No use! I need to try a different approach! I'm getting nowhere...I should flee and try sneaking up on him. I can't overpower him! I need to get behind him...

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Jack
en: I lose patience with your child's play. Cowering in the shadows, Miss Frye? Jacob thought he could hide from me too... Hiding are we? Ha! I learned all your tricks from your brother, Assassin! This is my time now. Jacob's is done and you must choose... Are you cat or mouse, Miss Frye? The people must fear us, and you know it! I've seen you wield your tools of terror, you're just like me... Do you see the truth your brother did not? Are we not the same you and I? Mine is the face of the true Creed! Will you join me? Or must I rip out your vitals and send them to your beloved inspector? As cowardly and inept as your twin... Come out, Sister, join Jack... See, Jacob?! Your noble sister has come to die for you! I will cut her like the others and display her innards for the world to see! For you, Jacob! Still think you can hide from me?

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Evie
en: What?

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Jack
en: Jack the Ripper cannot die! That woman thinks you're mad! Free yourselves! Kill that madwoman!

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Evie
en: I know you blame Jacob for your mother's death, but nothing can excuse the horrors you've committed... Jacob was like a father to you, Jack... You have betrayed his trust, and sullied the Creed.

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Jack
en: Show me your monster, Assassin. These lambs need slaughtering. You are weak, Assassin. ...a relic just like your precious Creed.... Cower before the new face of the Assassins. My legend will live forever. You cannot kill the Ripper. I will haunt men through time...

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Evie
en: I am not a monster! You will not make a monster of me.

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Jack
en: We are the same you and I...

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Evie
en: Oh, Jack... You were an Assassin, yes, but we are not the same. And that is why your memory must be erased for all time. Rest in peace now, Jack, you and your twisted acolytes.

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Evie
en: Jacob.

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Abberline
en: Miss Frye, what the hell happened here?

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Evie
en: Nothing, Inspector. Nothing happened here. Trust me, Jack the Ripper is dead.

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Officer
en: Inspector!

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Evie
en: Now help me, Frederick. No one must ever know that Jack the Ripper was an Assassin.

speaker: Officer
en: Inspector! The journalists are here.

scene: Live by the Creed, Die by the Creed
speaker: Abberline
en: I want those vultures gone this instant, is that clear.

en: I'll find her. I promise.

speaker: Evie

speaker: Nellie
en: Miss Evie! Thank god you're here. Save me friend, Miss Evie, I'm beggin' you -- she's nothin' but another 'whore' gone missing to the rest of 'em... Miss Evie, 'tis god-awful. They bashed her over the head and carried her off. She's one of us, you see.

speaker: Evie
en: I'll find her. I promise.

speaker: Prostitute
en: I don' want to die! Help me! Help! Over here! Save me! Here! Over here! Help! Someone please help!

speaker: Evie
en: You're safe now.

speaker: Prostitute
en: I can only repay you with my heartfelt thanks, Miss Frye.

speaker: Blake
en: “There's work to be done in this ever-growing city and not enough hands to do it. The 1830s saw the end of child labor but I say we bring it back! Now listen closely and hear me out before you start throwing tomatoes. We live in the most advanced society in the world with every country looking to surpass us. Shall we slow our progress and fall behind? No! This is the time for England to rise above the rest. If we bring back child labor, we bring back production. With children we get things done faster and cheaper. And it will make men out of your sons. If you're interested in our cause, come see me, Louis Blake, and sign your child up today! Help keep London ahead of the rest of the world!”

Let us demand the closure of all wicked houses of sin and impurity in our city. We shall petition our most gracious majesty, Queen Victoria. But what if our petition falls on deaf ears? en: Your Majesty, may I present Miss Evie Frye.

speaker: Queen Victoria
en: You are the one responsible for Mr. Gladstone's mishap?

speaker: Evie
en: Your Majesty, I apologize

speaker: Queen Victoria
en: The cake is particularly good. Enjoy the ball.

speaker: Evie
en: I really must be going.

speaker: Starrick
en: Miss Frye... may I have this dance?

speaker: Evie
en: Mr. Starrick, you've had your fun, but the game is over.

speaker: Starrick
en: Ah. Listen. One, two, three. One, two, three.

speaker: Starrick
en: Time is a wonderful thing, Miss Frye. It heals all wounds. We may make mistakes while dancing, but, the mazurka ends and then we begin again. Problem is everyone forgets. They trip on the same mistakes over and over.

speaker: Evie
en: People can learn.

speaker: Starrick
en: Can they? Isn't everyone around you repeating the same steps? But if one man could remember the dance? Could know the time? Then he could change things for the better.

speaker: Evie
en: I have had enough

speaker: Starrick
en: This dance is nearly over. Soon the people will forget the generation on this terrace, the ruin you nearly wrought on London. When this music ceases, Miss Frye, your time is up – and mine begins.

speaker: Jacob
en: Freddy!

speaker: Abberline
en: Starrick peppered the regulars with his own men and took several guards hostage. Your weapons are in there.

speaker: Abberline
en: Look.

speaker: Jacob
en: Right. I'll kill the impostors and rescue the captives.

speaker: Abberline
en: How? It's impossible to tell the difference.

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh ye of little faith.

speaker: Jacob
en: Now, to find the real royal guards. Ooh. Dancing. And with Starrick, no less. How awkward that must be.

speaker: Templar
en: Keep your eyes open!

speaker: Jacob
en: I'll get you out.

speaker: Guards
en: Thank you, sir. Thanks, mate!

speaker: Templar
en: The day shall be ours!

speaker: Jacob
en: Hold still for a moment.

speaker: Guards
en: You have my thanks! Thanks, mate!

speaker: Evie
en: The key to the waltz is one must lead with one's right foot.

speaker: Woman
en: Oh my!

speaker: Man
en: Everything all right, my dear?

speaker: Woman
en: Do you require assistance?

speaker: Evie
en: I never liked balls.

speaker: Evie
en: Here. The location of the vault. Go!

speaker: Jacob
en: Just like that? No plan?

speaker: Evie
en: No time for plans. I'll catch up as soon as I'm rid of this infernal contraption.

speaker: Jacob
en: What—what are you doing?

speaker: Starrick
en: Exploiting. I warned you, my boy. But you do not listen.

speaker: Evie
en: Requiescat in pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob!

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob, resist him! You're a monster! You don't know how to use the artifact!

speaker: Jacob
en: Evie! Stay back.

speaker: Starrick
en: London will soon be rid of your chaos! This city was a safe harbor, a light for all humanity. What alternatives do you propose? Bedlam?

speaker: Jacob
en: After Starrick! Don't worry about me. Leave me, stop Starrick.

speaker: Evie
en: The Shroud was never meant for you!

speaker: Starrick
en: You would rather destroy the fabric of society!

speaker: Evie
en: Mr. Starrick! You forgot to escort me home.

speaker: Starrick
en: Let me rectify my mistake!

speaker: Starrick
en: Another Frye to feed on! First you will fall, then the Queen! I will begin again. And this new London shall be even more magnificent.

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob, be careful!

speaker: Jacob
en: Evie, I'm coming! Don't die! I will find your weakness! Evie! Hold on!

speaker: Starrick
en: I admire your pluck, but there is little you can accomplish now. Like Jesus himself, I am immortal. Behold the power of the Shroud!

speaker: Evie
en: Jesus... wore... it better. Starrick cannot escape. I'll recover. Fight on without me! Starrick must fall. Not me. Face him!

speaker: Starrick
en: Come closer, my boy. We shall be fast friends!

speaker: Starrick
en: London deserves a ruler who will remain vigilant, who will prevent the city from devolving into chaos.

speaker: Evie
en: Chaos that you are about to cause!

speaker: Starrick
en: You two have generated quite enough on your own already!

speaker: Evie
en: And we've mended it!

speaker: Jacob
en: We did?

speaker: Evie
en: We did.

speaker: Starrick
en: No amount of planning or might shall beat me. I have history on my side.

speaker: Starrick
en: Get. Out. Of. My. City.

speaker: Henry
en: Evie!

speaker: Jacob
en: You cannot maintain this! We have you against the wall, Starrick! You're trapped! You're weakening! Starrick, your end is near! Starrick, your reign is nearly over.

speaker: Starrick
en: It has barely begun.

speaker: Evie
en: Henry!

speaker: Jacob
en: Die, old man.

speaker: Starrick
en: After you.

speaker: Evie
en: The Shroud will not protect you!

speaker: Starrick
en: You're wrong! The people of this city, my people, shall supply its energy!

speaker: Evie
en: This city is bigger than you will ever be!

speaker: Starrick
en: Surrender while you still can, girl!

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob!

speaker: Jacob
en: Evie, now!

speaker: Evie
en: Shall we?

speaker: Jacob
en: Let's.

speaker: Evie
en: Together!

speaker: Starrick
en: London will perish without me!

speaker: Jacob
en: You flatter yourself.

speaker: Starrick
en: I would have created a paradise.

speaker: Evie
en: The city belongs to the people. You are but one man.

speaker: Starrick
en: I am at the very top of the Order.

speaker: Jacob
en: You were, Mr. Starrick. You were.

speaker: Jacob
en: Shame we won't be partners anymore.

speaker: Evie
en: It's for the best, isn't it?

speaker: Jacob
en: Are you gonna wear the shroud and run London?

speaker: Evie
en: Whatever it gives, it takes from someone else. You'd continue to age without me. You'd become like Father.

speaker: Jacob
en: A fate worse than death!

speaker: Evie
en: Will you wear it?

speaker: Jacob
en: After you sorted out the boroughs? The chaos I caused? I couldn't compete.

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob Frye stepping back? Who's blackmailing you? Is it George?!

speaker: Jacob
en: He wouldn't dare. I've missed you.

speaker: Evie
en: Me too. Would it be possible to continue where we left off?

speaker: Jacob
en: I'd love nothing more.

speaker: Evie
en: I'm starting to think Father didn't know everything about everything.

speaker: Evie
en: Henry!

speaker: Jacob
en: It's a big world out there. With London in the center.

speaker: Evie
en: Perhaps not the very center.

speaker: Henry
en: I came as soon as I could. Do not worry. I'll—I'll head back to the train. Did I—did I jeopardize the mission?

speaker: Evie
en: Henry, you saved it.

speaker: Evie
en: I think you belong in the field. With me.

speaker: Jacob
en: A carriage! Nicely done, Freddy.

speaker: Victoria
en: Mr. Abberline, please.

speaker: Evie
en: Your Majesty.

speaker: Victoria
en: Miss Frye.

speaker: Jacob
en: You've met before?

speaker: Evie
en: Didn't I mention?

speaker: Victoria
en: Mr. Abberline informs me that you three are responsible for saving my life. Is this true?

speaker: Henry
en: It is, your Majesty.

speaker: Victoria
en: Evie Frye, step forward. And you...

speaker: Evie
en: My brother, ma'am. Jacob Frye. And this is Mr. Henry Green.

speaker: Victoria
en: Mr. Frye. Mr. Green. Kneel.

speaker: Victoria
en: Arise. I invest you all in the Order of the Sacred Garter.

speaker: Evie
en: Thank you, your Majesty.

speaker: Victoria
en: If you are as adept as Mr. Abberline implies, I may call on you.

speaker: Jacob
en: Sergeant Abberline tends to exaggerate your Majesty.

speaker: Victoria
en: We shall meet again. And Miss Frye?

speaker: Evie
en: Ma'am?

speaker: Victoria
en: Should you want it, I saved you some cake.

speaker: Evie
en: Father would be proud of you.

speaker: Jacob
en: Dame Evie Frye.

speaker: Evie
en: Sir Jacob Frye.

speaker: Jacob
en: Race you to the train.

speaker: Evie
en: You're on!

speaker: Duleep
en: Henry has an idea of what we'll tackle next. He is waiting for us at Southwark station. Go ahead, I will join you there.

speaker: Duleep
en: I'm afraid we have done too much! The British Indies Company are trying to capture your train!

speaker: Henry
en: My goodness, Agnes! I hope she's alright!

speaker: Jacob
en: Not to worry. I'll take care of these troublemakers.

speaker: Evie
en: Poor Agnes. I'll see to this immediately.

speaker: Duleep
en: I can handle the rest from here! Catch up with your train!

speaker: Henry
en: Miss MacBean should be headed for Whitechapel station!

speaker: Jacob
en: The train is too far away! I need to grab a carriage. Singh should have a carriage nearby...

speaker: Evie
en: The train is too far, I'll need to catch up by carriage. I should take the Maharaja's carriage!

speaker: Jacob
en: I knew I hadn't seen the last of you. I must board the train.

speaker: Evie
en: Here we go again. I must climb aboard that train!

speaker: Evie
en: I could jump down off this bridge and access the train.

speaker: Evie
en: If the train slows down near the station, I might be able to catch it.

speaker: Evie
en: I must take them all out.

speaker: Jacob
en: I need to get rid of them all.

speaker: Evie
en: I'll have to take them all out.

speaker: Duleep
en: What a catastrophe!

speaker: Jacob
en: The B.I.C. must not be very happy with how things are progressing.

speaker: Evie
en: The British Indies Company must not be very happy with how things are progressing.

speaker: Duleep
en: You could say that!

speaker: Jacob
en: But at least I quieted them down... For now.

speaker: Evie
en: That should keep them quiet for a while.

speaker: Duleep
en: Perhaps this is not the best time to bring up what I called you here for but... I have another plan.

speaker: Jacob
en: Go on, then.

speaker: Evie
en: I'm listening.

speaker: Duleep
en: It may sound mad but... I propose we steal the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

speaker: Jacob
en: Doesn't that belong to the Queen?250px|thumb|right|Singh explaining his new plan to Evie

speaker: Evie
en: A piece of the Royal Jewels? Whatever for?

speaker: Duleep
en: Her majesty may wear it, but it doesn't belong to her. It was a trophy, symbolizing the colonization of India and it deserves to be returned home. It would be an extremely delicate mission. But I know you'd be more than capable of such a feat. I have already procured some information pertaining to the location of the Koh-i-Noor. Come and find me when you've had a moment to think it over.

speaker: Bayley
en: I will not build a single bus for you criminals!

speaker: Blighter 1
en: Oh, you'll do as we say, Bayley, or we're gonna have to pay you and your family a visit.

speaker: Bayley
en: You leave them be!

speaker: Evie
en: Hey!

speaker: Blighter 1
en: After him!

speaker: Evie
en: Take deep breaths. They're gone.

speaker: Bayley
en: Not for long. They'll hurt my kids, they'll...

speaker: Evie
en: Tell me why you've got the Blighters after you.

speaker: Bayley
en: The city's been turned upside down since Attaway Transport and the Millner Company went belly-up. With no one to fill their shoes, the gangs made their move.

speaker: Evie
en: Well done, Jacob.

speaker: Bayley
en: As Ed Bayley, the only omnibus builder in the city, they are demanding that I work for them. I know good men who want to form a united transport company. What it is they say in America? ""? That is our intention for the . But those thugs got hold of the deed to Attaway Transport. We need it to begin our company.

speaker: Evie
en: Mr. Bayley, I am Ms. Frye. Consider me an ally to your cause.

speaker: Evie
en: I sent Roth's men a message. You and your family are safe.

speaker: Bayley
en: Ah, you are bloomin' brilliant!

speaker: Bayley
en: The founding members of the London General Omnibus Company. Good, moral men, all of them. We'll have buses rolling before you know it.

speaker: Bayley
en: Thank you, Ms. Frye.

speaker: Evie
en: My pleasure.

speaker: Queen Victoria
en: Our much lamented husband adored these gardens. He called them "his one safe port" in the midst of the mad seas of this world. We miss him dearly. But never mind all that. To business. Our mister Fleming has learned from the Templar prisoner that an attack is imminent. But before we could learn more, he escaped custody. He is believed to be hiding in Westminster. Recapture him for us, that we might learn his secrets.

speaker: Jacob
en: Slippery devil. I'll find him, ma'am.

speaker: Evie
en: He won't be free for long, ma'am, I promise.

speaker: Jacob
en: That's it, lead me to the rest of your group...

speaker: Evie
en: You will have to rendezvous with your fellow conspirators soon enough.

speaker: Leader
en: Explosives ready to go?

speaker: Templar 1
en: All in this here carriage. What took you so long?

speaker: Leader
en: Temporary setback, nothing more!

speaker: Templar 1
en: Got yourself pinched, did you?

speaker: Leader
en: Shut it, you balmy mug! I'm going on ahead to scout the location. Bring these explosives to the safe house and wait for my signal.

speaker: Templar 1
en: Yes, sir.

speaker: Jacob
en: Damn. I need to get these explosives away from the civilians... I'll deal with the Templar later.

speaker: Evie
en: Too many innocents nearby. I'll snatch away the explosives before continuing the hunt.

speaker: Templar 2
en: If we can't blow up a building, we'll just have to settle for blowing up an Assassin!

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm getting fed up with these bomb-crazed Templars.

speaker: Evie
en: Too close. I need to put an end to these upstart Templars. And quickly.

speaker: Victoria
en: Hello, my newly honored friends.

speaker: Jacob
en: Your Majesty.

speaker: Victoria
en: We understand that with Crawford Starrick gone, a certain secret society finds itself searching for leadership. An upstart faction seeks to enter London and seize power.250px|thumb|right|Evie promising the twins' aid

speaker: Evie
en: Do you feel your life is in danger, ma'am?

speaker: Victoria
en: No. Rather, I fear that the people of this grand city may suffer. I call upon you to foil this traitorous plot.

speaker: Evie
en: You can depend on us.

speaker: Victoria
en: You will meet my loyal aide at the docks for instructions. Your work begins immediately.

speaker: Fleming
en: I am Alfred Fleming. I run her Majesty's secret service. First things first, we need to clear the area of anything that might alarm the enemy. Like that police carriage. Would you kindly dispose of it?

speaker: Fleming
en: Good work. Now. My agents are here, disguised as civilians. Get them into position for our ambush. A ship will soon arrive from Boston. Its cargo, dynamite. Its crew, Templar. What say you to greeting it with an ambush?

speaker: Jacob
en: I'd say we're going to be very good friends.

speaker: Evie
en: If we must, we must.

speaker: Jacob
en: Now!

speaker: Evie
en: Come on! Let's have them!

speaker: Fleming
en: That's their leader! I want him brought to me at the station. Alive!

speaker: Jacob
en: I don't suppose you'd care to confess?

speaker: Evie
en: Would you care to tell me your plans?

speaker: Templar
en: Go to hell.

speaker: Jacob
en: Fair enough.

speaker: Evie
en: Now, now.

speaker: Templar
en: Starrick may be dead and gone, but the Templar Order will never die! We will rise again, like a phoenix from the ashes, and bring the world to its knees!

speaker: Jacob
en: Not exactly Grand Master material, are you?

speaker: Evie
en: Yes, well. Best of luck with that.

speaker: Fleming
en: Thank you. I'll carry on from here. My people are recovering their explosive cargo. You did fine work today. I will have a chat with our distinguished guest here to see what schemes he and his friends are brewing.

speaker: Jacob
en: Do get in touch when he spills his guts.

speaker: Evie
en: Do let me know if he says anything interesting.

speaker: Fleming
en: Of course.

speaker: Victoria
en: Mr. Fleming has attempted to force a confession from your prisoner. The miscreant refuses to talk. Will you speak to the villain and learn his secrets?

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, I'd be delighted, ma'am.

speaker: Evie
en: Leave it to me, your majesty.

speaker: Jacob
en: I don't suppose you'd like to spare yourself a tremendous beating and make a clean breast of it?

speaker: Evie
en: Must I pummel you severely about the head and shoulders? Or can we simply talk?

speaker: Templar
en: Might as well. The order was to load a train with explosives at Westminster. It'll detonate before reaching Southwark station and kill everyone aboard!

speaker: Jacob
en: I did not expect you to confess! Which train?

speaker: Evie
en: You people and your damned dynamite. When does it happen?

speaker: Templar
en: It's the next train! It should leave at any moment! You'll never make it in time!

speaker: Jacob
en: Damn! I can't reach the bomb. I'll detach the locomotive.

speaker: Evie
en: Locked! I'll separate the bomb from the other cars!

speaker: Victoria
en: The final group of upstarts are making their last, desperate stand. They have penetrated the House of Parliament and plan to detonate whatever explosives they have left. Please find Mr. Fleming so we might put an end to this once and for all.

speaker: Fleming
en: Multiple targets inside the palace. All armed and dangerous. Making matters worse—the Prime Minister has gone missing. I need you to deal with the Templars. Target one is in a nearby corridor, surrounded by civilians. He has explosives on his person. You need to take him by surprise. If he sees you, he'll detonate his bomb. In the meantime, I'll search for the Prime Minister.

speaker: Fleming
en: Well done. But there are still more bombers about. They must be removed--quickly and quietly.

speaker: Fleming
en: Catch the devil! He mustn't escape!

speaker: Templar
en: Don't come any closer!

speaker: Jacob
en: Mr. Fleming, I've located the Prime Minister!

speaker: Evie
en: Steady, Prime Minister, I'll have you free in a moment.

speaker: Templar
en: Not another step, Assassin! You've lost, don't you see? The Houses of Parliament are rigged to explode at the last stroke of twelve! There's nothing you or anyone else can do to stop it now. The Houses of Parliament will be leveled! Centuries of history are going to be blown away in a second!

speaker: Disraeli
en: I demand you kill this lunatic!

speaker: Disraeli
en: Find those bombs before they go off!

speaker: Disraeli
en: Thank you, my young friend. Now, please come with me. You and your sibling have been summoned.

speaker: Victoria
en: Approach. You have honored us with your loyalty and courage. Long may we strengthen the Empire together!

speaker: Jacob
en: Your Majesty. We will always work to ensure the safety of the people.

speaker: Evie
en: But with the greatest respect, our philosophy forbids us from assisting with the expansion of the Empire. Perhaps, ma'am, you could consider putting an end to your imperialist desires?

speaker: Victoria
en: I understand and respect your position, bound as you are by your Creed. You will indulge me one final time and receive these gifts. Goodbye and may God bless the noble Fryes!

speaker: Jacob
en: I don't suppose you'll be offered any more cake.

speaker: Opium Cargo
en: was a virtual representation of one of Evie Frye's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Dickens
en: Ah, my dear Darwin, do you think our young friend here, equipped with a multiplicity of talents, might be enough to ensure Mister Hammon safe passage?

speaker: Jacob
en: Who's Hammon when he's at home, then?

speaker: Evie
en: I do not believe I've had the pleasure of meeting a Mister Hammon.

speaker: Dickens
en: A mutual friend of ours. He arrives in London today.

speaker: Darwin
en: From South Africa no less!

speaker: Dickens
en: Mister Hammon is possessed of both tremendous wealth and charming innocence.

speaker: Darwin
en: Which makes him rather attractive prey for some of our great city's less savoury inhabitants. We fear he'll need a more robust escort than two old men might provide.

speaker: Jacob
en: I'm not a coachman, you know.

speaker: Evie
en: I'm actually rather busy.

speaker: Darwin
en: We have already told him to expect you!

speaker: Dickens
en: His train should have arrived ten minutes ago.

speaker: Jacob
en: Well then, I suppose a friend of yours, is a friend of mine.

speaker: Evie
en: Then I shan't keep him waiting.

speaker: Darwin
en: Splendid!

speaker: Dickens
en: Off you go.

speaker: Jacob
en: Mister John Hammon?

speaker: Evie
en: Mister Hammon, I believe?

speaker: Hammon
en: That is correct.

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: Jacob/Evie Frye. Mister Dickens sent me to meet you.

speaker: Hammon
en: Ah, good old Dickens. How very kind of him. Lead on, then.

speaker: Hammon
en: London... Can't say I've missed the weather. My father passed away recently and I have come home to settle his affairs. Also, I am to be married.

speaker: Jacob
en: You don't sound too keen on the idea.

speaker: Evie
en: You don't sound too eager for the happy event.

speaker: Hammon
en: I have never even met my future bride, Bella Wilton. It was all arranged for me. She may be a good woman. Or she may not. I stand to inherit a vast sum. Can I be certain that the lady is not simply in it for the money?

speaker: Blighter 1
en: Hand over your money, quick as quick.

speaker: Blighter 2
en: I like your togs. Care to trade 'em for mine?

speaker: Hammon
en: By Jove! You're handy to have around. I fear my wealth attracts too much attention.

speaker: Hammon
en: That did give me an idea. Perhaps I can test my bride's sincerity. I am now officially dead and have thus shed my fortune. I shall meet Bella Wilton as a nobody. We shall see if she'll have me now. Come, we must dispose of my body. Find us a carriage to take us to the river.

speaker: Hammon
en: Good work. How exciting! This is like something out of a novel!

speaker: Hammon
en: Excellent! Now let us go and meet my fiancee. I can't wait to see her response.

speaker: Hammon
en: I feel quite liberated. As if a great weight has been lifted from my shoulders. After this, just to be sure, would you take me to my fiancee's house? I shall deliver the sad news myself.

speaker: Jacob
en: Seems a bit risky to me.

speaker: Evie
en: Don't you think that's a little risky?

speaker: Hammon
en: She has never set eyes on me! Besides I need to ascertain whether I like her as well! And I want to see how she reacts to the news of my death... Come on, hurry up. This is taking far too long. You're going the wrong way. I'm sure of it. Please hurry. I'm very anxious to meet Miss Wilton.

speaker: Hammon
en: Miss Wilton?

speaker: Bella
en: Yes?

speaker: Hammon
en: My name is John Rokesmith. I am afraid I have some terrible news for you.

speaker: Bella
en: Oh?

speaker: Hammon
en: Your fiancé, John Hammon was found dead in the River Thames this morning.

speaker: Bella
en: Oh, how awful! Poor Mister Hammon. I am at a loss at what to say to you, sir, you must forgive me.

speaker: Hammon
en: She is delightful! Why I do believe I love her!

speaker: Jacob
en: Certainly an unu csual first meeting to talk about in your wedding speech!

speaker: Evie
en: I hope she's more intrigued than she is appalled!

speaker: Needham
en: I will be as Achilles was. I will be great and powerful. And I will live on in the minds of the weak.

speaker: Needham
en: This is it, this is my moment!

speaker: Needham
en: From now on, everyone will remember Peter Needham. Peter the Strong, Peter the Conqueror, Peter the Great!

speaker: Needham
en: The ancient ruins below will rise and the old will be new again.

speaker: Beckinridge
en: Keep the wheels turning at all costs. Stop for nothing!

speaker: Beckinridge
en: Back to work! We can't fall behind schedule now!

speaker: Beckinridge
en: If we don't meet our quota, I'll dock all your pay!

speaker: Henry
en: You may have not found a Piece of Eden—but this material is invaluable. Look! It says the London Assassins had found a Shroud...

speaker: Evie
en: "The Shroud of Eden is supposed to heal even the greatest even the gravest injury". If the Assassins had found something like this, surely Father would have known.

speaker: Henry
en: There must be something we're missing.

speaker: Evie
en: Something only we can see...

speaker: Evie
en: These look like directions! Are you coming?

speaker: Henry
en: Fieldwork is not really my specialty.

speaker: Evie
en: We've found a clue to a Precursor object—don't you want to follow it?

speaker: Henry
en: Put that way, one can hardly refuse.

speaker: Henry
en: Do you know, I think this map may be taking us to the Kenway Mansion!

speaker: Evie
en: Kenway? The pirate?

speaker: Henry
en: Master Assassin and pirate, yes.

speaker: Evie
en: How much do you know about the Shroud of Eden?

speaker: Henry
en: It's said to heal the sick—popular myth is that it brings people back from the dead, but the Assassin records say that's not true. I've never heard of one being in London, though. Do you really think Edward Kenway could have found one?

speaker: Evie
en: He traveled extensively, so it's possible. But if he did, he kept it a closely guarded secret.

speaker: Henry
en: But if it's true—what a find it would be.

speaker: Evie
en: Indeed. I'm eager to find out, myself. It's surprising that you haven't already searched the Kenway house.

speaker: Henry
en: Edward's son, Haytham, joined the Templars. When he died, the house passed on to Haytham's sister.

speaker: Evie
en: And in all your time in London, you didn't go and have a look around? Weren't even a little curious?

speaker: Henry
en: Truly, I didn't expect to find anything there. We've no way of knowing how many times the building's changed hands. I presumed Haytham would have had it stripped bare before he left.

speaker: Evie
en: But if Miss Thorne thinks the Shroud could still be there...

speaker: Henry
en: If there's a vault, the Templars haven't found it yet.

speaker: Evie
en: So, the Templars owned a house with Assassin treasures stored in it—and never located them.

speaker: Henry
en: We must be better at hiding things than they are.

speaker: Evie
en: I think this is it.

speaker: Henry
en: I think you're right. Look.

speaker: Thorne
en: I'll be in the study. I don't want to be interrupted, unless you have news of the lost notebook.

speaker: Evie
en: That makes getting in a challenge.

speaker: Henry
en: You still intend to enter?

speaker: Evie
en: If this is a Templar stronghold, it won't get any easier. But don't worry, we'll stay well away from Miss Lucy. Shall we?

speaker: Evie
en: Can you check over there?

speaker: Henry
en: Of course.

speaker: Templar 1
en: I'm telling you, the Assassins don't even know we're here.

speaker: Templar 2
en: But she says high alert, so we have to hop to.

speaker: Templar 1
en: I haven't seen Miss Thorne so angry since Charlie dropped that blood vial.

speaker: Templar 2
en: Who's Charlie?

speaker: Templar 1
en: Exactly.

speaker: Templar 3
en: I suppose patrolling is better than standing still. I wonder if this high alert is some kind of training.

speaker: Evie
en: That looks interesting.

speaker: Evie
en: Miss Thorne is quite the collector.

speaker: Evie
en: I can't believe they've kept all of this.

speaker: Evie
en: Something from Edward Kenway's time.

speaker: Evie
en: Another Assassin artifact.

speaker: Evie
en: I wish father could have seen this.

speaker: Evie
en: This should belong to the Assassins.

speaker: Templar 4
en: Still nothing here, same as last time.

speaker: Templar 5
en: This is a waste of my time. I feel like I'm being watched.

speaker: Templar 6
en: I don't even know what I'm looking for. If this keeps up, I'm gonna tell her I'm not patrolling anymore.

speaker: Templar 7
en: Heh, be my guest, but that won't end well for you.

speaker: Templar 8
en: What's Miss Thorne looking for, anyway?

speaker: Templar 9
en: No idea.

speaker: Templar 8
en: Miss Thorne's been jumping at shadows since the Assassins got that notebook, if you ask me.

speaker: Templar 9
en: Don't let her hear you say that.

speaker: Henry
en: What are we looking for?

speaker: Evie
en: I'm not quite sure...

speaker: Henry
en: What are the Templars not seeing?

speaker: Evie
en: Something only we can.

speaker: Henry
en: This piano is beautiful.

speaker: Evie
en: Do you play?

speaker: Henry
en: No. I wish I could. I love the sound. You?

speaker: Evie
en: A little. Enough to pass as a genteel young lady if I need to.

speaker: Henry
en: I would love to hear you play if the opportunity presents itself. Edward Kenway was a pirate. Where would a pirate hide his treasure?

speaker: Evie
en: I'd hide mine in a library.

speaker: Henry
en: Mine would be the library.

speaker: Henry
en: What are you doing

speaker: Evie
en: Did you hear that?

speaker: Henry
en: Not enormously subtle, is it?

speaker: Evie
en: Clearly, Kenway had a strong sense of spectacle.

speaker: Henry
en: This is incredible.

speaker: Henry
en: I think this is from the Jackdaw... To think, this has been hidden for a century... I wish we could take these with us.

speaker: Evie
en: A history of the London Assassins... bolt holes... vaults... a hidden key. This is it.

speaker: Thorne
en: You say you heard music?

speaker: Thorne
en: There was no opening there before.

speaker: Blighter
en: It's closing!

speaker: Thorne
en: Yes, I can see that! Help me block it!

speaker: Evie
en: We need to find another way out.

speaker: Thorne
en: You two! Get Henrietta! Try to find if there's another exit. There must be a switch somewhere! Check the walls! You said you heard the piano?

speaker: Blighter
en: Yes, Miss Thorne.

speaker: Thorne
en: That could be the trigger. Examine it closely. John! Get a crowbar! We'll force the hatch open! Those books! Check them! When this is all over, I will want to know how they got in here! Keep searching!

speaker: Evie
en: An entire vault filled with Assassin history, left behind once again.

speaker: Henry
en: We'll just have to reclaim this one later or find a better cache.

speaker: Evie
en: "We"? I thought you preferred to stay out of of fieldwork.

speaker: Henry
en: I... I was thinking more of you and your brother. I shall provide planning assistance. From the train.

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob's off marauding. There is a vacancy, should you desire to broaden your horizons.

speaker: Henry
en: Oh... Well, Evie, I-- Oh, well, Evie... I will think on it.

speaker: Evie
en: You do that. Come, let's get above ground.

speaker: Henry
en: Miss Frye! I brought some books. I hope I'm not intruding, by being here.

speaker: Evie
en: Quite the contrary. It's nice to have company.

speaker: Evie
en: A herbarium? Are you collecting flowers for someone?

speaker: Henry
en: Only myself. I'm told it's something of a British passtime. Did you know they all have symbolic meanings?

speaker: Evie
en: I had heard, something of the sort.250px|thumb|right|Henry accepting Evie's offer

speaker: Henry
en: Of course you have. Unfortunately, I have no time to fill the book.

speaker: Evie
en: I could collect some samples, if you would accept my help.

speaker: Henry
en: I would appreciate that. Thank you, Miss Frye.

speaker: Henry
en: Mignonette. Your qualities surpass your charms.

speaker: Evie
en: I'm not entirely sure if that's meant as a compliment. "Love in a mist", that's a pretty name.

speaker: Henry
en: ... alternately called "Devil in a bush".

speaker: Evie
en: Narcissus: self-love. I should buy a bouquet for Jacob.

speaker: Henry
en: Most unkind, Miss Frye.250px|thumb|right|Henry and Evie joking about message bouqets

speaker: Evie
en: As amusing as all this is, I really should be getting back to work. If you need me...

speaker: Henry
en: I'll send a bouquet.

speaker: Evie
en: ... of Irises.

speaker: Henry
en: "A message." Indeed.

speaker: Evie
en: A message... of hope. Perfection? A red tulip...

speaker: Henry
en: ... a declaration of love. I- Miss Evie Frye, you know that I hold you in the highest esteem... and regard. And I was wondering if you would do me the honor of- If you would, give me your hand... in matrimony.

speaker: Evie
en: Yes.

speaker: Evie
en: These old Navy ships were hulked out to hold prisoners until they were assigned a convict ship leaving for the colonies. So, this is where Jack keeps his quarry. Let's see if Jack is paying a visit to his captives...

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob? Is that you?

speaker: Prisoner 1
en: Help me... Miss... Please, why am I here? No one will tell me!

speaker: Prisoner 2
en: It's Jack! Jack the Ripper, I say! He's the one who abducted us.

speaker: Prisoner 3
en: He starves and tortures us until we write to our families begging them to do as he dictates or we'll be slaughtered!

speaker: Evie
en: Is he here? Have you seen the Ripper recently?

speaker: Prisoner 4
en: Not for weeks, but he'll come back...and bring more poor sods to dance on the Warder's cord for him!

speaker: Evie
en: Jack has locked them up like animals...they'll all die of cholera...if the Chief Warder doesn't hang them first.

speaker: Prisoner 5
en: I beg you, don't leave us to perish... The Chief Warder is a vile, sadistic man... No one spoke to me for weeks, then the Warder's assistant came to ask me how much I weigh...

speaker: Evie
en: I need to get into the main prison and find the Chief Warder before he hangs another man for Jack's entertainment...

speaker: Guard
en: Go and dredge the Thames, you lazy bastards! ...The Chief Warder wants privacy.

speaker: Prisoner 6
en: Don't lose heart, gentlemen, we can break out of here if we work together.

speaker: Prisoner 7
en: It's no use, we'd need explosives to blast through those doors.

speaker: Billingsworth
en: You gotta get the weight just right, drop 'em gentle, let them do the work. That way you can stretch their gullets a good four or five inches before they croak.

speaker: Prisoner 8
en: If you would, milady, free us. Blast open this cell door and we'll keep a few of those thugs occupied for as long as we can.

speaker: Billingsworth
en: Yeah, the stretch is good but it doesn't count, does it? He's dead. So where's the skill in that? Have him hanging for twenty minutes like that, stretching his gullet all the while. Mr. Jack likes when it lasts... Nah, you gotta get the weight just right, drop 'em gentle and let them do the work. This work makes me proud, see? It's important work. Mr. Jack understands that. And I'm very good at it. The trick is in the drop. You let 'em go too fast the neck breaks, they're dead, you take 'em down. I could stretch you out ten, twelve inches but if you're dead there's nowt in it for me, is there? That last one - right mardy, fat bastard he was - he took some faffin' but I managed to pull a good half a foot from 'im. Piss all down his kegs, reeked like a lass' churner on the rag, ha, ha... Ah, perks of the job, eh?

speaker: Billingsworth
en: Go see what is wrong up there, you simperin' ass!

speaker: Assistant
en: Yes, sir.

speaker: Billingsworth
en: Well?

speaker: Assistant
en: A problem with the new pulley, sir.

speaker: Billingsworth
en: Fix it, you jolterhead!

speaker: Billingsworth
en: Look at you! Goody two-shoes, is it? You think offing some 'ol hangman is going to change what we do here?

speaker: Evie
en: We?

speaker: Billingsworth
en: What do you think? This was your brother's vision...his inspiration!

speaker: Evie
en: I don't believe you.

speaker: Billingsworth
en: He taught Mr. Jack how to rip the filth from this rotten city, but you don't have the balls to see what's right and necessary.

speaker: Evie
en: Where is Jack? Where is the Ripper?

speaker: Billingsworth
en: Ah Ah Ah...!

speaker: Evie
en: To hell with your right and necessary. That vile sadist was working for the Ripper, but there is no sign of Jack here... Oh, Jacob, you did not intend to breed this monster--but he is ours to destroy. The legacy of our Brotherhood depends on it. I must inform Abberline about what I have discovered here...

speaker: Evie
en: I need to speak to Frederick Abberline. This is an emergency. Well, where is he? The Ripper has struck again? Where? All right, thank you, officer. WAIT! You need to alert the local constable. Send as many men as you can to the old Hulk prisons.

speaker: Dickens
en: Have you truly no recollection of the events that landed you in a cell?

speaker: Jacob
en: I remember what the other victims remember. A silver watch, the sound of a bell and a sort of shadow.

speaker: Evie
en: My mind is blank, save for the glint of a silver object, the toll of a bell, and a presence of some sort.

speaker: Dickens
en: A glint of silver and a tolling bell, eh? I must say, you look very tired.

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: Yes. I am so very, very tired.

speaker: Enzio
en: Now you're going to do a little job of work for me, aren't you?

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: Now I'm going to do a little job of work for you.

speaker: Enzio
en: You cost me a bit of money, mate, so I think it's only fair that you replenish my coffers with donations from the good people of London. You will steal money for me, won't you?

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: Yes. I will steal money for you.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: How dare you! Leave me alone!

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Help! Thief!

speaker: Civilian 3
en: Oi, get away from me, you dodger!

speaker: Enzio
en: Good, very good. Now, we can't have criminals like you roaming the streets. You will surrender to the police, won't you?

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: Yes, I will surrender to the police.

speaker: Enzio
en: Oh, and when you do, you're going to do a silly little dance for them.

speaker: Dickens
en: I say, you gave me a terrible fright. Muttering about a man named "Ezio".

speaker: Jacob
en: Enzio Capelli. Not a demon, but a hypnotist. And he's not even Italian!

speaker: Evie
en: I was hypnotized by Enzio Capelli. Not a demon after all. Nor Italian, for that matter!

speaker: Dickens
en: I suspected hypnotism from the very start! You must find the villain.

speaker: Enzio
en: You're going to stand watch while I ransack this house, aren't you?

speaker: Enzio
en: You're going to obey the bell, aren't you?

speaker: Blighters 1
en: Yes. I'm going to obey the bell.

speaker: Blighters 2
en: Keep an eye out for valuables.

speaker: Enzio
en: What was that noise? Go take a look!

speaker: Enzio
en: Release me at once! I admit it! I'm not Italian! It was just for my act! Nobody wanted to see a British hypnotist!

speaker: Jacob
en: Oh, shut up!

speaker: Evie
en: I don't care.

speaker: Enzio
en: I'll give you anything you want!

speaker: Jacob
en: I want you to shut your mouth. Do you know a Doctor John Elliotson?

speaker: Evie
en: I would like you to be quiet. Are you a contemporary of Dr. Elliotson?

speaker: Enzio
en: Never heard of the man.

speaker: Jacob
en: Do you really think mesmerism would work?

speaker: Evie
en: Mesmerism as a criminal enterprise was not a bright idea.

speaker: Enzio
en: How dare you! I'm a hypnotist!

speaker: Enzio
en: My body does not bend that way! This is really quite painful. Can we not work out an arrangement?

speaker: Jacob
en: Time to confess and free the people under your silly spell.

speaker: Evie
en: You will make reparation for your crimes and liberate the innocents you've used.

speaker: Robert Donston Stephenson
en: Please, my neighbors will lynch me! I swear I'm not the Ripper! Bring me to Scotland Yard and I'll prove it! Thank goodness the inspector got my message. I think I may've identified that madman, Jack the Ripper, but someone wants to see to it that I never reach the station alive. Take me to Inspector Abberline. I've information on the ripper murders, but my neighbors think I'm a suspect. Get me there alive and I'll prove I'm innocent. Don't let them hurt me, I'm innocent. Don't let them hang me! God! Please hurry, please please please... Don't let them kill me, please! Please, please, just get me to the Yard alive! I'm innocent! I swear! They want to kill me! Oh please don't let them...please, please! It's not what you think! I am not Jack the Ripper! What was that? Oh, please, please, please don't let—don't let them, please, please, please, please.

speaker: Frederick Abberline
en: My constables and I are grateful for your assistance. Thank you, Miss Frye. You've saved the suspect's life, and no doubt the lives of many of my constables.

speaker: Robert Donston Stephenson
en: I'd be dead and no way to prove my innocence if it weren't for you, Miss. I'm innocent. It's not me, I swear. Thank you, Miss.

speaker: Henry
en: Owning the railway wasn't enough. Now Starrick has bought an omnibus company as well. I suppose he wants to control the neighborhood's workers and keep them under his thumb.

speaker: Jacob
en: Pearl Attaway is Starrick's competitor, is she? Perhaps it's time I went into business.

speaker: Henry
en: And Miss Frye? What are your plans?

speaker: Evie
en: I studied the history we recovered from the Kenway Mansion's hidden room. I'm off to a certain monument.

speaker: Jacob
en: So the "hints" you found in the Kenway house lead... to the Monument?

speaker: Evie
en: What a wonderful use of your time, following me around asking obvious questions.

speaker: Jacob
en: Well, since Henry isn't here, I thought you might enjoy the company.

speaker: Evie
en: I don't require any company. And Mr. Green is following up on some leads of his own.

speaker: Jacob
en: "Oh, yes, Mr. Green. That's a fascinating idea". "Oh, please, Mr. Green, come and take a look at this book and stand oh-so-close to me, Mr. Green.

speaker: Evie
en: I do not- Well, perhaps you have nothing better to do, but I am busy protecting the Assassins.

speaker: Jacob
en: Are you, really? What was it Father used to say...

speaker: Evie
en: "Don't allow personal feelings to compromise the mission".

speaker: Jacob
en: Precisely. Anyway, I'm off. If I find any more wild geese for you to chase, I'll be in touch.

speaker: Evie
en: It will be all the more pleasant for your absence.

speaker: Speaker
en: We are gathered here at the Monument to the Great Fire, in an effort to ensure so great a tragedy will never happen again. I would like to thank our esteemed guests, the right honorable Premier Disraeli, members of Parliament and others, for being here today. Our proposed legislation will ensure that housing for the impoverished need not be a fire hazard. We have heard your concerns, there is no need for shouting. Please calm down. There is no need for all this disruption. Too many today live in what are little better than hovels, in crowded conditions near open flame and with few methods of fire control. Will you please stop shouting? You are only being moved out of your homes if it is unsafe! Please, show some respect for our guests! Our new proposal will ensure that these slums will be replaced with better, safer housing, sanitation facilities, and less open flame. What a racket! You sound like a bunch of children! You are being very grateful! Do you really want to keep living in firetraps? Well, we cannot continue this until you calm yourselves!

speaker: Policeman 1
en: Stay back, if you please. Keep back, please. This area is in use. Sorry, there's an event. This way is closed.

speaker: Policeman 2
en: Quit your shouting! Quiet down there! Right! I see you there! I don't want any trouble out of you! Calm down!

speaker: Policeman 3
en: Move it! We don't need you here! Quit your gawking! Get on with you.

speaker: Policeman 4
en: Move along, please. You can't get through here, move along. Keep moving.

speaker: Evie
en: This looks familiar.

speaker: Evie
en: The key to the vault... and the Shroud.

speaker: Thorne
en: Good day, Miss Frye. I'll take that.

speaker: Evie
en: You want the Shroud to cement your own power - but what if you cannot control it?

speaker: Thorne
en: And why do you want the Shroud? Merely to keep the Templars from having it. How like an Assassin - to hold the power of eternal life, and yet be too afraid to use it.

speaker: Evie
en: Eternal life? Is that what you think the Shroud offers?

speaker: Thorne
en: What I think is no longer your concern.

speaker: Thorne
en: Coming with me?

speaker: Evie
en: I have other plans.

speaker: Evie
en: Damn it!

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Bloody Nora sends word to remain on the lookout for this rebel gang. Nora urges us to remain vigilant, but we don't need warnings. The Blighters control this borough, this city. Warnings be damned!

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: With Kaylock gone, I suppose our plans for expansion will have to wait. Pity.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: Do not speak to me about these so-called Rooks. I have no interest in them and neither should you.

speaker: Driver
en: Bob, that sparrow-brained apprentice of mine, installed a wrong part for the Iron Duke we're running. If someone could nip down to the shop and pick up a seven-inch flywheel for me, I'd be grateful.

speaker: Evie
en: I would like a seven-inch flywheel, please.

speaker: Merchant
en: Hang on a minute! Damnit. I can't get a blessed thing done 'round here.

speaker: Bob
en: Miss Evie! I done something dreadful. The train won't stop!

speaker: Evie
en: Keep your flywheel.

speaker: Driver
en: Quick! The brakes are gone! She's burstin' into flame! Climb 'round and put out the fires while I fix the brakes!

speaker: Evie
en: These fires won't put themselves out.

speaker: Driver
en: Where does this blasted thing go?

speaker: Evie
en: I need to be quick. These damn fires keep cropping up! I can't let these fires take hold! Another one! I've got to stay on top of this. Damn! Another fire! I must get them out quickly. Another one over there! Just one more minute and we should be safe. Come on! Thirty seconds and we should be stopped. Only ten seconds left!

speaker: Driver
en: Damn this thing! Hellfire and damnation!

speaker: Evie
en: What was that? I better check on the driver.

speaker: Driver
en: I'm hurt! Engage the brakes! Now!

speaker: Evie
en: I really must tell Bob not to make anymore improvements on the train.

speaker: Duleep
en: I spoke with Mister Green and we have discovered the location of the British Indies secret headquarters. You are to meet him, and he will give you the details. There is a foundry nearby where the Templars and B.I.C. members have been meeting on a regular basis. Mister Green waits for you there.

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: But we still don't understand why they tried to frame you.

speaker: Duleep
en: We don't but Mister Green seemed to think they're using the factory to develop something. It's a good place to start digging. Good luck.

speaker: Henry
en: You made it.

speaker: Jacob
en: You found the British Indies Company hideout?

speaker: Evie
en: His highness said you found the British Indies Company headquarters.

speaker: Henry
en: They've taken over an abandoned foundry. It's heavily fortified and word has it, they're shipping something precious overseas.

speaker: Jacob
en: My gut tells me that "something precious" is something bad.

speaker: Evie
en: Whatever it is, it can't be good.

speaker: Henry
en: My thoughts exactly. Go find out what they're protecting and destroy it. Maybe you'll discover why they're after Mister Singh.

speaker: Jacob
en: So this is where they've been keeping that sleeping gas... They can't leave London.

speaker: Evie
en: This is where they're hiding that elusive sleeping gas... These crates can't leave London.

speaker: Jacob
en: They're shipping this to India? No... What do they want this for? War? I must destroy them.

speaker: Evie
en: They're shipping this to India? It can't be... They're creating a biological weapon. I must destroy them.

speaker: Templar
en: Sir!... Somebody get the boss. We've got a problem.

speaker: Jacob
en: Yes, go fetch the manager.

speaker: Evie
en: This is it. We've got them now.

speaker: Templar
en: Sir! The bomb shipments! They've been destroyed!

speaker: Jacob
en: Is that Ellsworth? I better get a closer look.

speaker: Evie
en: Is that Brinley Ellsworth? It can't be. I need to get a better look.

speaker: Ellsworth
en: Destroyed? How?

speaker: Templar
en: There's someone in the vicinity! A spy! One of those Rooks, I wager.

speaker: Ellsworth
en: It must be those damned renegades Singh is friends with. Who knew one caged bird could cause so much trouble.

speaker: Jacob
en: You're caught, Ellsworth. Give up.

speaker: Ellsworth
en: I knew you had something to do with this! Seize him!

speaker: Evie
en: You have been unmasked, Ellsworth. Give up.

speaker: Ellsworth
en: I knew you were to blame! Seize her!

speaker: Jacob
en: Damn it, he got away. I must tell Singh this news immediately.

speaker: Evie
en: He's gone. I must report back to Mister Singh immediately.

speaker: Duleep
en: What did you find out? Who's behind all of this?

speaker: Jacob/Evie
en: You are not going to like what I have to tell you, your Highness. Brinley Ellsworth is behind the attacks.

speaker: Duleep
en: Ellsworth...

speaker: Jacob
en: He was gone before I had the chance to follow him... But we need to track him down and put an end to this before anything worse happens.

speaker: Evie
en: He rushed off before I could catch up to him... I'm sorry, but we need to find him before he puts your life at more risk than he already has.

speaker: Duleep
en: I need some time to think on this.

speaker: Arthur Weaversbrook
en: Miss Frye... I have helped spread the Ripper's terror through my newspapers. I want to make amends for my part in forging this monster's legend. Miss Frye. has arrived to fan the flames of hysteria which have seen this – the world's first city! – slip into primeval barbarity. You must make sure this author will not act...

speaker: Suspect
en: The Ripper has captured the world's attention, maybe some good will come out of it... the east end needs to change...

speaker: Suspect
en: I confess. I wrote that letter, but it was politically motivated. Citizens are starting to demand reforms in this city, the people of Whitechapel need help, better living conditions...

speaker: Seweryn Klosowski
en: Please, my neighbors will lynch me! I swear I'm not the Ripper! Bring me to Scotland Yard and I'll prove it! Don't let them hurt me, I'm innocent. God! Please hurry, please please please... Don't let them kill me, please! Please, please, just get me to the Yard alive! I'm innocent! I swear! They want to kill me! Oh please don't let them...please, please! It's not what you think! I am not Jack the Ripper!

speaker: Civilian
en: It's Jack the Ripper! She's got the Ripper! Don't let 'em get away!

speaker: Evie Frye
en: They really seem to think you're the 'Ripper'.

speaker: Seweryn Klosowski
en: Don't let them hang me!

speaker: Frederick Abberline
en: Many lives would have been lost -- including the suspect's -- if not for your intervention. I thank you.

speaker: Seweryn Kłosowski
en: I'm innocent! It's not me, I swear... Thank you, Miss.

speaker: Client
en: Stop struggling whore. I am not done with you. I am not done with you.

speaker: Prostitute
en: Stop it! You ain't no gent! I ain't done nothing but what you asked, sir. Don't kill me poor old dolly.

speaker: Evie
en: You! Stop it! We're going to take a walk, you and I.

speaker: Client
en: This is not what you think... Please, my reputation will be sullied.

speaker: Evie
en: Let's see how the people of London judge your acts.

speaker: Crowd
en: Shame on you! Go home sinner! Look at 'im! Red as a boiled lobster he is! Leave our women alone, you bastard!

speaker: Nellie
en: Did you think you could treat us like dogs jus' because we're 'dollies'...

speaker: Client
en: No, no...truly, I'm sorry, I won't do it again.

speaker: Nellie
en: You'd better not, if you know what's good fer you.

speaker: Chase
en: What? What do you think you're doing? Did Miss Swinebourne send you?

speaker: Jacob
en: Be quiet. I said, be quiet.

speaker: Chase
en: I'm in the middle of work!

speaker: Jacob
en: Is it your job to pollute the river?

speaker: Chase
en: It's nothing personal, but a man must also make a living.

speaker: Jacob
