speaker: Darwin
en: Thank you for everything, my friends. Ideas, like people, can only thrive when they are free.

speaker: Duke
en: What do you think you're doing?! Get away from me!

speaker: Jacob
en: Hush. Quiet, Miss Duke. There's time for talking later.

speaker: Duke
en: And what do the coppers want from me this time?

speaker: Jacob
en: How do you know I'm with the police?

speaker: Duke
en: With all the tactics they've tried, nothing surprises me anymore. They want me for the countless crimes I've committed, but they never hold me for long.

speaker: Jacob
en: We'll see this time around.

speaker: Duke
en: What do you think you're doing?! Get away from me!

speaker: Evie
en: Now, Miss Duke, no need to fuss. Some quiet would be much appreciated.

speaker: Duke
en: I know Abberline sent you. He's been on my trail for a while.

speaker: Evie
en: Half my work here is done.

speaker: Duke
en: He won't keep me long, you know? I've been in and out of prisons more times than you can count. You can't keep me fenced in!

speaker: Evie
en: We'll see about that.

speaker: Duke
en: Aye, piss off! Get this idiot off my back! Some wench is chasing me down! A bit of help would be nice!

speaker: Duke
en: Oh, for crying out loud!

speaker: Jacob
en: Come now, Miss Duke. Enough of this nonsense.

speaker: Duke
en: I said, piss off!

speaker: Evie
en: Calm down, Miss Duke. There's business I need you to attend to.

speaker: Duke
en: Let me out! Get me out of here!

speaker: Abberline
en: Feisty one, she is.

speaker: Dickens
en: Thank goodness you're here! Impossible as it may sound, Spring Heeled Jack has returned! We need to do something before the unthinkable happens!

speaker: Jacob
en: I thought we'd already dealt with this nonsense.

speaker: Evie
en: He did say that we had not seen the last of the Spring-heeled villain...

speaker: Dickens
en: There may be more to this than we originally thought.

speaker: Victim
en: Get away from me you monster!

speaker: Jacob
en: You there! Stop what you're doing.

speaker: Evie
en: Stop!

speaker: Jack
en: You'll have to do better than that! I am a ghost. A fiend! A terror in the night! I am a ghost! The falling of feet of a devil on the air. Long have I stalked the streets of London I am the terror of London! No weapon forged by man can harm me! No one is safe from my beastly claws. You can't hurt me!

speaker: Jacob
en: What? How? Where?

speaker: Evie
en: Vanished! Impossible!

speaker: Jack
en: Spring Heeled Jack will never die!

speaker: Dickens
en: Thanks to you, the Ghost Club's reputation has grown tremendously! We are a beacon of reason in a world beguiled by superstition.

speaker: Evie
en: But I believe we have encountered one genuine spirit.

speaker: Dickens
en: Can you be certain? That's the question. One might surmise that the spirits that haunt us are simply our deepest fears, manifested as apparitions.

speaker: Jacob
en: Shame. I've always wanted to see a ghost. Or a goblin!

speaker: Dickens
en: I propose a toast! To the Ghost Club, and the virtuous twins that have aided it: Miss Evie and Mr. Jacob!

speaker: All
en: Cheers!

speaker: Josephine Fletcher
en: And what do we say afterwards?

speaker: Children
en: May the Father of Understanding guide us.

speaker: Josephine Fletcher
en: And who do you serve?

speaker: Children
en: The Grand Master.

speaker: Josephine Fletcher
en: Excellent! Run along now!

speaker: Francis Fletcher
en: Our plan is coming along splendidly, darling.

speaker: Josephine Fletcher
en: Where's our next recruitment, dearest?

speaker: Francis Fletcher
en: Charing Cross. No one looks for tourists' missing children.

speaker: Josephine Fletcher
en: We'll have an army for the Grand Master in no time.

speaker: Kent
en: Where've you been? I've been minding the docks for hours without a word from you.

speaker: Raphael
en: Miss Swinebourne dropped by for a quick about.

speaker: Kent
en: And you didn't think to tell me?

speaker: Raphael
en: It wasn't urgent.

speaker: Kent
en: Like hell it wasn't! It's not every day Miss Edith drops in for a cup of tea. We are in this together! This trading business is ours, not yours.

speaker: Raphael
en: Brother, please, I understand. She merely dropped by to thanks us for our efforts.

speaker: Kent
en: What?

speaker: Raphael
en: Thanks to us the Blighters are now fully equipped. She says our loyalty will not be forgotten.

speaker: Kent
en: Is that it then?

speaker: Raphael
en: And she kissed me! Right on my forehead!

speaker: Kent
en: What? Then I deserve one too!

speaker: Hiding civilian
en: I'm in trouble now, only God knows who's on the menu tonight. Oh God! I hope they don't notice me.

speaker: Ada
en: People sneer at the street cleaners but they have no idea how better things are because of us.

speaker: Clyde
en: Those dreaded turncoats are the next to go.

speaker: Ada
en: We'll feast on those Rooks tonight.

speaker: Ada
en: Tonight is the night of the full moon.

speaker: Clyde
en: Another hunt is on the rise, who should we target this time, Ada?

speaker: Ada
en: The order from Strain is that we go after the Rooks.

speaker: Stronghold leader
en: I have spoken with Octavia. She requests that those willing to take up arms against the Rooks report to me for reassignment immediately. You Blighters make me proud. We will take those Rooks down, one by one if we have to. Those Rooks are little more than a nuisance. They are as powerful as they are pretty, which is to say not very.

speaker: Big Pete
en: Another brew, and two for Charlie

speaker: Charlie
en: You're too kind, you ugly bastard.

speaker: Big Pete
en: Your performance today was staggering, dear sister.

speaker: Charlie
en: I'm at my best when they struggle.

speaker: Big Pete
en: We need to thread lightly, for the next month maybe.

speaker: Charlie
en: We can't risk losing our supply.

speaker: Big Pete
en: If they find out I've been letting you lot in, I'll get sacked from the zoo.

speaker: Charlie
en: And that won't be the worst of it, either...

speaker: Blackroot
en: Lovely day, is it not, my beauties? Lovely, lovely day.

speaker: Blackroot
en: What a glorious shade of red.

speaker: Blackroot
en: Who knew such special ingredients could bring life so much joy?

speaker: Blackroot
en: You're hungry, aren't you? I'll make sure you're well fed tonight.

speaker: Evie
en: What good is a key if you don't know what lock it opens?

speaker: Henry
en: I dare say Miss Thorne is in the same predicament.

speaker: Evie
en: Henry! Mr. Green, here, this is it.

speaker: Henry
en: This matches a casket owned by the Queen. Kept in... the Tower of London.

speaker: Evie
en: It's a fortress. I don't suppose you have any friends there?

speaker: Henry
en: A guardsman. If you can... find him once you're inside...

speaker: Evie
en: I'll talk to you again when I have the Shroud. Thank you for your help.

speaker: Henry
en: Right, yes. Good luck. Evie.

speaker: Evie
en: Lots of guards. Predictable patrol routes. Thorne may already be inside. Better stick to the shadows.

speaker: Thorne
en: The Shroud is in a chest that matches the key. Find it and bring it to me.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Halt!

speaker: Guard 2
en: Escort to the keys. Halt!

speaker: Guard 1
en: Who goes there?

speaker: Chief Yeoman
en: The keys!

speaker: Guard 1
en: Whose keys?

speaker: Chief Yeoman
en: Queen Victoria's keys!

speaker: Guard 1
en: Pass, Queen Victoria's keys! And all's well.

speaker: Ally
en: You're not with the Royal Guard. How many of you are there? Tell me!

speaker: Miller
en: Let me go! This is treason! Just you wait until I get out! There'll be hell to pay!

speaker: Chief Yeoman
en: Chin up, soldier!

speaker: Guard 3
en: Yes, sir.

speaker: Templar 1
en: For God's sake! I wish they'd just knock the constable out.

speaker: Miller
en: Is someone out there?

speaker: Evie
en: Yes. A friend.

speaker: Miller
en: Oh, that's good. Say, friend, could you get me out? Guards ran off with the keys.

speaker: Miller
en: Thank you! It's treason, is what it is. And desecration of the chapel! Miss Thorne told me to be grateful they didn't kill me outright! The nerve!

speaker: Evie
en: She's after an object of great power. She cannot be allowed to steal it.

speaker: Miller
en: Not the ?

speaker: Evie
en: Something much more important.

speaker: Miller
en: We must stop her. I still have men loyal to me. I'll rally them.

speaker: Miller
en: All right, gentlemen, we are facing an enemy we never expected—traitors in our midst! But this young woman is our ally, and she knows their methods. Follow her directions as you would my own.

speaker: Guards
en: Yes, sir! If the constable says so, then it's our duty. For Queen Victoria!

speaker: Chief Yeoman
en: Constable Miller told me what happened. No wonder I couldn't find him! You have my thanks for your help.

speaker: Thorne
en: Report anything suspicious to me immediately. Find her! Stop her! Go after her!

speaker: Templar 2
en: That's all I know! I swear it!

speaker: Ally
en: Then you'll have to answer for your crimes.

speaker: Ally
en: You're one of Green's friends, aren't you? Thank heavens you've come. That Thorne woman has Templars everywhere, disguised as guards. I think I could pass as one of them long enough to sneak you inside. Except, the guards out here already know my face. You'd need to deal with them first. Meet me by the White Tower when you're ready.

speaker: Ally
en: That's all for the men out here. What's next?

speaker: Evie
en: Miss Thorne wants me captured. If she sees me in chains, she might let her guard down. Can you make it look convincing?

speaker: Ally
en: You mean pretend like you're my prisoner? I'll do my best, ma'am.

speaker: Ally
en: If we get too close, those Templars might realize I'm not one of theirs.

speaker: Evie
en: Then let's keep our distance.

speaker: Ally
en: I've caught the Assassin! Open the door! Inform Miss Thorne I'm bringing in the Assassin!

speaker: Templars
en: I knew we'd draw you out. Nice to see an Assassin in chains for once! Ha! You got her! Good man! Ha ha! Look who we have here, lads!

speaker: Thorne
en: There must be something here.

speaker: Ally
en: I found her wandering inside the walls, ma'am. Thought you'd want to speak with her.

speaker: Thorne
en: Welcome, Miss Frye. Do you care to tell me where the Shroud is?

speaker: Thorne
en: As you wish. I shall find it without your help. And then, I'll strangle you with it. Watch her closely.

speaker: Thorne
en: If you're here, you haven't found the Shroud either. By all means, let me know if there's more information you'd like to share. However, I suspect you don't have any. Typical of the Assassins. All you do is follow us.

speaker: Thorne
en: So, you have murdered me after all. But what good will that do you? The Shroud isn't here.

speaker: Evie
en: You sought a tool of healing in order to extend your own power!

speaker: Thorne
en: Not mine, ours. You are so short-sighted. You'd hoard power and never use it, when we would better the condition of humanity. I hope you never find the Shroud. You have no idea what it truly can do.

speaker: Evie
en: Tell me, then.

speaker: Thorne
en: No.

speaker: Ally
en: You'd better go. We can finish the rest of them.

speaker: Miller
en: I need to sound the alarm. You'd best get yourself away before I do. I'll hold off as long as I can. Hold on, lads. We can wait a bit longer. It'll be my job if I hold off much longer.

speaker: Guard
en: You'd best sound the alarm, then.

speaker: Starrick
en: Take this down. Then I want it sealed until you receive further orders. "Miss Thorne. You supplied me with the means to secure London's future. The city thanks you. The Order thanks you. I thank you. But the Shroud can only be worn by one. Therefore, I hereby dissolve this partnership. I promise to endow you with an income into your old age, but that is the most I can do. May the Father of Understanding guide you."

speaker: Starrick
en: Yes, what is it?

speaker: Servant
en: Miss Thorne, sir...

speaker: Starrick
en: What of her?

speaker: Servant
en: I'm sorry, sir. She is dead.

speaker: Starrick
en: And the key? Where is the key?!

speaker: Servant
en: There was no key found on her body, sir.

speaker: Starrick
en: ARGH! The Shroud will be mine, even if I have to raise hellfire to do it. Burn the letter.

speaker: Evie
en: What is this place?

speaker: Clara
en: It's nice to meet you both at last. This is Babylon Alley. Here, we make it our business to know the streets, and provide children with the opportunity to control their own destinies.

speaker: Evie
en: Clara. Mister Green said we might be able to help one another?

speaker: Clara
en: In exchange for our services, we ask a small favor.

speaker: Jacob
en: Well, why not? You seem to have taken most of my money. Why not take a small favor, too?

speaker: Clara
en: There are several factories about the city that are powered almost entirely by child labor. Those children work long hours, with little pay, and most are not permitted even to leave the factory grounds. They suffer terribly. I need you to save them.

speaker: Jacob
en: A small favor?

speaker: Clara
en: In return, we offer you intelligence. Something YOU clearly need.

speaker: Jacob
en: Now hold on a minute

speaker: Clara
en: I'm late for an appointment. What of these terms?

speaker: Evie
en: We accept.

speaker: Clara
en: Pleasure doing business with you.

speaker: Tom Eccleston
en: was a virtual representation of one of Jacob Frye and Evie Frye's genetic memories, relived by a Helix initiate through the Helix Navigator.

speaker: Crowd
en: Highway robbery! That's what it is! Oi, you can't keep us down no more! How much are our lives worth to you? No more exploitation! No more slashed wages!

speaker: Policemen
en: Move away, or I'll knick you for insulting an officer! Move on, or you'll get in trouble!

speaker: Evie
en: What has happened?

speaker: Abberline
en: Your brother!

speaker: Evie
en: What's he done this time?

speaker: Abberline
en: The newspapers are all over Twopenny's murder. And, if that weren't enough, someone has stolen the currency printing plates. Was that also Jacob's doing?

speaker: Evie
en: I doubt it.

speaker: Abberline
en: Now, no one trusts the bank, or England's currency. There-there will be inflation. Riots. Manufacturing will jump to America for the cheap labor. In short, Britain is done for.

speaker: Evie
en: Jacob, you've really put your foot in it now. What if... I smuggled the plates back into the bank?

speaker: Abberline
en: Well, would certainly help. Better yet, it would call into question the stories on Twopenny's murder... which would restore confidence in the economy.

speaker: Evie
en: That's settled, then. Britain lives to see another day.

speaker: Abberline
en: Oh, and if it's not too much trouble, would you mind destroying any counterfeit notes you come across so they don't circulate?

speaker: Evie
en: Of course.

speaker: Abberline
en: It really is very good of you to help. Follow me. The counterfeit money is being spent nearby. Well, if you can call it counterfeit. With those printing plates, it's nearly impossible to tell the real notes from the fake ones.

speaker: Evie
en: Mr. Abberline

speaker: Abberline
en: If this gets out - well, I've said this already. When people don't trust their currency... and we're already seeing riots

speaker: Evie
en: Mr. Abberline

speaker: Abberline
en: I have the utmost faith in you, Miss Frye.

speaker: Counterfeiter 1
en: You two. Follow me. I don't wish to be robbed on my way to the cart.

speaker: Evie
en: The counterfeiters.

speaker: Counterfeiter 2
en: Heard about the rioting at the bank?

speaker: Counterfeiter 3
en: They can riot all they like. We won't be giving back those plates.

speaker: Counterfeiter 2
en: What difference does it make? It's not like he has any real cash on him.

speaker: Counterfeiter 3
en: Since we've got the printing plates, it's all real cash.

speaker: Counterfeiter 2
en: Did you hear those crowds? Sounds like all of London is rioting.

speaker: Counterfeiter 3
en: Nothing to do with us.

speaker: Evie
en: I can't believe Jacob's managed to shatter the entire economy. Father was right. He acts in haste... and repents not at all.

speaker: Driver
en: Where to now, sir?

speaker: Counterfeiter 1
en: Back home, if you please.

speaker: Driver
en: Have you seen the papers today?

speaker: Counterfeiter 1
en: You mean about Twopenny's murder? Yes. A terrible shame, but it worked out all right for us, didn't it?

speaker: Driver
en: You're not worried that the police will be asking after you? Someone might've seen you going into the bank.

speaker: Counterfeiter 1
en: My good man, you're not worried, are you? Let your conscience be at ease. I am not responsible for Twopenny's death. I merely took advantage of a... fortuitous situation. If Scotland Yard comes nosing around, I was at that bank on business, and you know nothing else about it. I'll see you're given double your salary for your trouble.

speaker: Driver
en: Paid in your counterfeit bills, no doubt.

speaker: Counterfeiter 1
en: I didn't quite catch that.

speaker: Driver
en: Nothing at all, sir.

speaker: Counterfeiter 1
en: Keep your eyes open! Anyone could be trying to get in.

speaker: Counterfeiter 4
en: Yes, sir.

speaker: Counterfeiter 1
en: Keep this place locked down.

speaker: Counterfeiter 4
en: Yes, sir.

speaker: Counterfeiter 1
en: Guard this place as you would the Bank of England itself.

speaker: Counterfeiter 4
en: Absolutely, sir. Must have been a tough find getting those plates.

speaker: Counterfeiter 5
en: Not at all. We just walked right in on the chaos.

speaker: Counterfeiter 4
en: Nobody stopped you?

speaker: Evie
en: Now to sneak these bank into the bank.

speaker: Guard
en: Keep your distance! Nobody gets in without my saying so! You can yell all you want. You're not getting in if it's up to me. I said stay back! No one gets in!

speaker: Crowd
en: You absolute bunch of bankers are being wankered! I shall not leave without my pounds, my shillings and my pence, sir! I've read the papers. This'll be the ruin of us! You have a lot to answer for! I want you to tell me if this money's real or not, come on, then! Something must be done! You ought to be ashamed! This is an outrage!

speaker: Evie
en: This could be rather useful.

speaker: Evie
en: There. As if they were never taken.

speaker: Abberline
en: Well, the London papers are running a story about how it was all a hoax. No more riots! Faith in the bank restored! Finally, I might get a quiet night on patrol. Miss Frye, I can't thank you enough.

speaker: Evie
en: Glad we've averted catastrophe, Sergeant. Although it's Jacob who should be thanking me.

speaker: Evie
en: Inspector. The inquest mentions that Miss Nichols made quite a spectacle of her drunkenness on the night of her murder... Do you think Jacob may have put her up to it?

speaker: Abberline
en: Bait, you mean? I don't know what to think anymore, Miss Frye... Jacob kept lodgings nearby, right in the heart of this cesspool. Be careful.

speaker: Evie
en: I will not fail you.

speaker: Evie
en: More signs... What am I not seeing? There must be something more here... You knew I would come, brother. So give me a sign!

speaker: Evie
en: Weapons of intimidation, much like those we learned to use with our Indian Brothers.

speaker: Evie
en: So much blood... I hope it's not yours, brother.

speaker: Evie
en: A letter...

speaker: Evie
en: The newspapers printed this letter three days before Miss Stride and Miss Eddowes were murdered—it was signed 'Jack the Ripper'...

speaker: Evie
en: The last time Henry, my brother and I were together was in India...fifteen years ago. When the photograph was taken, we stood facing a temple of Kali... And that's one of the boys Jacob brought to train with the Brotherhood. What did we call him? ... 'Jack the lad'!—reckless and roguish, much like my brother...

speaker: Evie
en: I've got it, Jacob!

speaker: Evie
en: Kali the Destroyer. I gave this to you on your last visit to India...

speaker: Evie
en: Unfortunately? What is Jacob trying to say? We loved old Nellie. Could he be referring to an 'Unfortunate Woman'?

speaker: Evie
en: Nellie may be in the brothel nearest Jacob's lodgings...I'll start there.

speaker: Rook 1
en: She'll be here any minute!

speaker: Rook 2
en: Mr. Jack says we can have our way with her...

speaker: Rook 3
en: Right. Look sharp, lads.

speaker: Evie
en: This bomb will strike fear in their hearts.

speaker: Evie
en: Let's hope this Nellie has news of you, and can lead me to the Ripper. If Jacob's former pupil is the Ripper, then he is 'our' Ripper... I must catch him.

speaker: Evie
en: That is quite the welcoming committee.

speaker: Evie
en: One of these women must know Nellie. Pardon me, does Nellie work here?

speaker: Prostitute 1
en: Nellie? 'Fraid I can't say, Miss.

speaker: Evie
en: Where is Nellie?

speaker: Prostitute 2
en: Who's askin'? I don't know you, and I don't know Nellie.

speaker: Evie
en: Have you seen Nellie today?

speaker: Prostitute 3
en: What do you want with Nellie? Who are you? ...If you're a friend, then you may already be too late.

speaker: Evie
en: Where is she?

speaker: Prostitute 3
en: On her way to see Lady O, in the company of the brutes paid to keep us in line... Hurry if you want to catch her.

speaker: Rook 4
en: Now, come nicely, Nellie. Lady O is expecting you.

speaker: Nellie
en: I don't want to! Let me go!

speaker: Evie
en: I need to find Nellie before something bad happens to her. Where did they go? Nellie is in grave danger.

speaker: Evie
en: There's the carriage...Nellie must be inside the building. Nellie is in there somewhere, no doubt closely guarded...and in mortal danger.

speaker: Rook 4
en: Don't make me hurt you in front of all the ladies and gents.

speaker: Nellie
en: Take your hands off me.

speaker: Rook 4
en: Hush. Keep yer voice down, Lady Owers is speaking.

speaker: Owers
en: And so I am delighted to announce to you all today that we shall be taking on even more poor unfortunates in due course. These desperate young women, innocent victims of these uncertain times, shall be offered a roof over their heads, a warm fire, three meals a day and, above all, the love and support they need to regain a foothold in society. The understanding and help from those of you in our charity allows all our girls an opportunity to pick themselves up and stand tall once more, whatever their past sins or failings. As long as they repent and acknowledge the errors of their ways, they shall find a home with us. This is the work we do, it is the work of God, work of which I am extremely proud, and I shall not stop until every one of these fallen women has been saved.

speaker: Evie
en: Shh. Don't be afraid.

speaker: Nellie
en: Jacob's sister! We can't talk here, please, he'll kill me, she'll see to it...

speaker: Evie
en: Who?

speaker: Nellie
en: Lady Owers. Jacob said you must kill her to find him...

speaker: Owers
en: Smile and be polite, or I'll tell the Ripper where you sleep, my beauties.

speaker: Owers
en: Dame Frye.

speaker: Owers
en: Take Nellie and see to it that woman does not follow us.

speaker: Evie
en: Where did she go?

speaker: Evie
en: That must be the carriage I'm after!

speaker: Evie
en: Damn! I mustn't lose her! Lady O is escaping! She's getting away! Where did she go, damn it!

speaker: Evie
en: Lady Owers—Nellie! I am so sorry...

speaker: Nellie
en: She used me as a decoy and fled to Owers Manor.

speaker: Evie
en: Hoping I'd cause your death, no doubt...

speaker: Nellie
en: She knew you'd come, Miss Frye. Lady O is the Ripper's eyes and ears in London...

speaker: Evie
en: Kill her, and Jack will be forced to show himself.

speaker: Evie
en: I'll look in on you soon, Nellie, I promise.

speaker: Evie
en: Lady Owers will be expecting me, and I would not want to disappoint her.

speaker: Marx
en: I'm so relieved to have found you! I fear my upcoming meeting is going to be disrupted. Strike-breakers, maybe, or police spies. Ruffians, who fear the march of progress.

speaker: Jacob
en: Ah. So I'm bodyguarding, then. Marvelous!

speaker: Marx
en: I worry that any agitation will incite terrible violence, so please remove any trouble makers without attracting any attention. Wunderbar! (Wonderful!) Thank you! I must prepare, but I will see you inside shortly!

speaker: Marx
en: I'm so relieved to have found you! I fear my upcoming meeting is going to be disrupted. Strike-breakers, maybe, or police spies. Ruffians, who fear the march of progress.

speaker: Evie
en: Fear not, Mr. Marx. I'll look after you.

speaker: Marx
en: I worry that any agitation will incite terrible violence, so please remove any trouble makers without attracting any attention. Wunderbar! (Wonderful!) Thank you! I must prepare, but I will see you inside shortly!

speaker: Announcer
en: Ladies and gentlemen, united workers, the man we're here to see needs no introduction, but I shall give him one anyway. He has sacrificed so much in the hope that we may all benefit. Please give a warm reception to Mr. Karl Marx.

speaker: Marx
en: Workers, Comrades. Thank you for your most generous welcome. I come before you today with a heavy heart. England stands at the head of commercial and industrial Europe. In the last two decades there has been an unheard of development of industry and unprecedented increase in exports and imports. While these are facts to be celebrated by the provident classes, for the workers very little has changed. You well know under what conditions of shattered health, damaged morals and spiritual ruin this increase of wealth and power was produced for the upper classes, by the working class. It has become a truce that no perfecting of machinery, no application of science to industry, no improvement on the means of communication, no new colonies, no immigration, no opening out of new markets, no free trade and not all these things put together can do away with the misery of the toiling masses. But rather, on the contrary, that upon the present false basis, every new development of the productive power of labour must lead to the widening of the gap between the classes and to the heightening of social antagonisms. During this epoch of economic progress, death from starvation has raised itself almost to the rank of a social institution, here in London, the capital of the British Empire. In the annals of world history, this age will be characterized by the more impetuous force, the more expanded range and the deadlier effects of the social plague known as the commercial and industrial crisis. I believe that it is not necessary that the means of labour should be monopolized as a means of dominating the workers and exploiting them. That just like slavery and serfdom, so also wage labour is only a transitory subordinate social form, which is destined to vanish before associated labour, which will accomplish its work with willing hands, vigorous mind and cheerful heart. It has been said that the is a House of Landlords. I put it to you today, that to capture political power is now the great duty of the working class! We must attempt the political reorganization of the workers if we are to improve their lot. The workers must go forward in a united fashion, with the simultaneous demand that the simple laws of morality and justice, which are considered right in the relations of private persons, shall be recognized as the supreme law governing labour in this country! The struggle for such a policy is embraced in the universal struggle for the emancipation of the working class. And so I say to you, proletarians of all lands, unite! In order to free the workers, the cooperative system of labour requires to develop on a national scale. And following from that, must be furthered by national means. For their part, the lords of the land and the lords of capital will continue steadily to use their political privileges for the defense and perpetuation of their monopoly. Instead of furthering the emancipation of the workers, they will act so as to bring every possible obstacle in the way.
